News.title: Andy Burnham lashes out at Boris Johnson over Brexit as he denies reigniting 'toxic' debate
News.content:
Andy Burnham lashes out at Boris Johnson over Brexit as he denies reigniting 'toxic' debate

The Prime Minister said he would not be taking advice from Boris Johnson, saying he lumbered Britain with a bad Brexit deal and 'burned bridges' with allies in Europe

View 2 Images Andy Burnham said Boris Johnson left Britain with a 'bad Brexit deal' (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/Press Association)

Andy Burnham has insisted he is not reigniting a "toxic" Brexit debate - as he lashed out at Boris Johnson for wading into the growing row.

‌



‌



The Prime Minister said he would not be taking advice from Mr Johnson, saying he lumbered Britain with a bad Brexit deal and "burned bridges" with allies in Europe. It comes after the ex-PM warned him against reigniting the debate on Europe and claimed the UK would vote to leave again in another referendum.

‌



Mr Burnham revived the fraught Brexit debate in a speech to Labour conference in September, where he said he would lay out options for closer ties with the bloc around a key EU-UK summit on Friday.

‌



But today he appeared to shift the timeframe, saying that the highly-anticipated next steps would come alongside his 10-year plan for Britain, which is expected before Christmas.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 2 Images Boris Johnson claimed Britain would vote to leave the EU again in another referendum (Image: CARLOS ORTEGA/EPA/Shutterstock)

‌



UK on brink of EU deal to bring down price of weekly shop after Brexit disaster, says Andy Burnham READ MORE :

Pressed on whether reopening the Brexit topic had become toxic, Mr Burnham told Sky News: “I’m in a negotiation about improving the Brexit deal. That’s what I’m doing this week. We’ll see how it goes.

‌



“And then we will consider whether there are options to further the relationship with the EU. And I’ll set that out later this year alongside the ten-year plan. But I don’t agree with you at all, actually, that it’s a toxic debate.”

He denied changing the timeframe, saying: “I will set out next month what the next phase looks like. And that is exactly what I said at my conference speech.”

‌



Mr Burnham told the Cabinet last month that he hoped the summit will lead to "some important, concrete steps". In a letter to top ministers, he added: "Beyond it, we will need to consider the UK's long-term relationship with the EU as part of our Ten Year Plan."

The Prime Minister also tore into ex-Tory PMs Mr Johnson and David Cameron who both broke cover to warn against closer ties. Asked about their interventions, he said: “You can quote whomever you like, but I just don’t think he’s an authority on these matters.

‌



“He [Johnson] left us with a bad Brexit deal that has led to Britain losing more than its gained… I’m afraid I’m not going to listen to Boris Johnson on this particular matter. He burned bridges and created a lot of bad feeling.

“And consequently Britain has suffered as a result of that, it is right to build back and get a better, more constructive working relationship with our biggest market. And why wouldn’t I do that?”

Article continues below

Grilled on whether he would put the option of re-joining the EU on the table, Mr Burnham said: “All I’m going to do is look at what options might be available. And so that people can see the pros and cons, but will set those out, in due course. There’s no rush to do that.”

Mr Burnham said Labour's 2024 manifesto red lines – which rule out returning to the customs union, single market or free movement – would remain before a general election. “[The] British public will be in charge of whatever comes next," he said.

News.title: William and Kate live: New Prince Harry clash as interview teased moments before Earthshot Prize Awards
News.content:
The Prince and Princess of Wales dazzled at William's star-studded Earthshot Prize Awards in Mumbai today - but it appears there was another awkward clash with Prince Harry

The Princess of Wales dazzled in red as she joined husband Prince William at his Earthshot Prize Awards today.

Both she and William looked closer than ever as they glided down the green carpet in Mumbai in outfits honouring India as the annual celebration of solutions to repair the planet began.

The couple walked down the green carpet amid a battery of flash bulbs before stopping for around 30 seconds to pose for photographers, with William placing his arm around his wife’s waist and could be seen stroking her back. Kate later gave a speech where she talked about how "nature is precious".

But as they arrived at the glittering ceremony, a new interview with Prince Harry was teased on social media. It has emerged that he has given a sit-down interview on “Ukraine, Russia and preparing for war” with the conversation trailed on social media minutes before his estranged brother arrived at his awards.

The timing of the announcement, which appeared on the Telegraph’s website and social media accounts, will raise questions about the clash with William’s flagship event. The prince has been estranged from his younger brother, who moved back to the UK this summer, for several years and the rift shows no sign of abating.

It comes as William and Kate rubbed shoulders with the likes of Hollywood actor Rami Malek, Indian cricketing legend Sachin Tendulkar, Bollywood stars Alia Bhatt and Sonam Kapoor, and Bridgerton’s Simone Ashley at the Earthshot Prize Awards. Meanwhile, five environmental solutions to repairing the planet have been awarded £1million each to scale up their solution to repair and protect the planet.

News.title: RUTH CURTICE: 'Finally, a plan to help Britain's young people that isn't being done on the cheap'
News.content:
RUTH CURTICE: 'Finally, a plan to help Britain's young people that isn't being done on the cheap'

Ruth Curtice, chief executive of the Resolution Foundation, says Alan Milburn's review into the NEETs crisis is 'big, bold and brash' - but warned some young people could lose out

View 2 Images 'Alan Milburn’s review of how to help the one million young people across Britain who are neither in employment, education or training is big, bold and brash' (Image: Stefan Rousseau/Press Association)

Alan Milburn’s review of how to help the one million young people across Britain who are neither in employment, education or training is big, bold and brash.

‌



‌



It’s big on the scale of the challenge – Milburn warns that a failure to act will create a ‘lost generation’ of young people.

‌



It’s bold on the extra investment needed – almost £6billion a year in extra mental health provision, further education funding and employment support for young people. And it’s brash on welfare reform – young people will no longer be left alone on benefits.

‌



Alan is absolutely right on all three fronts. While the word 'Neet' has risen up the political agenda in recent months, in truth this crisis has been years in the making.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Should young people lose access to DWP benefits? READ MORE :

View 2 Images Ruth Curtice, chief executive of the Resolution Foundation, said: 'For too long, Britain has tried to get away with supporting young people on the cheap'

‌



For too long, Britain has tried to get away with supporting young people on the cheap. Funding for further education has been cut by 8 per cent since 2010.

Employers bleat a lot about young people not being ready for work but spend far too much of their apprenticeship funding on courses for existing, older staff at the expense of young people. And our welfare system tries to rush young people into the first available job whatever their skills, and leaves those in poor health to fend for themselves.

‌



Alan Milburn’s review offers a chance to turn the page and offer young people the help they need to get their careers off the ground. But turning his recommendations into reality are far from straightforward.

‌



New investment won’t come cheap, so in these straitened times, young people will need to be at the heart of the Government’s Spending Review next year. The new systems of support for young people need to be up and running asap as benefit cuts are suggested to soon follow.

Make no mistake the Milburn proposals involve a sharp reduction in benefits paid to some young people. The review says £3.6billion of savings will be made from removing or reducing benefits for young people who are ill or have a disability. There are around 300,000 young people getting disability benefits who are not NEET. Most of them will lose from the changes.

Article continues below

There will certainly be winners too – most clearly those young people who find work thanks to the additional support and opportunities provided. Letting them keep more of that money before benefits are removed is a crucial change.

Milburn has laid bare the extent to which young people in Britain have been short changed. The details need debating, but the first step is to step up to the plate with a whole-government focus on better services for young people. Everyone will benefit if they are given the education, training and first job opportunities they deserve.

News.title: Horror moment Nottingham taxi driver strangled by thugs as moving cab spins out of control
News.content:
Horror moment Nottingham taxi driver strangled by thugs as moving cab spins out of control

Joshua Campbell and Brad-Lee Barber were jailed at Nottingham Crown Court after CCTV captured a violent taxi robbery in Carlton, Nottingham, which saw the driver strangled while behind the wheel.

Terrifying moment duo rob taxi driver whilst car was still moving

A taxi driver was grabbed by the throat and strangled during a violent robbery that sent his moving vehicle spinning out of control, with the horror attack caught on camera.

‌



‌



Joshua Campbell, 33, and Brad-Lee Barber, 30, turned on the cabbie after becoming angry over the cost of their fare while travelling through Carlton, Nottingham, at around 10pm on April 28.

‌



Campbell lunged forward from the back seat and put the driver in a chokehold as the victim desperately tried to break free, before grabbing the steering wheel and causing the taxi to career down the road.

‌

View 4 Images Joshua Campbell and Brad-Lee Barber attacked the driver after arguing over the fare (Image: Nottinghamshire Police / SWNS)

Charles Bronson to remain in jail as bid for release fails after half a century behind bars READ MORE :

Barber stole the vehicle's cash float and fled, with footage showing Campbell losing his cap through an open door as the taxi careered down the road.

‌



The vehicle eventually stopped on Carlton Hill, where Campbell released the driver and escaped, leaving the shaken cabbie to call 999.

View 4 Images The robbery took place in Carlton, Nottingham, on April 28 (Image: Nottinghamshire Police / SWNS)

‌



Nottinghamshire Police launched an investigation following the attack, with Campbell and Barber later arrested. Campbell was charged with robbery and intentional strangulation while Barber was charged with a range of other offences.

Barber was also responsible for breaking into a Nottingham café and stealing the till on November 24 last year. He committed nine separate shop thefts at stores across Nottingham between October 2025 and May 2026.

‌



After admitting their offences, Barber and Campbell were both sentenced at Nottingham Crown Court on November 12.

View 4 Images (Image: Nottinghamshire Police / SWNS)

‌



Barber, formerly of Radford, Nottingham, was jailed for four years and seven months, while Campbell, of no fixed address, received a four-year and three-month prison sentence.

Detective Constable Andre Foster said afterwards: "Campbell and Barber were responsible between them for putting their victim through a terrifying ordeal.

‌



"Having got agitated about the price of a taxi, both men suddenly rounded on the driver, with Campbell strangling the man while the car was still moving.

View 4 Images Joshua Campbell, 33, attacked the taxi driver from the back seat and grabbed the steering wheel during the robbery. (Image: Nottinghamshire Police / SWNS)

‌



"Barber, meanwhile, took it upon himself to snatch the taxi's cash float, with the car spinning dangerously out of control as a result of the pair's actions.

"While thankfully nobody was hurt during this incident, the victim was put through a harrowing experience.

Article continues below

"In addition to the robbery – which is a very serious offence on its own – Barber was also responsible for a burglary and a series of shop thefts too.

"This type of behaviour cannot be allowed to go unchecked, so it was pleasing to see that Campbell and Barber have both received lengthy custodial sentences."

News.title: Lee Reeves' final opponent posts heartbreaking 95-word tribute after boxer's death aged 31
News.content:
Lee Reeves' final opponent posts heartbreaking 95-word tribute after boxer's death aged 31

Boxer Lee Reeves died at the age of 31 on Monday, having spent three months in a medically-induced coma following his fight with Gary Cully

View 2 Images Lee Reeves last fought Gary Cully (Image: Queensbury)

The final opponent of Lee Reeves has penned a heartbreaking statement after the tragic news of the boxer's passing at 31. Gary Cully shared the ring with Reeves at Dublin's 3Arena back in August, winning the bout via a 10th-round knockout.

‌



‌



Reeves was rushed to hospital and underwent surgery in the aftermath, before he was placed in a medically induced coma for three months. It was confirmed this week that the Limerick-born fighter had died.

‌



Reports also added that Reeves had contracted an infection at the weekend which led to his death. A statement from Queensberry read: "Everyone at Queensberry is devastated to learn ‌of the passing of Lee Reeves.

‌

"Lee was an immensely talented boxer, as well ⁠as a true role model and inspiration to his community. Our deepest condolences go to Lee's family, friends and all those who loved him.

"We ask that their privacy be respected at this incredibly difficult time. Rest in peace, Lee."

‌



Now, Cully has also paid tribute to the man he shared the squared-circle with just a matter of months ago. On Instagram, he wrote: "We shared the ring back in August but we been going back for years.

"I still remember the stadium days when I used to watch Lee in the nationals the weight above me and always be impressed by his fights and his flashy gear myself and Luke Thomas used to plague him to spit us out an MC when we were staying in Dublin on training camp and they’d always be fire.

"What a character and a gent. It’s never been nothing love between us champ can’t really believe I’m writing this but RIP brother."

Jonathan O'Brien, Reeves' long-time friend and coach, also shared a touching tribute online. He said: "Goodbye son, sleep tight, you fought so hard till the end.

"We love you so much, rest in peace with your mam and brother waiting at the heavenly gates. Look over your sisters and your father, give them the strength to get through this. We love you Lee."

Limerick City councillor Catherine Slattery, meanwhile, said: "Limerick is a very dark place tonight with the loss of Lee Reeves. Lee was not just a boxer that excelled in his career - he was a mental health advocate who highlighted mental health and how it can affect young people.

News.title: Premium Bond holders forced to return winnings after major blunder
News.content:
Premium Bond holders forced to return winnings after major blunder

National Savings and Investments (NS&I) said it paid out duplicate Premium Bonds prizes worth £518,000 to thousands of customers following a 'technical error'

View 2 Images The NS&I has forced customers to return the money (Image: Getty Images)

Thousands of Premium Bond holders have been forced to return their winnings in another major blunder by National Savings and Investments (NS&I).

‌



‌



The Treasury-backed bank wrongly told customers they had won Premium Bond prizes following May's draw, paying out £518,000 to around 3,500 people after having duplicated payments in a "technical error".

‌



Many of these payments were automatically reversed from customer accounts, but the bank is still needing to track down and return an outstanding £1,600 in overpaid prize money.

‌



One customer, who genuinely won £1,700 said NS&I held his money hostage after he was overpaid a further £325, with access to his accounts frozen until the funds were recovered, reports The Times.

An NS&I spokesperson told the Mirror: "In May this year, due to a technical error, duplicate Premium Bonds prize payments were made to around 3,500 Direct Saver accounts.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



View 2 Images The payments were made following a 'technical error,' NS&I said (Image: Getty Images)

"We contacted all account holders and apologised for the inconvenience caused and cancelled the duplicate payments."

‌



Despite a series of recent errors, Premium Bonds remain Britain's most popular savings product and are held by around 22 million people.

They work in a similar way to an easy access savings account, allowing holders to win tax-free prizes and avoid penalties for cashing in bonds.

‌



The latest error comes after the bank faced a major scandal in March 2026 involving around £476 million in unclaimed or delayed funds belonging to roughly 37,500 bereaved families.

An administrative and system failure meant that legacy products, savings, and Premium Bonds belonging to deceased customers were not properly identified or paid out to their estates.

‌



NS&I management was alerted to the problems in December 2025, but the scandal became public in March 2026, sparking criticism that the warning signs were ignored for a number of years.

Chief executive Dax Harkins resigned in March 2026 and was replaced by Sir Jim Harra, the former boss of HM Revenue & Customs.

‌



In June 2023, NS&I also paid the wrong rate of interest to 3,265 customers, sending them an extra £600 and losing £2m. At that time, those who were overpaid did not have to return the money.

In August, a bereaved family were wrongly told they had inherited £30,000 of Premium Bonds.

‌



A male relative, who said he intended to use the money to pay for a loved one's funeral, complained to the Financial Ombudsman Service but was given just a few hundred pounds in compensation.

Consumer rights expert Martyn James said that while customers were not entitled to keep payments made in error, they may be able to appeal to the bank for compensation.

‌



"If they told you you'd won it and given you the expectation the cash was yours, you could argue that you shouldn't have to give it back," he said.

"While you may not get the lot, a suitable compensation payment may apply if you can demonstrate you entered into an agreement off the back of what the firm told you.

Article continues below

"So if you were told you'd won £3,000 and bought a three-piece sofa suite, you could say you wouldn't have done that had you not been told you'd won the money."

News.title: Russian Antonov An-12 military plane crashes with 'up to 17 people dead'
News.content:
Russian Antonov An-12 military plane crashes with 'up to 17 people dead'

Seventeen people have been killed after an Antonov An-12 plane crashed into a field in Siberia, according to Russian media reports

View 2 Images A Russian Antonov An-12 aircraft has crashed in Siberia (Image: @bayraktar_1love/X)

Seventeen people have been killed after a Russian plane crashed into a field in south-west Siberia, according to Russian media reports.

‌



‌



The Antonov An-12 was flying from Novosibirsk to Kansk, both cities in Siberia, when it reportedly came down near the village of Yagunovo, in the Kemerovo region, on Tuesday night (local time). All 17 people on board were killed, according to the Russian Telegram channel SHOT, which reported that wreckage was scattered across an area with a radius of around 500 metres.

‌



Ilya Seredyuk, governor of the Kemerovo region, said an "aviation incident" had occurred near Yagunovo, adding that emergency services were working at the scene.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and find them easily on Google, make us your preferred source. It's free and easy to do - just click here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 2 Images The crash happened on Tuesday (Image: Telegram)

‌



Premium Bond holders forced to return winnings after major blunder READ MORE :

An emergency response centre has been set up at the crash site, Seredyuk said.

When a fire broke out on board, the crew desperately tried to steer the aircraft away from residential areas, Russian broadcaster Ren TV reported.

Article continues below

The cause of the crash is under investigation.

The An-12 is a Soviet-designed turboprop transport aircraft used for military and cargo operations. Initial reports suggest the aircraft was operating as a cargo plane at the time of the crash.

News.title: Supermarket cheddar beats Cathedral City and Pilgrims in taste test
News.content:
Supermarket cheddar beats Cathedral City and Pilgrims in taste test

This budget-friendly cheese has come out on top

View 4 Images You don't have to spend big for big taste (Image: Getty)

Christmas is just over five weeks away, and when the festive season kicks off, so does the season of cheese boards. Of course, no self-respecting cheese board is complete without a gorgeous sharp, crumbly cheddar — but which one offers the best combination of value and taste?

‌



‌



Thankfully, consumer champion Which? rounded up 75 cheese lovers to put 11 extra mature cheddars through their paces. The blind taste test has revealed that a budget supermarket own-brand has beaten Cathedral City and Pilgrims Choice to claim the top spot.

‌



The Which? taste test of extra-mature cheddars pitched eight supermarket own-brands against one another, alongside three well-known branded options

‌



View 4 Images These are the best cheese on the market (Image: Getty)

What is the best mature cheddar?

Taking first place with an impressive approval rating of 78% is Aldi's Specially Selected West Country Extra Mature Cheddar. It also scoops a Great Value accolade, coming in at just £2.99 for 350g.

Three quarters of tasters felt the cheddar's colour looked just right. And a similar proportion were won over by its smooth, firm and creamy texture.

‌



View 4 Images This Aldi cheese came out on top (Image: Which?)

Julie Ashfield, chief commercial officer at Aldi UK, said: "We're delighted to see our Specially Selected West Country Extra Mature Cheddar recognised by Which? as a Best Buy. We know how important quality and value are, particularly at Christmas, and this award is a fantastic result for our team. At just £2.99, shoppers can enjoy an award-winning cheddar that delivers on both taste and value, making it a great addition to any festive cheeseboard."

‌



Another cheese awarded a 'Best Buy' in the taste test was Pilgrims Choice Extra Mature Cheddar, priced at £4.25 for 350g (£1.21 per 100g). It achieved a score of 76% from testers, with cheese enthusiasts praising its smooth, creamy and salty qualities.

Waitrose Davidstow Cornish Extra Mature Cheddar also earned a 'Best Buy' rating at £4.25 for 350g (£1.21 per 100g), securing an overall approval rating of 75%. Tasters were won over by its salt levels and creamy texture.

‌



What were the other favourites?

Cathedral City Our Extra Mature Cheddar: £3.50 for 350g (£1 per 100g)

This well-known branded cheese received a 74% approval rating, with tasters won over by its appearance, saltiness and smoothness; however, some felt they would have preferred a slightly stronger flavour and a crumblier texture.

View 4 Images Cathedral City scored well (Image: Which?)

‌



The appearance and smoothness of this cheese helped it secure a 74% score. The majority of cheese lovers applauded its firmness and saltiness, and most were impressed by its creaminess and level of crumble - though a third felt it crumbled a little too much.

Sainsbury's Taste The Difference Extra Mature Cumbrian Cheddar £3.95 for 350g (£1.13 per 100g)

This cheese also scored 74%, though just over a third of tasters felt it lacked sufficient crumble. Nevertheless, it boasted an appealing appearance and a robust flavour.

‌



Although this cheese was priced the same as the Aldi favourite, it didn't fare quite as well for flavour, achieving a score of 73%.

Testers appreciated its appearance and smoothness, and its creamy texture was considered just right by a large majority, who also felt salt levels were spot-on.

‌



How did the rest of the cheeses score?

Tesco came bottom with 66% and was among the more expensive choices at £3.50 for 200g (£1.75 per 100g).

Asda Exceptional Wyke Farms Somerset Extra Mature Cheddar £3.52 for 300g (£1.17 per 100g)– 72%

Marks & Spencer Cornish Cruncher Extra Mature Cheddar £5.25 for 300g (£1.75 per 100g) – 70%

News.title: Rooney says he considered taking his own life at Man Utd
News.content:
Warning: This article contains references to suicide

Wayne Rooney says he was "contemplating suicide" during his playing days at Manchester United and was "speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up".

The former England captain joined United from Everton in 2004 and went on to become the club's record goalscorer, with 253 goals in 559 appearances.

But Rooney, speaking with Gabby Logan on the Life at the Midpoint podcast, external, detailed his struggles off the pitch when eldest son Kai, who is now 17, was a baby.

"When I was drinking, I would lock myself in my house for two days and just drink," said Rooney, when asked about the lowest point in his life.

"This is probably in my best part of my career playing wise."

The 41-year-old went on to explain how he "struggled to deal with it all" and, after opening up to his wife Coleen and his mother, knew he "needed help to get through it".

"I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with," he added.

"I didn't want Kai seeing me like that, so that's why I'd hide away as well.

"I got to a place where you're contemplating suicide. I just didn't want to be around anyone. I didn't want to see people in the streets. I didn't want to go into shops.

"I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else, [I] really struggled with it."

Rooney, who scored 53 goals in 120 England appearances, was recently named pundit of the year at the Broadcast Sport Awards and is currently appearing on reality TV show I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here.

He helped United win five Premier League titles, the Champions League, Europa League, FA Cup and three EFL Cups before leaving them to return to the Toffees in 2017.

But the former forward said he learned to mask his feelings during his lowest moments.

"You don't want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it," Rooney added.

"Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man, if you like, for doing that.

"I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because when I look back I was probably at the height of my career, I've just had a young son, I've just been married.

"It should be the happiest point in my life and it wasn't.

"It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking.

"Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it."

News.title: William and Kate celebrate Earthshot Prize winners in Mumbai
News.content:
The Prince and Princess of Wales have said environmental innovators are changing the lives of future generations as they celebrated this year's winners of the Earthshot Prize.

Five award-winners were named at a ceremony in Mumbai, India, and will each receive Â£1m to scale up their projects.

One of the winners was a country - with Bhutan being recognised for its environmental policies that help to safeguard water supplies for nearly a fifth of the world's population.

Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, actor Rami Malek and Bollywood stars Alia Bhatt and Sonam Kapoor were among those who attended the ceremony, which saw performances from Take That and Bridgerton's Simone Ashley.

The annual event, founded by Prince William and now in its sixth year, was hosted by Karan Johar, presenter of The Traitors India and one of the country's most well-known film makers.

Prince William was joined by Catherine at the ceremony as the royal couple continued their first official overseas trip together in four years. Catherine's cancer treatment has limited the amount she has travelled internationally.

They arrived on the event's green carpet wearing outfits celebrating Indian fashion.

Prince William wore a bespoke Bandhgala, a classic Indian formal jacket, while Catherine was dressed in an Anarkali dress by Mahima Mahajan made from handwoven silk Georgette with traditional Banarasi gold detailing.

During his speech, Prince William said this decade was the moment when positive change becomes irreversible" and remarked that history was "not written by challenges alone", but also by those who rose to meet them.

He added that "around the world, we are witnessing human ingenuity on a remarkable scale".

Separately, Catherine highlighted the "hope" represented by entrepreneurs, organisations and scientists tackling the environmental crisis.

The princess, who presented an award, also said: "Just as the natural world finds ways to adapt and flourish, so too can we, when we nurture new ideas and give them the opportunity to grow.

"The people we're celebrating tonight are a huge part of that story. Their work will inspire and create seismic change that will improve lives for generations to come."

News.title: How Met failed to stop rape-unit detective who abused women
News.content:
Warning: Contains details of violence, coercion and sexual abuse - and strong language

The Metropolitan Police repeatedly missed opportunities to stop a predatory detective inspector from sexually exploiting women whose cases he investigated, including one who married him and later died in unexplained circumstances, BBC Panorama can reveal.

Warren Arter used his position - running a unit investigating sexual assaults in south-east London - to target women it was his job to protect.

Two women, speaking out for the first time, have told Panorama how Arter groomed them. One says he raped her.

In the case of his wife, Rebekah, he filmed her being sexually abused and distributed the footage. She died in Barbados two years ago, while on holiday with him. On Sunday, the BBC revealed how he lied about what happened on the Caribbean island.

There were multiple investigations into Arter while he was employed by the Met. Now the former detective who led one of them has told the BBC that senior bosses tried to interfere with his inquiries, despite him having found potential victims.

While Arter was suspended as a result of that investigation, he remained on full pay for seven years - before being sacked in 2023 for drug offences.

The following year, the Met - having learned of his wife's death in Barbados - arrested him on his return to the UK for sexual offences alleged by another woman.

Arter took his own life days later in HMP Wandsworth. Despite the evidence against him, the Met has not reviewed all the cases he handled.

News.title: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements
News.content:
The UK has sanctioned companies it said are involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, in the first package of measures since the government announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.

The government said the sanctions against eight construction and property development firms would disrupt their flows of finance and ability to support building in the West Bank.

The construction of settlements, which are illegal under international law, has risen sharply in recent years. Settler attacks on Palestinians and their property have also surged.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar called the sanctions a "hostile act targeting private, law-abiding companies".

Criticising the move on X, he wrote that Israel - as it has done in the past - will respond with "countermeasures", and that "decisions will be announced in due course".

"Israel will not bow to external pressure or change its policies as a result," Saar said, adding that they will "consider new ways to strengthen Jewish communities" in the West Bank, and "protect those involved in developing and building".

Israel previously condemned UK sanctions related to West Bank settlements, accusing the Labour government of "systematically acting against the State of Israel".

The Palestinian foreign ministry welcomed the sanctions and called on other countries to follow suit.

It comes two days before the deadline for bids for construction tenders in the highly sensitive E1 area east of Jerusalem.

The plans, which have been condemned internationally, would in effect divide the West Bank in two and cut it off from East Jerusalem.

UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said the E1 development would render a two-state solution "unviable" by "cutting through the heart of Palestine".

The sanctions also target Tzav 9, an Israeli activist movement which the UK government says has organised and carried out blockades to prevent aid entering Gaza.

Responding to the announcement, the group said: "Tzav 9 is a movement of abiding citizens from all the political spectrum, and we've always protested peacefully."

It comes after the UK expanded its human rights sanctions regime last month, enabling the government to sanction individuals and companies involved in violations of international humanitarian law anywhere in the world.

The government is also developing separate legislation to ban the import of goods from Israeli settlements and the provision of advertising services for settlement properties in the UK.

News.title: Woman who accuses Russell Brand of rape says prison message 'upsetting'
News.content:
A woman who has made allegations against Russell Brand has said she finds it "upsetting" and "really shocking" that he was able to claim he was innocent from prison, following his conviction for rape and sexual assault.

Speaking after the comedian's wife Laura read out a message from him on their Sunday Service show on YouTube, Mia Latter told BBC Radio 4's Today programme she found it "appalling" to hear "this Christian message alongside absolute lies".

"I just felt for those women that stood trial and everything they went through," she said.

Latter, 37, who has alleged she was raped by Brand when she was 16, was not a complainant in his recent criminal trial and he denies her claims.

Brand is currently serving a 10-and-half-year prison sentence after being found guilty at Southwark Crown Court of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, involving four women.

In recent years he has positioned himself as a Christian influencer, and has a large following, including in the US. In the message read out by his wife on their show, Brand said: "I am not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for."

Latter said the broadcast "was really shocking to me... it was appalling, frankly, it was upsetting to watch".

She said the woman who gave evidence in the trial "got their verdict, and for him to say, 'I'm innocent, I'm not guilty' - well, you are, you're a convicted rapist now. There's no arguing with that".

Downing Street said on Monday it expects action to be taken if Brand is found to have broken prison rules.

Justice Secretary Alex Norris said that "prisoners are rightly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims".

Latter said she was 16 when she met Brand, who was 30 at the time.

She was one of six women who made allegations against him as part of a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches investigation in 2023. None of the women were involved in his recent trial.

In an interview with the Sunday Times this week, Latter said Brand told her to keep their relationship secret from her school friends and claimed that he referred to her as "the child" in front of his entourage.

She has waived her right to anonymity in order to campaign for a staggered age of consent to be introduced in the UK that would make sexual relationships between 16 and 17 year-olds and adults illegal.

Latter told the Sunday Times the Crown Prosecution Service decided not to include her as part of Brand's criminal trial but police wanted her to be part of "subsequent" proceedings. She told the paper that she would not continue with the criminal process so she could focus on her campaign.

News.title: Channel 4 admits it doesn't know number of Married At First Sight UK sex abuse complaints
News.content:
Channel 4's bosses were also questioned at length about Brand by MPs in the hearing.

Brand's work on Channel 4 included hosting Big Brother sister show Big Brother's Big Mouth and its celebrity equivalent from 2004 to 2007, a chat show in 2006, and appearing on Big Fat Quiz of the Year.

Addressing Dogra and Channel 4's chairman Geoff Cooper, MPs said the member of staff who made two complaints about Brand "fell through the cracks".

In response, Dogra said: "I'm not sure we can apologise enough as an organisation for putting her through that twice. We have apologised in public in the past and in private."

She accepted that the woman's complaints were "not handled properly" and added that "it's almost unforgivable that happened twice".

When asked by the committee if junior members of staff could raise complaints against a star without fear of losing their job, Dogra replied she "can't say 100%" that that would be the case.

"What I can do is set the standard, set the tone, make sure that the facilities are available, make sure that my staff and the production companies understand the repercussions of not complying, and understand the kind of culture that I'm trying to set, and we're trying to set as an industry."

She also said she found the "cultural personality" around Brand "horrendous".

"I find it distasteful, and I look at the jokes... that is the lowest form of humour, because these are jokes that are made at the expense of someone else's physical safety.

"I don't believe it should have been acceptable then, and I certainly don't think it's acceptable now."

During the session, Dame Caroline also put to Channel 4 bosses that in both the MAFS UK and Brand cases, the broadcaster appeared like "a child with their hand in the cookie jar".

The committee chairwoman asked: "To what extent can you reassure us that Channel 4's priority is genuinely the welfare of the staff who work there, the staff who have worked there, and the people who take part in your shows - rather than purely when the world is looking at you and you suddenly feel that you've got a reputational reason to take a look at these shows?"

Dogra responded by saying that when Channel 4 commissioned the review, "we didn't even know whether the Panorama programme would be made".

She added: "We had received a right-to-reply letter and the programme came out six weeks later, but it equally it could not have been made. We always intended to do the review."

In the instance of the woman who tried to complain about Brand, she added: "I'm not sure there are more apologies we can give. Because none of those things should've happened."

If you have more information about this story, you can reach Noor by email at noor.nanji@bbc.co.uk

News.title: Henry Nowak killer applies to appeal against conviction
News.content:
The man jailed for murdering Henry Nowak has applied to appeal against his conviction.

Vickrum Digwa, who stabbed the 18-year-old student with a large dagger in Belmont Road, Southampton, on 3 December 2025, has also asked the Supreme Court to review his sentence, his lawyers have confirmed.

Earlier this month the Court of Appeal raised his minimum term from 21 to 25 years, after the Attorney General argued it was unduly lenient.

The BBC understands Digwa wants to argue that his conviction for murder is unsafe on four grounds. The applications do not mean Digwa will automatically get any further hearings or reviews.

Imran Khan and Partners, Digwa's lawyers, said: "An application has been lodged seeking to appeal against Vickrum Singh Digwa's conviction.

"That application concerns the safety of the conviction and is separate from the proceedings concerning sentence."

News.title: Government must act now or lose Royal Mail, former minister warns
News.content:
Former Business Secretary Peter Kyle has said the government must act urgently to "level the playing field" for Royal Mail or risk the business becoming unviable.

He said he was concerned that the firm was being "undercut" by rival parcel delivery firms who did not employ staff under the same conditions.

Royal Mail, which is owned by International Distribution Services, has struggled in recent years with increased competition, fewer letters being sent and fines from the regulator for missing delivery targets.

A government spokesperson said it would consider whether further reforms are required to the parcel market after the watchdog, Ofcom, publishes its annual monitoring report in December.

Kyle had started to prepare officials at the Department for Business and Trade (DBT) to look at the delivery market for parcels shortly before he was replaced in his job by Jonathan Reynolds as business secretary in July.

He said a "crunch point" had been reached where the government had to make a decision about whether it wants Royal Mail "to be a viable proposition in the future".

He said his review would have looked at where the costs in that market lay and where the profit was being made, to see successful companies upheld "the values of business in Britain today".

"If we leave it another few years then Royal Mail will just become unviable and it will just collapse under the weight of having full-time employees," he said.

According to Royal Mail, 98% of its 130,000 workers are permanent employees, with rights to benefits including pensions, sick pay and holiday pay.

Some other parcel delivery companies use self-employed delivery drivers, with some offering an opt-in service that gives couriers limited additional benefits.

Royal Mail is also legally obliged to offer customers a "one price goes anywhere" service across the UK and to deliver first class letters six days a week to every address.

Kyle's proposed review would not have considered further changes to Royal Mail's universal service obligations or to terms and conditions for its staff.

News.title: Ex-Reform Wales leader Dan Thomas faces no further police action after assault arrest
News.content:
A police investigation into Reform's former leader in Wales has been dropped, two months after he was arrested on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviour.

Thomas said he had been "vindicated" by Gwent Police's decision that he should face no further action.

The arrest had led the Member of Senedd (MS) for Casnewydd Islwyn to resign from his role leading the largest Senedd opposition group, triggering a leadership contest and the election of Helen Jenner as his replacement.

Nigel Farage said he was "very pleased that Dan Thomas has been cleared", adding he had "stood by him throughout this process".

Jenner will remain as the party's Welsh leader, the BBC understands.

Thomas said he had been subjected to "false allegations" and had been "fully cooperating with the police".

"When this began, I said I had done nothing wrong. Today, I have been vindicated."

He said Farage, Jenner and Senedd colleagues had been "incredibly supportive".

"To my family and the people of Blackwood, my hometown, thank you for standing by me. Those constituents who have stopped me in the street to wish me well have been a real source of strength."

On X, Jenner said it was "great news".

She added she was "so pleased to see a close friend having his name cleared".

Farage said: "I am very pleased that Dan Thomas has been cleared. I have stood by him throughout this process."

Dan Thomas was picked by Farage to be the party's Welsh leader before the 2026 Senedd election.

The news that he was quitting as leader following the arrest broke on the same day that Sarah Cooper-Lessad announced that she was quitting his party for Plaid Cymru.

At the time of the arrest Gwent Police said a 45-year-old man from Aberbargoed, Caerphilly, had been arrested on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviour.

A spokesperson for Gwent Police said: "We take all allegations of assault and controlling and coercive behaviour extremely seriously, [and] a thorough investigation took place.

"The 45-year-old man who was arrested has been released with no further action."

News.title: British Airways plane veers off Heathrow taxiway
News.content:
A British Airways plane became stuck in the grass at Heathrow Airport after it veered off the taxiway.

The Boeing 787 Dreamliner bound for Lagos in Nigeria became stuck after its front wheel entered the grass as it was taxiing independently from the gate to the runway shortly after 10:00 GMT.

A spokesperson for the west London airport said they were continuing to assist the plane back to the aircraft parking area, adding that there were no injuries and no impact on wider operations.

A spokesperson for BA said: "We're very sorry to our customers for the disruption to their flight. Our teams are working to get them on their way as quickly as possible and are in touch with them to put things right."

It is not clear why the incident involving BA flight 75 happened. All the passengers disembarked safely and efforts to extract the aircraft are still taking place.

News.title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable
News.content:
The author of the independent review into gender identity services for young people says she does not support the current draft bill banning conversion practices - having previously welcomed it.

Baroness Cass told BBC Radio 4's Today programme while it is "desirable" to ban the practices, "the challenge is that we have not yet as far as I can see got a workable bill".

At a parliamentary committee scrutinising the bill, she also said it risked "serious unintended consequences" for parents of children suffering gender distress, or medical professionals working in that area.

A government spokesperson said they welcomed her comments.

They added they would take all evidence put forward by the committee seriously as they "want to get this ban right". The government has said the bill would protect LGBT people in England and Wales.

Conversion practices are generally described as interventions, treatments or activities designed to change or suppress someone's sexual orientation or gender identity.

This can sometimes happen in religious or family settings and can be very distressing for the person at the centre of it.

There have been long-running campaigns in the UK to outlaw such practices, and in its 2024 manifesto, the Labour party promised to introduce a bill banning them.

When the government introduced its draft legislation, external in June this year, Baroness Cass was quoted in the publicity for it, external.

In it, she said: "I am pleased to see that the government is bringing forward legislation which not only gives a clearer definition of what conversion practices are, compared to previous drafts, but also what they are not."

She went on to say she looked forward to the bill receiving further scrutiny before it became law.

But asked at the Draft Conversion Practices Bill committee if she supported the bill's current form, she said simply "no".

Baroness Cass said the increased "polarisation" used in the debate around gender meant people may use the new law in a way that wasn't intended.

The current wording of the bill requires the victim to suffer "serious harm to the individual's physical or mental health, or serious alarm or distress to the individual which has a substantial adverse effect on their usual day-to-day activities".

But Baroness Cass said she worried this wording left open the possibility of "vexatious" complaints that could put therapists working with young gender-distressed people at risk of prosecution.

"Therapeutic interactions can be distressing and often are because you're discussing quite sensitive issues," she told the Today programme.

"So If a young person comes away feeling upset, distressed, angry, that might be the result of a quite appropriate therapeutic intervention but still could be judged as poor professional practice."

She told the committee that professionals working at the new NHS Gender Dysphoria Clinics were concerned that even complaints processes that didn't result in a prosecution could be damaging.

"The problem is the chilling effect of professionals knowing that they may be open to complaint, and indeed prosecution," she told the Today programme.

Baroness Cass also raised concerns about the possible impact the new law could have on families.

She said that, for instance, if a parent stopped a child's money if they thought they might buy a "breast binder or hormones" that this may also fall within the scope of the bill and result in prosecution.

Asked about her apparent support for the bill when it was first published, Baroness Cass said that she was in favour of the idea but had not had the time to read the details before the press release was to be published, but went ahead and gave the quote anyway.

When she published her report on gender identity services for young people in 2024, she described conversion practices as "abhorrent". She says she still feels no LGBT people should be subjected to conversion practices.

She told the committee she wants "a bill that protects the people it's supposed to protect, but doesn't accidentally entrap those who you don't want to [entrap]".

The bill has received support from several LGBT charities, such as Stonewall, and organisations like the British Association for Counselling and Psychotherapy.

The government said: "We want to get this ban right, which is why we have put this draft bill forward for pre-legislative scrutiny.

"We welcome both Baroness Cass's support for taking action to end abusive conversion practices, and her comments on the need for legislation to avoid adverse consequences.

"We will take all evidence put forward by the committee seriously as we move forward in ending almost a decade of delay for LGBT+ people who should never have to suffer abuse in an effort to change who they are."

The committee hearings continue.

News.title: Restaurant with zero hygiene score fined thousands for 'stomach-churning' offences
News.content:
A restaurant has been handed fines of thousands of pounds over "stomach-churning" food hygiene offences, after council inspectors found "exceptionally poor" cleanliness, including rodent droppings and leaking grease, on the premises.

Mohammed Sueb, of the Taj Restaurant in Merthyr Tydfil, admitted 12 food hygiene offences.

The Indian restaurant was ordered to close following an inspection in November 2025, which saw it given a 'zero' hygiene rating.

A later re-inspection by environmental health officers in January led to legal proceedings.

Last week, Merthyr Tydfil Magistrates' Court was told of a "blatant disregard" for regulations, leading to a fine of Â£8,000 and more than Â£4,000 in charges.

News.title: Man pleads guilty to harassing Jess Phillips MP
News.content:
A man has pleaded guilty to two charges of harassing the Labour MP Jess Phillips by sending her aggressive and threatening emails.

At Gloucester Crown Court, Lee Owens, 47, admitted sending an "excessive volume" of emails to Phillips, the MP for Birmingham Yardley, between January 22 and January 25, and July 10 and July 14 last year.

Phillips, the former minister for safeguarding and violence against women and girls, said in a statement: "While I already have a tiring and difficult job trying to help victims of harassment and abuse get justice and care, it's made even harder when you are suffering as a victim yourself."

Owens, of Matson in Gloucester, will be sentenced on 7 January 2027.

News.title: E-motorbike killer's jail sentence increased
News.content:
The rider of an illegal e-motorbike who knocked down and killed an 86-year-old grandmother has had his "unduly lenient" jail term increased by almost two years.

Billy Stokoe, then 18, had taken cannabis and was using a mobile phone when he hit Gloria Stephenson on a zebra crossing in Sunderland last year, then rode off.

In May he admitted causing death by dangerous driving and was sentenced to six years and nine months but, after a referral by the solicitor general, judges at the Court of Appeal raised it to eight years and six months.

Julie Francis, one of the victim's daughters, said the decision would not "bring our mum back" but "I feel like as a family we've been listened to".

Dashcam footage showed Stokoe did not slow down or try to avoid Stephenson, who was walking her daughter's dog and trying to complete her 10,000 steps a day.

Stokoe was thrown off the motorbike but did not stop at the scene.

Instead, he rode away to change his clothes and hide the bike at a friend's house before handing himself in at a police station just over an hour later.

News.title: Apple down: Music, Apple Pay, App Store, iCloud and more not working in major outage
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Many of Apple’s online services appear have gone down in a major outage.

Apple Music, the App Store and other iCloud services were affected by the technical issues. Some users also reported issues with Apple Pay.

Other Apple platforms, such as its Apple TV streaming service, appeared to be working as normal however.

Apple said that the affected services “may be slow or unavailable” on its official status page. It gave no indication of the cause of the problem or when it would be fixed.

The Apple outage comes after a run of technical problems at other major technology services. Microsoft Outlook was down for a day last week, for instance, and a separate outage meant that planes were grounded across the US just hours after.

The troubles have led to conspiracy theories that , or suggestions that . But

More follows

News.title: Andy Burnham paves way for new welfare system to end Neets crisis
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Andy Burnham has paved the way for a completely new welfare system in the wake of a long-awaited blueprint designed to end Britain’s youth unemployment crisis.

No 10 said the prime minister wanted the wide-ranging report by former Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn – which recommended a system with more employment support but significantly lower benefit payments – to be a “watershed moment in how we think about welfare” as ministers promised “a new settlement for young people”.

The government endorsed Mr Milburn’s 278-page report shortly after it was published on Tuesday – including by giving the author a new government role – but Mr Burnham will now come under pressure to commit to the sweeping proposals, which includes £3.6bn in savings a year in social security cuts by 2036.

Campaigners and charities have welcomed the report as an attempt to solve the problem of a “lost generation” of under-25s across the UK not in education, employment or training – known as Neets.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham has already said his government is ‘ready to grasp the nettle here and make a better system for young people’ ( PA )

But some pointed to the fact the projected savings would only amount to £200m a year after a decade, while the IFS, the leading economic think tank, said it was hard to judge “the plausibility” of some of the projected effects, including Mr Milburn’s aim to get 440,000 young people into work by 2036.

The major report called for:

An “entirely new” benefits system for young people that would see the health element of Universal Credit and personal independence payments (Pip) replaced with a “youth allowance”

Devolved Youth Opportunity Services to bring employment, health and career support together under one roof, guaranteeing young people access to a named adviser after 14 days

The creation of incentives for employers to hire young people, including payments of between £3,000 and £7,000 for hiring those who have been Neet for six months

The lowering of the rate of national insurance contributions for employees between 21 and 24 over a five-year period, with retail and hospitality prioritised for the tax cut

A boost in the number of children ready for school by age five from 63 per cent to 90, as well as introducing a more vocational curriculum to make pupils ready for the working world

After the report was published, work and pensions secretary Pat McFadden told MPs: “We need a new settlement for young people.

“This new settlement must give people the best chance of higher living standards for the whole of their lives. It must change the equation that sees us spend £25 on the consequences of inactivity for every pound to be spent on opportunity.”

open image in gallery Alan Milburn warned of the risk of a ‘lost generation’ ( PA )

The proposals would see ministers spend £5.8 bn by 2036-37, funding the new youth opportunity service and support, including tax breaks and bonuses for firms employing young people.

In return, they would save £3.6bn from the welfare bill and £2.4bn in extra tax revenue, saving £200m that year.

Launching his report, Mr Milburn said: “Britain is at risk of losing a generation of young people, not because they lack talent, not because they lack ambition, not because they do not want to work. This is not a crisis of aspiration; it is a crisis of opportunity.”

He also warned ministers that “half measures will not do” because “the scale of the problem is just too big for that”. Advising against cherry-picking his recommendations, he added: “It sort of does fit together as one package.”

Mr Milburn also demanded a “downpayment” of £500 million in the next financial year, arguing his proposed package must be a top priority in next year’s spending review.

He also warned Mr Burnham he did not have much time. “Prime Minister Burnham is a half-term prime minister and so he needs to get on with it. And I know that he wants to. So I’m very hopeful indeed,” he said.

open image in gallery Work and pensions secretary Pat McFadden made a statement to MPs following the publication of the Alan Milburn's review into youth unemployment ( PA )

If legislation was passed quickly, he said, then welfare savings could begin to be delivered by the end of the decade.

Mr Milburn also told Labour MPs, who derailed attempts by Keir Starmer to cut he benefits bill, that his scheme aimed to get people into work, which was “a very different argument” and was a change from a “fiscal grab”.

In response, the government said it would take a number of steps, including creating a new youth opportunities unit reporting directly to the PM, but only respond fully to the report later this year.

Labour MP Rachael Maskell, previously a rebel on welfare issues, said she welcomed the “ambition” though the “details are yet to be spelt out and therefore I will work with government to ensure they land in the right place.”

Earlier Mr Milburn admitted that policies introduced by the Labour government have affected the jobs market and “made it harder” for companies to employ young people.

Hours before he unveiled his report, he even warned a “course correction” was needed after his party’s National Insurance hikes.

Meanwhile, the Institute for Fiscal Studies said the proposals would mean “many of those with less severe disabilities would be likely to see large income losses initially”, although this could be offset if they enter work.

The forecast £3.6 billion a year savings would be equivalent to 41 per cent of projected spending on health-related benefits for young people in 2036–37, the think tank said.

The report’s own modelling anticipates its proposals would bring an extra 440,000 into work, bringing the Neet rate to 7% by 2036, slightly short of their target.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said: “We don’t need costly government schemes to fix Labour’s own mistakes.

“We need to stop making it so expensive and risky to hire young people.”

News.title: Wales v Portugal LIVE: Visitors continue life without Cristiano Ronaldo in Nations League decider
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Manchester United’s Bruno Fernandes at a Portugal training session in Cardiff ahead of playing Wales on Tuesday ( PA Wire )

Portugal aim to secure their first victory since the retirement of captain Cristiano Ronaldo as they visit Wales in the final round of the Nations League.

Portugal suffered a humiliating 4-1 home defeat to Denmark as they paid tribute to their record goalscorer on Saturday, which also meant they missed the chance to secure top spot in their Nations League group.

Portugal will ensure top spot if they avoid defeat in Cardiff, with Denmark needing to beat Norway in the other game in Group A4 to have any chance of overtaking them. Wales will finish bottom after losing 3-1 to Norway last time out.

Craig Bellamy’s side are safe from direct relegation from League A and will instead enter the relegation/promotion play-offs in March regardless of tonight’s result, but will be playing for pride as they seek to end the Nations League on a winning note.

Follow updates from Wales v Portugal below

News.title: Bono accidentally destroys table during interview to promote U2’s new album
News.content:
U2 frontman Bono suffered an embarrassing mishap during an interview to promote their new album when he accidentally broke a table.

The Irish superstars were appearing on the Track Star* YouTube channel and podcast on November 16 to promote their 16th studio album, Carnaval De Luz, which was released last week.

While guitarist The Edge was answering a question, Bono tentatively put his feet up on a coffee table in front of him, causing it to collapse and bottles of water to fall to the floor.

Quick as a flash, he quipped “ Edge, you are such a mess,” to the amusement of his bandmates.

News.title: Fox News is already starting the culture wars over the new Grand Theft Auto VI
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

As gamers anxiously await this week’s release of Grand Theft Auto VI, Fox News hosts are already starting the culture wars over the crime-fueled video game series.

Fox & Friends Weekend hosts Rachel Campos-Duffy, Charles Hurt and Griff Jenkins recently looked at a preview of the new game, featuring characters Jason Duval, an Army veteran working for local drug runners, and Lucia Caminos, who was previously jailed after fighting for her family.

“I’m gonna push back a little,” Campos-Duffy, wife of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, said. “I’m not thinking that this is a good thing for our culture.”

Jenkins then suggested Campos-Duffy could play as Luicia, prompting her to ask, “Is she the hooker?”

“No, she’s a partner-in-crime,” Jenkins said. Campos-Duffy then laughed it off. “You can maybe play and get her to go straight,” Jenkins added.

open image in gallery Fox & Friends Weekend hosts Rachel Campos-Duffy said in response to the forthcoming Grand Theft Auto VI, ‘I’m not thinking that this is a good thing for our culture’ ( Fox News )

Conservatives and liberals have long fought over cultural beliefs, typically when it comes to civil rights, including diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives and LGBTQ+ issues.

Fox News is known to promote the conservative view, railing against DEI and trans rights. And now, the network is coming after your favorite video game.

In Grand Theft Auto VI, set to be released at midnight on Thursday, Jason and Lucia will find themselves in the middle of a criminal conspiracy in the fictional state of Leonida, where they will need to rely on each other to make it out alive.

Grand Theft Auto, or GTA for short, is one of the most popular gaming franchises of the century. GTA fans have been waiting more than a decade for a new game in the series, making Thursday’s release even more exciting for them.

open image in gallery Fox News is known to promote the conservative side of culture wars, railing against DEI and trans rights. And now, the network is coming after your favorite video game ( AFP via Getty Images )

Roughly 15 million copies of Ground Theft Auto VI have been preordered, CNN Business reported, citing Sensor Tower data.

Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of GTA’s publisher, Take-Two Interactive, told Variety that presales of the new game are “running far in excess of our expectations.”

Violent games like GTA, Call of Duty and Mortal Kombat have faced scrutiny over the years for potentially leading to bad behavior in players, such as aggression.

But a study published in Molecular Psychiatry in 2018 found no changes in behavior between participants who played Grand Theft Auto V, the non-violent video game The Sims 3 and those who played no game at all.

News.title: Is Wales v Portugal on TV? Channel, kick-off time and how to watch Nations League decider
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Wales bid to salvage some pride in the Nations League as they host Portugal in Cardiff.

Craig Bellamy’s team lost 3-1 to Norway on Saturday and will finish bottom of Group A4.

But they are safe from direct relegation and will instead enter the relegation/promotion play-offs in March regardless of tonight’s result.

Portugal are aiming to beat Denmark to top spot, and will be looking to bounce back from their shock 4-2 defeat to the Danes on Saturday.

Portugal were playing for the first time since the retirement of their record goalscorer and former captain Cristiano Ronaldo.

Here’s everything you need to know

Is Wales v Portugal on TV?

News.title: US urges Ukraine backers to prioritize front-line gear, warns deep strikes are not working
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Pentagon on Tuesday urged Ukraine’s Western backers to focus their military support on equipment used for front-line combat and warned that Kyiv’s deep strikes into Russia are counterproductive.

Ukraine’s cutting-edge drone capabilities developed since Russian President Vladimir Putin launched his full-scale invasion in 2022 have allowed it to hit oil facilities and other installations right across Russia.

U.S. President Donald Trump has demanded that Ukraine halt strikes on Russian oil refineries and infrastructure used to produce and distribute diesel, saying the attacks are causing a global shortage.

At NATO headquarters Tuesday, U.S. Undersecretary of Defense Elbridge Colby said that deep strikes “have not been effective in driving an end to the war, nor do they contribute to blunting Russia’s advances on the front line.”

He said that “such strikes, especially those that target civilian infrastructure such as Wildberries, have actually probably hardened the Russian public’s resolve and Kremlin’s own willingness to escalate.”

Earlier this year, Ukraine’s armed forces delivered repeated blows to Wildberries, Russia’s biggest online retailer. The size and commercial importance of the e-commerce giant have seen it compared to Amazon.

Ukraine says goods sold by the company include equipment and technical components that are used by the Russian military, which the company denies. The attacks have unsettled Russians living far from the front and hurt small businesses.

Speaking at a meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group, which meets to drum up arms and ammunition, Colby said Ukraine’s army is “very effective” when it focuses on front line fighting, using drones to slow Russian advances and hit their supply lines.

Colby said the U.S. believes “that focusing our support on the front lines and on associated midrange strikes is the most effective way to enable Ukraine’s defense and thus to set the conditions for an end to the war.”

Asked later by reporters about restrictions on Ukraine’s use of the Starshield satellite communications system and how they are hindering its ability to intercept Russian drones, Colby declined to comment.

But he followed by saying he had explained to Ukraine’s backers “that we are very focused on supporting Ukraine’s ability to defend itself, and these kind of midrange strikes, and we’re taking steps that are consistent with that policy.” He did not elaborate.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that limitations on Starshield, operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, are costing lives and could weaken defenses around Ukraine’s energy infrastructure as winter approaches.

___
