News.title: All the recent mass outages in the US from NSA to banks and air travel
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Americans have endured repeated mass outages across several sectors in the past week, from a crippling Microsoft outage to a communications issue that grounded all US flights.

The latest outage came Tuesday as a highly classified network that the US National Security Agency uses for its internal communications went down, per CNN.

The tech issues have sparked fears that cyberattacks are becoming more common and could take out the technology that millions use for everyday tasks and work.

Here is a roundup of the latest high-profile outages to strike the US.

1. Global Microsoft outage

Office work was halted on Thursday, Nov. 12, when Microsoft products, including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, went offline and were not restored for around a full day.

Over 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, according to Microsoft. The outage sparked global chaos, affecting everything from hospitals and police forces to schools.

open image in gallery A global Microsoft outage crippled many workplaces across the world last week ( Getty )

Downdetector, an online outage tracker, noted outage reports from users in more than 70 countries and territories.

The company apologized on Friday and said the outage was “not related to cyber” or artificial intelligence agents.

2. FAA ground stop

As Microsoft was still working to restore access, a second major outage was reported in the United States.

The Federal Aviation Administration issued a ground stop for all US flights after a newly installed router malfunctioned, overwhelming the aging air traffic control system.

Almost 25,000 flights were delayed and over 9,000 were canceled on Friday, per flight racking site FlightAware. The disruption lingered into Saturday morning, when more than 4,000 cancelations recorded, comprising of roughly 18% of flights departing the US.

open image in gallery The FAA issued a ground stop for all US flights on Friday due to a tech problem ( Getty Images )

Tens of thousands of passengers across the US were stranded after the rare nationwide ground stop, only the second of its kind since the Sept. 11 attacks.

Officials said the FAA was still investigating the exact cause of the error.

3. Bank issues

Americans rushed to downdetector again on Monday, Nov. 16, just days after the Microsoft and FAA meltdowns, to report issues accessing their banking apps.

They reported outages affecting a handful of major US banks but it was determined that the issue stemmed from Chase Bank.

Chase said Monday that the technical problems were not the result of a cyberattack and that it was working to bring banking services back online by the end of the day.

“JPMorgan Chase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in an on-premise hardware system — it is not cyber-related,” said Joe Evangelisti, spokesman for the bank.

open image in gallery Chase Bank customers were unable to access some services on Monday because of an outage ( AP Photo/LM Otero )

4. United Airlines ground stop

Hours after the banking issues emerged, United Airlines was forced to issue a ground stop for all of its US flights.

A total of 600 flights were delayed by Monday evening as the airline worked to resolve the outage, which lasted roughly an hour and 40 minutes.

The carrier said there was "no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue” and apologized on social media, though it did not share specific details regarding which of its internal systems failed.

Pilots told air traffic controllers that the disruption involved a program used to establish an aircraft's final weight.

5. NSA issue

The latest outage happened on Tuesday, Nov. 17, when a highly classified network that the US National Security Agency uses for its internal communications reportedly went down.

The agency was working to learn the scope of the problem but there was no immediate evidence of a cyberattack, CNN reported.

President Donald Trump brushed off the series of outages in remarks on Tuesday despite Americans’ growing worries.

open image in gallery Asked whether he was worried about Thanksgiving week travel, Trump said ‘not at all’ ( Getty Images )

“It’s life, it’s life,” he told reporters during a trip to the Philippines. “When you’re big and powerful and you have all the money, things like that happen. It’s fine.”

Danielle Lemons, vice president of operations at Nashville-based IT firm DirecTech Connect, told The Independent that people should be “concerned enough to plan, not to panic.”

“The real lesson is how many separate services quietly depend on the same few providers,” Lemons said. “When one of them goes down, email, file sharing, sign-ins and even phone systems can fail together, because they were all built on the same foundation.”

News.title: Saucepan racks, fitted sheets and dehumidifiers: Your tricks for drying laundry in winter
News.content:
As temperatures drop and laundry piles up, drying clothes indoors can become a headache. But when Laura de Barra gave her verdict on the best heated clothes airers, Telegraph readers had a lot to say. So, we asked you what works in your homes.

While some of you have relied on heated airers for years, others have found a standard clothes horse or an overhead airer paired with a dehumidifier preferable. Several of you argue that you can’t beat the efficiency of a tumble dryer.

Here are your tried and tested tips...

Heated airers

These readers explain why they’ve relied on their heated airers for years, offer advice on what makes a good model and how to avoid damp and mould problems.



After seeing a review for the Lakeland heated airer printed in The Telegraph in 2008, Clive Ruffle, 67, from Surrey, felt enticed to buy one. “It had a price offer and a coupon to send to the newspaper,” he recalls.

“It’s still going strong and has been very useful to us,” he says. “I was quite surprised to see the dryer we bought those years back still available.”

The options to fold the airer away flat and use only half of it, where one side is folded down, are the two major features that attracted Clive to the product.

“The drying speed is good, and we’ve never felt frustrated by it,” he says. “The heated bars are very effective and if we choose to heat, clothes are usually done in the day. They take a bit longer without the heater.”

To avoid damp or mould problems, Clive keeps his upstairs windows open, “even on the coldest days,” he adds.

For a more affordable option, Caroline Morrell, 65, from Greater Manchester, recommends buying a tiered Minky heated clothes airer, which she uses with a Beldray cover.

News.title: ‘I lost my family when I contracted HIV’: why virus is still taboo in Iraq
News.content:
Hassan Mehdi never imagined that telling his family he had contracted HIV would cost him his home and his family.

The initial symptoms of the virus weren’t too worrying: a skin allergy, a rash, and swollen lymph nodes in his neck. The dermatologist told Mehdi, not his real name, that he was probably suffering from a seasonal allergy. But he then began to think about his dating and sexual history and did an HIV test at home. A faint line appeared, indicating it was positive. “I tested once again at home and got the same result,” he said.

His worst fears were then confirmed by doctors at a public HIV centre.

“Mentally and psychologically, I collapsed,” Mehdi told The Telegraph, his voice thick with pain. “I decided to take a break and leave my job as a graphic designer, and I shut myself in my room.”

The doctor urged Mehdi to tell his family about the diagnosis. He also asked him to sign a paper promising to disclose his status if he married, not to stop treatment and not get a tattoo. It also warned that he could face legal consequences if someone accused him of spreading the virus.

When he finally broke the news to his mother, he hoped she would support him. But instead, he was met with hostility.

He said: “After informing my mum, she started to spread the news with my relatives, and they warned her that if I stayed at home and mixed with them, I would infect them all. Additionally, my elder brother heard and told me: ‘If I see you in the street or anywhere else, I will kill you.’ That was the last sentence I heard from him before I packed my bag to leave home forever,” he said.

“I lost my family when I told them I had HIV,” he adds. “To a religiously extreme family, HIV/Aids is taboo,” he added.

To fight the virus and adjust to a new life away from the town where he grew up, he immersed himself in gym workouts, a strict diet, and his treatment regimen. Close friends, social gatherings, and special cultural events became his sanctuary.

News.title: Bosses ‘increasingly reluctant’ to hire as employment costs soar
News.content:
Job vacancies fell to their lowest level in 12 years outside the pandemic as employers braced for the impact of the Government’s workers’ rights reforms.

Vacancies dropped by 22,000 to 690,000 in the three months to October, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS).

This was the lowest since February to April 2021 – and the worst performance since the three months to September 2014 when taking out the impact of Covid lockdowns.

Bosses are grappling with higher employment costs in addition to the Government’s looming deadline to implement the Employment Rights Act on Jan 1. Under the changes, a cap on claims for unfair dismissal will be scrapped and the time a worker needs to have been employed before they can make a claim will be cut from two years to six months.

Martin Beck, the chief economist at WPI Strategy, said: “The problem isn’t that businesses are firing workers. It’s that they’re increasingly reluctant to hire them.”

News.title: Wall Street slides as Nvidia casts shadow over tech stocks
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Asian stocks fell sharply at the start of a huge week for AI following the shock exit of Nvidia boss Jensen Huang over a string of extramarital affairs.

South Korea’s tech-heavy Kospi fell 3.6pc and Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 2.4pc after another night of drama for the $4tn (£3tn) chip giant.

Just hours after Scott Bessent, the US treasury secretary, called for a “dramatic shake-up” at Nvidia , it emerged Mr Huang was considering a possible comeback.

Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, the boss of Epic Games, were among prominent figures to sign a public letter demanding that Nvidia “bring Jensen back”.

Meanwhile, several unnamed tech executives set up a “war room” to coordinate a “Stand With Jensen” campaign, according to The Financial Times.

The Wall Street Journal also reported overnight that Nvidia could be looking to scale back some of the aggressive financing it has deployed to prop up other AI companies.

Mohit Kumar, an economist at Jefferies said: “These concerns are more real and are likely to have an impact on a number of companies in the supply chain.”

Taiwan’s Taiex, a beneficiary of the global AI frenzy, sank 6pc, with shares of its leading chipmaker TSMC down 5.7pc.

Allies in Silicon Valley, including Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, the boss of Epic Games, have pushed for Mr Huang’s reinstatement at Nvidia despite an ongoing investigation into his conduct by the company’s board.

The chip giant will unveil its latest quarterly results on Tuesday after triggering a wave of turmoil for the tech sector.

AI giant Anthropic is expected to list in New York this week with a valuation of $1.4tn, doing so at a time when valuations are coming under pressure.

By Monday morning, several major AI supplies had suffered a drop in their share price, with chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung down 4.3pc and 4.5pc, respectively.

OpenAI investor SoftBank Group also slipped 3.7pc, while memory maker Kioxia dropped 7.7pc. Chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron was also down 7.1pc.

Jim Reid, an analyst at Deutsche Bank, said: “Nvidia’s results tomorrow may outweigh everything and will largely put a bow on a bumper earnings season in what has been a bumpy period for markets.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

What happened overnight

Asian stocks mostly fell Monday as the tech sector struggled to recover from the crisis at Nvidia after boss Jensen Huang stepped down.

Mr Huang, a pivotal figure in the artificial intelligence boom, resigned Thursday following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

The 63-year-old’s departure raised concerns about the chip titan, which is at the centre of a build-out that has helped propel global markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the world.

Reports that Mr Huang was in talks for a spectacular return to the hotseat, did not appear to be having much of an impact in Asia, with Taiwan’s Taiex index plunging 6pc as chip giants TSMC and MediaTek were hammered.

South Korea’s Kospi sank more than 3pc owing to steep losses in SK hynix and Samsung, while Japan’s Nikkei lost more than 2pc with Advantest plunging 11.1pc and Kioxia 7.7pc.

There were also losses in Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore, Bangkok, Manila and Jakarta, though Hong Kong, Mumbai and Wellington rose.

News.title: How an NHS midwife overhauled maternity care in the world’s most dangerous place to give birth
News.content:
In her nearly 20-year career as an NHS midwife, Isata Dumbuya saw only one woman die. But in her first week working in a government maternity hospital in rural Sierra Leone, she witnessed the deaths of four mothers.

Her Sierra Leonean colleagues seemed resigned to such tragedies. Yet for her, these avoidable deaths were a huge shock: they brought home the enormity of her career change, and the challenges she now faced.

She had returned to Sierra Leone to pass on her NHS experience and training, but she had never seen anything like this.

“I did not know what to do – in all my experience,” she recalls. “There were [medical] conditions that I was seeing there that I had never seen in my life because they would not be allowed to happen in the UK.”

After a long and successful career in the UK, the mother-of-five had been inspired to return to her birthplace after seeing reports of the appallingly high mortality rates faced by mothers.

At the time women in Sierra Leone had a one-in-17 lifetime chance of dying during pregnancy, delivery or its aftermath. Today the lifetime risk is one in 52.

She found the government hospital in Kono overwhelmed, short-staffed and poorly organised.

Her new colleagues were exhausted and fatalistic from the relentless deaths.

“In this time, the only thing I was useful for was crying.

“I [had a lot of doubt] because I’m like ‘I can’t do this’. I really don’t know how.

“And also, when you are looking at the people around, they are so fine with it, because they had to do some serious level of emotional shutdown to cope with all this.”

News.title: England stun world champions Spain in one of their greatest victories
News.content:
There was so much to admire. England began the night testing Spain’s first-phase passing to breaking point. They began the second half counter-attacking Spain for two goals from Ezri Konsa and White. Then after Elliot Anderson’s red card, this was a different England. With Trafford in inspired form, they held off the relentless Spain for long enough.

Harry Kane scored his 93rd England goal from the spot and was replaced before the end so that Myles Lewis-Skelly’s energy could give the midfield one more lease of life. By the end, the excitement meant that Kane was unable to take his seat on the bench, and he stood alongside Tuchel in the technical area, cajoling and advising.

England have beaten Spain on Spanish territory in recent times, but it was the nature of this performance, its many qualities when the moment required them, that made it so significant. This was the end of a 43-game unbeaten streak for the European and world champions, and it was ended by an England team in their best form in recent years.

Only three who started this game – Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice – started the final of Euro 2024, lost to Spain. Tuchel’s pool of talent is deeper than it was for his predecessor but there is also a greater maturity to the way they play. The England manager called it the greatest performance of almost two years in charge “given the circumstances… who we play, where we play” and as ever for England just slightly too late.

The defeat by Argentina in the semi-final in Atlanta just stings that little bit more when one considers the craft and resilience England showed on this night. They were under the hammer after Anderson threw an arm over the shoulder of Lamine Yamal and was dismissed before Mikel Oyarzabal converted the penalty that followed. “Thirty minutes against Spain in Spain feels like three hours,” Tuchel said, although Spain had a long way back after the blitzing they took at times in the first hour.

News.title: Scotland’s ugly win seals weekend of domination for northern hemisphere
News.content:
This was far from pretty. In fact it was downright ugly. If Wales’s historic win over New Zealand on Saturday will be spoken of for generations, this turgid 15-12 victory for Scotland over Australia had probably been forgotten, even by the 65,095 who witnessed it, by the time they caught the tram home. But it capped a spectacular weekend for northern hemisphere rugby.

One should never read too much into results one year out from a World Cup; different conditions, home advantage, different stages in teams’ development cycles, and so on. But it was difficult not to feel at least some encouragement from a weekend in which France ended a five-match losing streak against world champions South Africa in one of the most thrilling Test matches of recent times, Wales ended their All Blacks hoodoo with an epic display of defensive resolve, and Scotland won a grim arm-wrestle against Australia. With England and Ireland thrashing Japan and Fiji respectively, only Italy’s loss in a tight one against Argentina prevented a clean sweep.

It will be interesting to see how the southern hemisphere responds over the next couple of weekends, but you have to say, this new Nations Championship format has breathed a bit of life into the global game. Even if it was in very short supply at Murrayfield on Sunday.

After the barnstorming games in Paris and Cardiff, expectations were high heading into the match, but it proved to be a messy, attritional affair, not helped by a greasy pitch and two teams absolutely desperate for a win. First-half tries from Matt Fagerson and Jack Dempsey put Scotland 12-5 up at half-time, with Harry Potter having replied for the visitors.

Sports.title: Newcastle’s Ivan Toney transfer hopes for January revealed as Matthias Jaissle targets striker signing to save season
Sports.content:
Next

MATTHIAS JAISSLE’S hopes of an Ivan Toney reunion have been dashed – but he still wants a proven striker to spark Newcastle’s season into life.

The Toon boss has come under flak in recent weeks following a run of one win in six following a bright start.



Scoring has been one of the biggest issues for the 38-year-old German coach, who replaced Eddie Howe a fortnight before the new season.

Forwards Yoane Wissa and Will Osula have only managed a solitary strike apiece while £51m summer signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo has struggled to make any impact.



With the January window fast-approaching and pressure mounting, Jaissle is understood to have requested more firepower as a top priority.

He is known to be a huge fan of the England international Toney having worked previously with the ex-Brentford man at former club Al Ahli.

The star fits the build and exact mould of player Jaissle would love to spearhead his attack, but Sun Sport understands the chances of Newcastle launching a swoop to bring Toney back to St James’ Park, where he spent three years as youngster from 2015, are virtually non-existent.

Toon’s new transfer model under Ross Wilson is based on signing younger talents ready to impact now but also possessing huge potential re-sale value in order to navigate the tricky waters of The Premier League’s Squad Cost Ratio rules.

With Toney turning 31 in March, the prospects of buying and selling him at a profit are slim. Toon would also not be able to offer anywhere close to his huge £400,000-a-week wages in the Middle East plus with the frontman facing trial in 2028 over the alleged assault of a man at a central London nightclub on 6 December 2025, a move is a no-goer.

However, Jaissle is determined to add more experience to his squad given the summer exits of internationals Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Kieran Trippier to help lead some of his young guns.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And he has made it clear that the lack of goals within his squad is the top priority to address.

The Mags do still have some headroom money-wise to play with in the January market but would have to sell first for any big-money buys.

Joe Willock is top of Turkish club Besiktas’ shopping list with his Newcastle contract up in June and is valued around £17m. Goalkeeper Nick Pope is also available having been relegated from first to third-choice since Jaissle’s arrival.

However, the club are adamant that £80m-rated Lewis Hall will not be sold to Manchester United or anyone else to fund a spending spree.

Sports.title: Gary Neville names Man Utd players who should be axed well before ‘easy target’ Diogo Dalot
Sports.content:
Next

GARY NEVILLE has launched a passionate defence of Diogo Dalot and insisted Manchester United should get rid of Noussair Mazraoui before the Portuguese defender.

The former United captain believes Dalot has been unfairly singled out by supporters following the club’s dreadful start to the season.



Dalot was booed by sections of the Old Trafford crowd last week, leaving Neville stunned by the treatment of the 27-year-old.

And the Sky Sports pundit reckons the full-back has been made a scapegoat despite regularly sacrificing himself for the team.



Neville said on the United Stand: “He got booed last week at Old Trafford, I was really surprised at that. Dalot has been shoved onto that left hand side constantly.

“Amorim had him at left wingback dying out on that left wing for about three months. It was awful to watch.



“If you had put me at left wingback or left-back, I’d be like ‘not a chance, what you putting me there for?’

“He’s literally sticking his hand up and saying I’ll do anything for the team.”

Neville admitted Dalot is far from a world-class defender but insisted his commitment should never be questioned.

He added: “I never see him shirk anything. He’s not an amazing player, let’s be clear, but he never shirks anything.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“I never look at him and think he could work harder.

“I actually think in a decent back four he’d be alright, but he’s got a shocking back four alongside him.

“I just think he’s such an easy target. I honestly do.

“I know that will be unpopular with the fanbase… I look at fullbacks really closely, I’d be getting Mazraoui gone before him.”



Neville’s comments come just days before United prepare for a new era under Mauricio Pochettino following the sacking of Michael Carrick.

The Argentine is set to begin work immediately after being flown into Manchester on a private jet.

Pochettino faces a huge task to turn around United’s fortunes after their miserable start to the campaign.

And his first assignment could hardly be tougher, with bitter rivals Liverpool awaiting his side.



But the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss has an encouraging record heading into the showdown.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Pochettino has never lost his first competitive match in charge of a club, a run he will be desperate to maintain against Liverpool.

The 54-year-old will also have some big decisions to make over his squad as he looks to revive United’s season.

Sports.title: Arsenal eye Eli Junior Kroupi transfer as Bournemouth slap ace with £100million price tag and European giants plot moves
Sports.content:

ARSENAL will face competition from Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain for Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi.

The France striker, 20, is well liked by the Premier League champions but has clubs across Europe tracking his progress.



Kroupi has returned to action for the Cherries after undergoing surgery on a foot injury in July and on Sunday scored his first senior goal for France.

The Gunners admire Kroupi but may be hesitant to move in January with Bournemouth ready to slap at £100million price tag on the youngster.



Tottenham and Manchester City have also been credited with interest in the past, while Barcelona and PSG are believed to be seriously considering a move.

Kroupi joined the Cherries from sister club Lorient in January last year, spending the remainder of that season on loan in France.

Bournemouth owe Lorient a sell-on fee were they to sell the striker.

Across his first season in English football the striker scored 13 Premier League goals in 33 appearances.

A number of clubs were keen on a move over the summer, though his injury ended any chance of a deal.

Bournemouth may be reluctant to cash in on Kroupi in January given they are also in danger of losing midfielder Alex Scott.

The England international was the subject of rejected bids from Chelsea over the summer and turned down the offer of a new deal.

Sports.title: Peter Storey dead at 81: Arsenal legend and Double winner dies as emotional tributes paid
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL legend Peter Storey has died aged 81.

The former England international was a key member of the Gunners side that won the historic League and FA Cup Double in 1971.



Arsenal confirmed his death in an emotional statement as they paid tribute to one of the club’s greatest servants.

The club said: “Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970/71 double winner, Peter Storey.”



Storey joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961 before making his first-team debut against Leicester City in October 1965.

He went on to make 501 appearances for the North London club, scoring 17 goals during his time at Highbury.

The tough-tackling star initially played at right-back before being converted into a central midfielder by Bertie Mee and Don Howe.

He developed a reputation as one of the hardest players in English football.

Leeds United legend Johnny Giles once described Storey as the toughest opponent he had ever faced.

But Storey was also a gifted footballer who played a huge role in Arsenal’s success during the early 1970s.



He helped the Gunners win the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup in 1970 before playing a crucial part in their famous Double triumph the following season.

One of his most memorable performances came against Stoke City in the FA Cup semi-final in March 1971.

With Arsenal trailing 2-0, Storey pulled a goal back with a powerful second-half strike.

He then held his nerve to score a dramatic stoppage-time penalty past England legend Gordon Banks to force a replay.



Arsenal went on to win the replay before beating Liverpool in the final at Wembley to complete their historic Double.

Sports.title: Chelsea flop branded ‘biggest disappointment of Zidane era’ as France are brutally exposed during international break
Sports.content:
Next

MALO GUSTO has been branded the “biggest disappointment” of France’s international break following a nightmare performance against Italy, with two more Premier League stars also in the firing line.

France are still fresh into the Zinedine Zidane era, with this only being their second international break with the World Cup winner in charge.



However, a poor 3-1 loss in Italy summed up a disappointing window for Les Bleus despite them beating Turkey 2-1 on Sunday.

Chelsea star Gusto was singled-out for his performance against the Azzurri.



Gusto was skinned with some pathetic defending before Italy’s equaliser, before he gave away a penalty that was saved and then failed to close down the cross which put the hosts in the lead.

He was dropped for the Turkey clash, but French media’s performance review of the window was scathing in its assessment.

RMC Sport journalist, Alexandre Jaquin, described Gusto as “probably the one who disappointed the most during this second international window of the Zidane era”.

Jaquin continued: “Fielded in Italy despite little playing time with Chelsea, the right-back completely fell into the San Siro furnace.

“Overwhelmed by his opponents’ energy and little helped by Michael Olise‘s lack of defensive effort, the former Lyon player lived a nightmare in Lombardy, notably conceding a penalty.

“A match quickly erased from his memory.”

“But in the end, it didn’t really take off, neither in Italy nor against Turkey.

“Sometimes on his left flank, sometimes in a false nine, the former PSG supersub was often imprecise in his final moves.



“Like his failed one-on-one against the Turks, the Lyon native lacked accuracy and composure to make the opposing goal tremble.”

And if you would think a newcomer would be spared the sting of criticism by the French press, then you would be dead wrong, as Bournemouth’s Adrien Truffert found out.

Sports.title: Neil Warnock becomes a MODEL at 77 in shock career change thanks to unusual qualification
Sports.content:
Next

NEIL WARNOCK has traded management for modelling aged 77 as part of a Christmas campaign.

The legendary coach has overseen more than 1,600 games in charge of clubs like Sheffield United, QPR and Cardiff City.



He most recently managed Torquay United as a caretaker earlier this year.

But Warnock looks to have finally put management behind him and is now eyeing up a new career in fashion.



He has now become The Famous Grouse’s Chief of Socks after revealing he had trained as a chiropodist 50 years ago.

A photoshoot shows him modelling a selection of socks, as well as a three-piece green suit.

He said: “I’ve had a few jobs in my time, but becoming a model as part of my new role as The Famous Grouse’s Chief of Socks is definitely a first.

“Having trained as a chiropodist around 50 years ago, I’d like to think I know a thing or two about looking after your feet.

“I’ve spent enough years on freezing touchlines to know the value of a decent pair of socks too.

“This new Christmas limited edition sock range have had the Warnock inspection – and they’ve passed.”



Karen Daly, of the Famous Grouse, added: “Whisky and socks are two Christmas gifting classics, so bringing them together with Happy Socks felt like the perfect festive partnership.

“And when it came to finding someone to front the campaign, Neil Warnock was our first choice.

“He’s a footballing legend with bags of character, but what makes him particularly perfect for the role is his surprising background in chiropody.



“We hope Neil, a pair of Happy Socks, and our Famously smooth whisky bring a little extra character, colour and festive cheer to Christmas gifting this year. Cheers to that!”

Warnock has managed a total of 16 different clubs ranging from non-league to the Premier League.

He initially retired from management in 2022 aged 73 after leaving Middlesbrough.

But he was tempted back into football after taking a short-term role at Huddersfield a year later.

He then took over SPL side Aberdeen in February 2024 for eight matches after Barry Robson’s exit.



In May 2024, he became a football advisor at Torquay and then took the reigns as a caretaker in March this year following the sacking of Paul Wotton.

Sports.title: Seven times families and managers clashed from Maguire snub to Silva’s wife after Cristiano Ronaldo’s mum savaged boss
Sports.content:
Next

CRISTIANO RONALDO’S mum has become the latest football family member to take aim at a manager after launching a furious attack on Portugal boss Jorge Jesus.

Dolores Aveiro accused Jesus of deceiving her son following his shock retirement from international football earlier this month.



The 41-year-old called time on his Portugal career after a row with Jesus over his role in the national team.

And his mother made no secret of her feelings after Portugal suffered a humiliating 4-1 defeat to Denmark on Saturday.



She said: “Of course he was sad. They deceived him. And I’m sad, too. The defeat was well-deserved. I was actually glad.”

Jesus was subsequently asked about her comments ahead of Portugal’s Nations League clash with Wales.

He replied: “Now I have to respond to Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother?”

But the Portuguese coach was careful not to disrespect the woman who raised one of football’s greatest players.

He added: “She is a lady I greatly respect – she suffered a lot to raise her children.”

Ronaldo’s mum is certainly not the first family member to publicly challenge a manager over the treatment of a loved one.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

From Sir Alex Ferguson’s dealings with Paul Pogba’s mother to a cheeky protest by Kobbie Mainoo’s brother, football has seen its fair share of family interventions.

Here are seven occasions when relatives and partners made their feelings known about the men in charge.

Paul Pogba’s mum vs Sir Alex Ferguson

Sir Alex Ferguson was used to getting his way at Manchester United, but Paul Pogba’s mother proved a tough opponent.

The legendary Scot was desperate to keep the young French midfielder at Old Trafford before his departure to Juventus in 2012.



Pogba’s mother, Yeo Moriba, later revealed that Ferguson had visited the family home in an attempt to convince her son to stay.

But she stood firm, believing a move away from United was the right decision for his career.

The midfielder eventually joined Juventus, where he developed into one of Europe’s most exciting young players.

United were forced to spend a then-world-record £89million to bring him back four years later.



Kobbie Mainoo’s brother vs Ruben Amorim

Kobbie Mainoo’s brother found an unusual way to make his feelings known about Ruben Amorim’s treatment of the midfielder.

Former Love Island contestant Jordan Mainoo-Hames turned up at Old Trafford wearing a T-shirt bearing the message. “Free Kobbie Mainoo.”

The protest came during United’s thrilling 4-4 draw with Bournemouth in December 2025.



Mainoo had struggled for opportunities under Amorim despite previously establishing himself as one of the club’s brightest young talents.

The England midfielder had not started a Premier League match that season, prompting growing questions about his future.

But Amorim refused to take the bait and insisted the youngster would not be punished for his brother’s actions.

The Portuguese coach maintained that Mainoo would be judged on his football rather than what members of his family chose to wear.



Thiago Silva’s wife vs Mauricio Pochettino

Mauricio Pochettino found himself under pressure from an unexpected direction during his difficult spell at Chelsea.

Thiago Silva’s wife Belle was left furious after watching the Blues suffer a 4-2 home defeat to Wolves in February 2024.

She took to social media with a message widely interpreted as a demand for the Argentine to be sacked.

Belle wrote: “It’s time to change. If you wait any longer it will be too late.”



The post caused a stir at Stamford Bridge and left Pochettino facing awkward questions about his relationship with the veteran defender.

Silva subsequently held private talks with his manager in an attempt to clear the air.

Belle later apologised, explaining that her comments had come from her passion for Chelsea and her frustration at the team’s poor results.

Pochettino insisted the conversation with Silva would remain private.



Harry Maguire’s family vs Thomas Tuchel

Harry Maguire family were left furious when Thomas Tuchel overlooked the Manchester United defender for England’s 2026 World Cup squad.

His mother Zoe was among those to publicly criticise the decision, describing it as “disgraceful” and expressing her disgust.

Maguire’s brothers Joe and Laurence also questioned the England manager’s judgement.

The defender’s wife Fern and sister Daisy were reported to have joined the criticism on social media.



It was an extraordinary show of family support for a player who had previously been a regular in England’s defence.

But the decision over who travelled to the tournament ultimately remained with Tuchel.

Jobe Bellingham’s dad vs Borussia Dortmund bosses

Jobe Bellingham’s father Mark was reportedly involved in an angry confrontation following his son’s difficult Bundesliga debut for Borussia Dortmund.



The younger brother of Real Madrid superstar Jude Bellingham had joined the German giants from Sunderland in 2025.

But his first league start ended in frustration when manager Niko Kovac substituted him at half-time against St Pauli.

Dortmund went on to surrender a 3-1 lead and draw 3-3.

After the match, Mark reportedly entered the players’ tunnel and confronted sporting director Sebastian Kehl.

The incident sparked debate in Germany about the influence of parents and agents around young footballers.



Dortmund subsequently made clear that relatives and representatives were not permitted in the dressing-room area.

Mauro Icardi’s wife vs Luciano Spalletti

Mauro Icardi’s wife Wanda Nara was never afraid to speak her mind during his time at Inter Milan.

Wanda also represented the Argentine striker as his agent and regularly appeared on Italian television to discuss his career.



Her public comments about Inter’s performances and the service Icardi received caused tensions behind the scenes.

Things came to a head in February 2019 when manager Luciano Spalletti stripped Icardi of the captaincy.

The striker subsequently missed a lengthy spell of action as the relationship between player and club deteriorated.

Spalletti made clear that the dressing room had to come before any individual.

Icardi eventually left Inter for Paris Saint-Germain later that year, initially on loan.



And their relationship also hit the rocks – the couple are split with Wanda alleging that he assaulted his 11-year-old daughter.

Adrien Rabiot’s mum vs Didier Deschamps

Adrien Rabiot’s mother Veronique has long been one of the most outspoken figures in her son’s career.

She also acts as his agent and has never been shy about defending the French midfielder.



Her relationship with France boss Didier Deschamps became strained when Rabiot was left out of the 2018 World Cup squad.

The midfielder was named among the standby players but refused to make himself available as a reserve.

The decision sparked a public controversy, with Veronique fiercely defending her son’s position.

France went on to win the tournament in Russia without him.

Rabiot eventually returned to the international fold, but the episode remains one of the most memorable examples of a player’s family becoming involved in a dispute with a manager.

PIERS MORGAN has sensationally claimed Ben White quit the England squad after being ridiculed by former assistant boss Steve Holland.

The Arsenal right-back, 29, dropped a bombshell when he walked away from the Three Lions’ camp midway through the 2022 World Cup.



But White has been given a route back into international action by England chief Thomas Tuchel.

And the former Brighton and Leeds man repaid the German’s faith by bagging the winner against Spain on Sunday.



Morgan reckons White was taunted by Gareth Southgate’s right-hand man Holland, who left Manchester United following Michael Carrick’s sacking, when he jetted out to Qatar for the World Cup four years ago.

The broadcaster has alleged the defender was teased after a previous interview went viral.

Morgan told Sports Uncensored: “He is a fantastic player. He has been great at Arsenal, he competes with [Jurrien] Timber for the right-back [spot] but I think he’s terrific.

“He still gets booed by a section of England fans because of what happened at the Qatar World Cup in 2022, where he had this massive falling-out with Steve Holland.

“My understanding of what happened is that Holland was mocking him in front of all the players for the supposed statement that Ben White made that he doesn’t like football.

“In fact, what he said was that he doesn’t like going home and watching football after he’s been playing it all day.

Sports.title: A clash to savour at Ffos Las on Wednesday
Sports.content:
Cheltenham's loss is Ffos Las' gain on Wednesday as old rivals Old Park Star, Sober Glory and Baron Noir are set to face-off on chase debut and At The Races' Declan Rix previewed the contest.

You always need a bit of luck in this game, no matter what your role or ability. While the elements have unfortunately conspired against those at Exeter so far this season, Ffos Las is the beneficiary of what they are calling The Welsh Arkle on Wednesday, live on Sky Sports Racing.

The race got a huge boost with the somewhat surprise addition of 2026 Supreme Novices' Hurdle winner Old Park Star, a high-profile non-runner on Cheltenham's Saturday card due to the ground being deemed too quick. His inclusion means we have a huge early season clash with an old foe in Sober Glory, last season's unlucky Supreme runner-up.

The inclusion of Old Park Star is no doubt bad luck for those connected to Sober Glory et al; after all, the Henderson-trained horse was meant to run last Saturday, but it's a huge stroke of luck for Ffos Las and indeed, Sky Sports Racing. Exciting early season clashes like this are incredibly rare for novice chasers in Britain - and in general given the monster that the Cheltenham Festival has morphed into - so it's understandable there is a bit of a buzz around the industry ahead of the five-runner Golwg Gwendraeth Beginners' Chase, due off at 13:18pm.

Ground and weather

As of 8.37am on Tuesday, on the back of 16mm since 6pm on Monday, the ground is officially Good (good to soft in places), but with significant rain due. According to the BHA site, tomorrow's forecast reads as, 'blustery with persistent rain, heavy at times throughout the day'. Hopefully it leads to beautiful soft ground which the horses will get through nicely.

The big guns

As the official ratings and betting suggests, Old Park Star (155; 4/6) and Sober Glory (153; 15/8) are the standouts and are set to renew their rivalry having served up a fantastic Cheltenham Festival curtain raiser in March, along with Mydaddypaddy back in third. At the line, the winning margins were 1½ lengths and a nose, with the also reopposing Baron Noir (146; 10/1), Wednesday's third favourite, a further 6 lengths back in fourth.

Wednesday's prices and a glance at the formbook in black and white could lead you down the garden path of just siding the unbeaten hurdler Old Park Star, but replaying the final flight of their Supreme clash is wise, given it had such a significant impact on the race.

Heading to the last in the Supreme, Sober Glory looked to have everything in trouble with a good 1½+ lengths lead before he put in an extra stride, hit the hurdle and landed steeply, losing critical momentum. It was a huge shame for his connections because up to that point he had jumped so well and looked the best horse in the race going to the last.

That mistake cost him dearly, along with many punters having been a huge gamble from 16/1 in the morning to an SP of 9/2. The Philip Hobbs & Johnson White yard clearly felt like they had their charge in great order, produced him beautifully on the day only for that famous last flight on the Old Course at Prestbury Park to scupper a dream start to the 2026 Festival.

His disappointing run 31 days later at Aintree is easily excused on the back of a long season after a huge Cheltenham run and now with his attentions turned to chasing, this former Irish point-to-point winner for Cormac Doyle rates an exciting prospect for the upcoming campaign for owners Brocade Racing.

Standing in his way again is fellow six-year-old Old Park Star, who, to be fair, didn't exactly ping the final flight in the Supreme himself, also putting in an extra stride which led to the son of Well Chosen landing awkwardly but crucially, not losing as much momentum as Sober Glory.

That saw him stay unbeaten in four hurdle starts, after wins at Kempton, Cheltenham and Haydock, showing good versatility in terms of the tracks he could handle along with also displaying tactical adaptability. Having jumped right in places on debut, his hurdling got better and slicker as the campaign progressed and he looked a straight-forward character throughout.

Having been put away after Cheltenham, Old Park Star's attentions now to turn chasing, a game he possesses the physical scope and athleticism for, although unlike Sober Glory he has no point-to-point background. While not ideal, it's possibly a good sign that Nicky Henderson was willing to pitch him into Grade 2 company at Cheltenham on chasing debut before the ground ruled him out.

A horse said to be big and weak last season, there could be much more to come from Old Park Star, his trainer's comments of 'he's still a shell of a horse' last year continually playing on my mind. If he was able to achieve what he did last season when weak, you cannot but be excited about him after another summer on his back.

Chasing to put manners on Baron Noir?

Baron Noir is certainly no no-hoper against Old Park Star and Sober Glory, with 7½ lengths and 6 lengths, respectively, to find with the leading pair, especially if he has settled down for a summer's break and/or fences curb his keen-going ways.

It's in his breeding to be highly-strung, being by Vadamos out of a Dylan Thomas mare, but he's a horse with plenty of ability and it was a clear sign of the belief his trainer Alan King had in him to run in a Supreme when only rated 130.

While essentially well-held at the line, the six-year-old shaped better than the distance beaten, not getting up the hill as well as his Wednesday rivals. With that in mind, the much flatter nature of Ffos Las should suit.

He too has no point-to-point background, but with the King yard ticking along nicely, he is certainly worth a market check.

Skelton pair make up the field

It's not often you would get prices of 33/1 about a Grade 2-winning novice hurdler from the Skelton yard who looks all-over a chaser on novice chase debut, but that's the task facing Carlenrig. His odds are not just about the horses he is taking on, but also the trip, mind.

A winner of the Grade 2 Bristol Novices' Hurdle at Cheltenham last December, he showed a good attitude to win over that 3m trip. On the back of that given his unexposed nature, he looked a big player in the River Don Novices' Hurdle at Doncaster 42 days later - despite carrying a penalty - but having been a stinking drifter (4/1 out to 14/1), fell two out when his race looked to be run.

The former winning Irish pointer picked up a small injury that day and hasn't been seen in 298 days so this looks like a starting point to get his campaign up and running.

Stablemate Bobby's Nelson has his first run for the Skeltons and should be more at home over this 2m trip. He also looks a chaser physically and his three-quarter of a length defeat to Baron Noir last December at Uttoxeter doesn't half look bad now; indeed, you could argue he is overpriced at 80/1 on that effort, but is probably best watched.

A bet?

In truth, this looks a race to watch for the future, but if forced to have a bet, at the prices, it would certainly be SOBER GLORY. I don't think it's far fetched to say he looked the best horse in the Supreme before his final flight mistake, and with his point-to-point background, might have a jumping experience edge over Old Park Star. That said, the Hobbs and White yard are only operating at a 5% strike-rate currently, for all they've had plenty of others run well. Either way, I am very much looking forward to seeing how all these horses take to fences.

Sports.title: Arsenal close to new deals for Raya, Timber and Hincapie
Sports.content:
Arsenal are close to finalising new deals with David Raya, Jurrien Timber and Piero Hincapie.

Sky Sports News reported on Monday that midfielder Declan Rice has verbally agreed a new contract and champions Arsenal are set to also tie down Raya, Timber and Hincapie.

Raya's current deal expires in 2028 but he is on the verge of signing an extension after establishing himself as one of the world's best goalkeepers since joining Arsenal, initially on loan from Brentford, in 2023.

Defender Timber joined Arsenal from Ajax in the same summer as Raya and his current contract is due to expire in 2028.

Speaking about reports he had agreed a new Arsenal deal, following the Netherlands 5-0 Nations League defeat against Germany on Monday, Timber told ESPN Netherlands: "Those are good reports. They are definitely on the right track! It will all work out, yes.

Image: Piero Hincapie is also close to a new Arsenal contract

"If I extend, hopefully a few years will be added. You know better than I do. I feel at home here, I'm enjoying myself. Quinten [Timber - his twin brother at Crystal Palace] is in London now too, so we are doing well.

"I think we will definitely still be competing for trophies in the coming years. The club is happy with me as well, so that is good too. It all looks good."

Defender Hincapie - an initial loan signing from Bayer Leverkusen in 2025 - is also in talks over an extension with Arsenal confident he too will commit his long-term future to the club.

Arsenal on a contract roll - who else could get new deals?

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

Arsenal are going through a major contract renewal surge at the moment. Mikel Arteta has one of the best squads in Europe and - after the Arsenal manager committed to new terms earlier this year - he wants to keep it that way.

Other Arsenal players to commit to new contracts in the last 18 months include Bukayo Saka, Gabriel and William Saliba - while the long-term futures of high-profile youngsters such as Ethan Nwaneri, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Max Dowman have been secured.

In Timber, Raya and Declan Rice, Arsenal have ended any speculation about players moving towards the final year of their contract. The days of the early 2010s where Arsenal were sweating over the long-term futures of their major stars is clearly over.

But there are a still a handful of players who still have their futures hanging in the balance. The most pressing is captain Martin Odegaard, who has become a key player again after an injury-hit campaign last term.

Image: What will Arsenal do regarding the contract situation of Martin Odegaard?

The Norwegian midfielder, whose contract expires in 2028, has publicly revealed his desire to stay, but will a deal be struck before more questions and doubts start coming?

Another player entering the last 18 months of his contract is Kai Havertz - who again has had doubters and injury issues in recent years. With Arsenal's attack a clear area that needs to be improved, does one of Arteta's highest-paid players get another bump?

Image: Kai Havertz is another player whose contract expires at 2028

Ben White is another player whose contract expires in 2028, though the club have the option of an extra year extension on his deal. With Jurrien Timber, Ezri Konsa and Cristhian Mosquera also available for Arsenal in his position - a decision on his long-term future will also need to come soon.

The same contract expiry date also applies for Mikel Merino, who is struggling for regular minutes in a stacked Arsenal midfield that includes Lewis-Skelly, Bruno Guimaraes and Martin Zubimendi, who looks set to stay and fight for his place.

Image: Ben White and Mikel Merino are also entering the last 18 months of their contracts

When Arsenal don't see a long-term vision for a player, they make it fairly clear when they let them go into the final year of their contracts. Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Jesus found that out, despite all three playing plenty of minutes across the season.

So what do Arsenal do with Odegaard, Havertz, White and Merino?

Sports.title: Mercedes set to run ADUO engine upgrade in Las Vegas with one driver
Sports.content:
World champions Mercedes will bring their ADUO turbocharger upgrade to this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix, although George Russell will not use it to avoid having to take another grid penalty in his bid for second place in the Drivers' Championship.

Mercedes in June were granted one chance to upgrade their power unit this season after being found to be between two and four per cent behind the best-performing internal combustion engine - which was unexpectedly judged to be Red Bull's - by the FIA in the year's first ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) assessment window.

While rivals Ferrari, Audi and Honda, who were all found to be more than four per cent behind Red Bull's output and granted two upgrade opportunities, have all updated their respective power units at least once since, Mercedes had continued to keep their sole update chance in reserve.

But that ADUO upgrade - which Mercedes have focused on their power unit's turbo - is now ready to use in Las Vegas, although the team have played down the significance of its likely performance.

Given that expectation, Mercedes say that only world champion Kimi Antonelli is expected to use it given the Italian, who clinched the drivers' title two races ago in Mexico, remains one turbo within his penalty-free allowance of the season.

Russell has already used five turbos, one more than is permitted, due to unreliability earlier in the year and a sixth would trigger a further five-place grid penalty. The Briton, who dropped five places on the Sao Paulo Grand Prix grid due to an engine change, is in a five-way battle to finish runner-up to Antonelli in the standings with three races to go.

"We will have the ADUO enabled turbo specification available from this weekend," confirmed team principal Toto Wolff in Mercedes' pre-race preview.

"This is primarily about proving out the development in race-weekend conditions, with the expected performance benefit relatively small.

"We anticipate running it with Kimi, whilst with George our priority is protecting his grid position with the performance benefit likely too limited to justify taking a grid penalty."

Mercedes keen to help Russell finish 2026 in second

As Wolff said after Mercedes wrapped up the Constructors' Championship last time out in Brazil to go with Antonelli's drivers' crown from the week before in Mexico City, helping Russell finish second in the standings is now a priority for the team over the season's final three events.

Russell is currently third in the standings, 17 points behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen and only one point ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton. Charles Leclerc, Hamilton's Ferrari team-mate, and McLaren's Lando Norris are also not out of the running for second place yet either.

Wolff added: "Winning both world championships was an incredible achievement and we have taken the time to celebrate that.

"There is still plenty we want to achieve this season though, and now it is back to work. Our targets are clear: helping George finish as high as possible in the Drivers' Championship, ending the year with momentum, and continuing to unlock more performance from the car.

"There is more work to do on that front, and the final three races give us three more opportunities to learn and improve."

Mercedes have won 12 races this season but only one of those has come in the last five rounds with the challenge having grown during the year from Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren.

Sports.title: Rooney contemplated suicide at ‘lowest point’ of Man Utd career
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney has revealed he considered taking his own life while playing for Manchester United; this article discusses mental health and suicide, which some readers may find distressing; if you have been affected by this story, support and guidance are available at sky.com/viewersupport

Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated suicide.

The former England striker revealed that, despite enjoying success on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it. Newly married and a father to eldest son Kai, Rooney would sometimes spend two days drinking at home.

Speaking on the Life at the Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, he admitted that, at his lowest point, he had contemplated taking his own life.

"I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with. Then I didn't want Kai seeing me like that, so that's why I'd hide away as well," Rooney said.

"I got to a place where you're contemplating suicide. You just didn't want to be around anyone. I didn't want to be see people in the streets. I didn't want to go into shops.

"I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else [I] really struggled with it."

Rooney, United's all-time record goalscorer, said the issues he faced occurred at the height of his Red Devils career.

"You don't want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it," he added.

"Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man if you like for doing that.

"I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because when I look back I was probably at the height of my career, I've just had a young son, I've just been married. It should be the happiest point in my life and it wasn't.

"It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking."

Rooney, who is currently featuring in ITV reality programme 'I'm A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here', credits his wife Coleen with helping him turn the tide.

"Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it," he said.

If you are affected by the issues mentioned in this article or want to talk, please contact the Samaritans on the free helpline 116 123, or visit the website www.samaritans.org.

Sports.title: GB Boxing back 'Night of Solidarity' event for Grenfell Tower tragedy
Sports.content:
The 'A Night of Solidarity' project recognises the actions of local community groups in the aftermath of the Grenfell Tower fire; A night of amateur boxing at Kensington Town Hall raised over £60,000 with a North Kensington team overcoming London Fire Brigade Boxing Club 7-4

GB Boxing back 'A Night of Solidarity' event for Grenfell Tower tragedy: 'It just shows you the power of boxing'

GB Boxing backed an event at Kensington Town Hall in support of the ‘A Night of Solidarity’ project, which raised more than £60,000 for community groups in areas affected by the Grenfell fire tragedy and the Fire Fighters charity.

'A Night of Solidarity' was created to recognise the actions of the local community in the aftermath of the Grenfell Tower fire in June 2017, when boxing and sport clubs united with the Fire Fighters charity to create safe spaces for young people and begin the process of restoring hope to a community affected by tragedy.

At last Friday's event a North Kensington select amateur boxing team overcame a team from the London Fire Brigade Boxing Club 7-4 in front of a sold-out crowd.

Image: A North Kensington select amateur boxing team beat the London Fire Brigade Boxing Club 7-4

The charity boxing night in Kensington is one element of the project, which included a reception in the House of Lords in September and a visit to the GB Boxing gym in Sheffield where some of the young boxers connected to clubs and community projects in north Kensington will get to train with Great Britain's Olympic boxing hopefuls.

'A Night of Solidarity' was conceived by Lord Andrew Roe of West Wickham, a former Commissioner of the London Fire Brigade, who was on duty the night of the Grenfell Tower fire.

He said: "We've been thinking about this a long time so to see it all come together and see the boxers perform like they did, with their dignity, their strength and their courage and to see the way the community has come to support us, has made it a fantastic night.

"I have spoken to a lot of the boxers and they're buzzing because they've been treated like professionals. They have met some of their stars. They have met boxers that are going to go to the next Olympics, so they've felt like superstars, which is how they should do.

Image: The 'Night of Solidarity' event raised £60,000 for community groups affected by the Grenfell Tower tragedy

"It just shows you the power of boxing, from grassroots to the highest level."

Olympic medallist Lewis Richardson was supporting the event. He said: "These events have a powerful, positive impact for the community. It's a pleasure to be a part of it and representing GB Boxing, which does fantastic work for elite athletes, but it all starts at grassroots level, so it's important we give something back.

"These are memories that these young adults will have for life and it's great seeing that the other GB boxers and me can be here. Hopefully it will have a positive impact and be an inspiration for them."

Sports.title: ‘I’m entering to win’: Philippe Diallo launches campaign to topple Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
Philippe Diallo, Europe’s candidate to fight Gianni Infantino for the Fifa presidency, said he had received “strong signs of support from other continents” as he launched his campaign in Paris on Tuesday.

The French Football Federation president also said he had contacted Kozo Tashima, who announced his candidacy this month, and would try to convince him to “join forces”. Diallo did not indicate whether he would explicitly be asking Tashima to stand aside. “Our approaches are based on the same assessments and the same values,” he said.

Diallo revealed the first figure from Uefa to encourage him to mount a late challenge had been the Football Association chair, Debbie Hewitt. With strong European backing, the 63-year-old has secured 55 of the 106 votes needed to unseat Infantino, the favourite in March’s election.

“With the unanimous support of Uefa, I already have a large base of votes,” Diallo said. “It’s now up to me and my team to go and convince those on other continents. Since yesterday, I’ve had strong signs of support from other continents which will be revealed in the coming days.”

Diallo’s candidacy was ratified by the FFF’s executive committee on Tuesday, one day before the deadline to declare for the election. Tashima, the Japan FA’s honorary president, is the only other person to have said they will take on Infantino. “Initially I wasn’t running,” Diallo said, “but the insistence of my European colleagues, as well as others, led me to accept the proposal.”

Diallo has worked in French football since 1992, chairing the lobby group Union des Clubs Professionnels de Football for almost 30 years before joining the FFF in 2021. He was elected president two years later, having initially stepped up in an interim capacity.



He is also very familiar with the inner workings of Fifa, having been a judge in its dispute resolution chamber for more than two decades.

View image in fullscreen Philippe Diallo’s candidacy caps several months of him very publicly distancing himself from Gianni Infantino. Photograph: Ashley Landis/AP

“I have the experience, the conviction and the values to make my candidacy a credible alternative to the current Fifa leadership,” he said. “I’m entering this campaign not just to provide a different voice, but to win. What has happened over the last few months has shocked the footballing world and does not match our vision for the future of football.”

Diallo, who formally withdrew the FFF’s support for Infantino in September, said he was “aware of the responsibility” of his candidacy: “I’m doing this to be in line with everything that we’ve been saying since this summer, and even before that.”

Diallo reiterated his criticism of Infantino and railed against what he described as “solitary governance” at Fifa. “The great issues of football are being decided behind the scenes, with no transparency, without consulting the stakeholders,” he said.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

According to Diallo, recent events have “damaged football’s image, its credibility, and have introduced the poison of division”. He cited the Fifa Peace Prize, the lifting of Folarin Balogun’s red-card suspension during the World Cup, the extended half-time break during the final and the failed World Cup sell-off plan.

Diallo indicated he had not spoken with Infantino in months. “The last time I saw him was at the World Cup, when he came to a few France matches,” he said. “Unfortunately he didn’t take the opportunity to share some of his projects with us. I considered that to be an act of defiance.”

Diallo said he would go into detail on his manifesto on 6 December at the Euro 2028 qualifying draw in Belfast. “My vision is that of open governance,” he said. “It’s one where the authorities truly play their role and the president is in charge of vision and strategy but leaves the day-to-day management to the secretary general. I think that certain stakeholders, namely the clubs and players, need to be more directly involved.”

Sports.title: Peter Storey, Arsenal Double winner and England international, dies aged 81
Sports.content:
Arsenal have paid tribute to Peter Storey, a key member of their 1971 Double-winning team, after the death of the former England midfielder at the age of 81.

Storey was part of the Bertie Mee team that secured the First Division title and FA Cup in a season that remains one of the most celebrated in Arsenal’s history and played 501 times for the club. That places him eighth on their appearances list.

Storey, who represented England on 19 occasions from 1971-73, earned respect for his uncompromising approach and versatility, also featuring at right-back.

View image in fullscreen Peter Storey playing for England against Scotland at Wembley in May 1973. Photograph: Ed Lacey/Popperfoto/Getty Images

Storey died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family. Arsenal said: “Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 Double winner Peter Storey. All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time.”

Born in Surrey, Storey began his career at Arsenal and made his debut shortly after his 20th birthday in 1965. He is fondly remembered by the club’s fans for scoring a stoppage-time penalty in the 1971 FA Cup semi-final against Stoke that forced a replay and kept the Double dream alive.

Storey left for Fulham in 1977 and retired eight months later when his contract was cancelled, going on to own a pub in north London. He was later convicted of several criminal offences, including financing a plot to counterfeit gold coins and smuggling pornography. He released an autobiography, True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, in September 2010.

Storey’s family said: “We are deeply grateful for the many kind messages, tributes and good wishes we have received. It has been a great comfort to see the affection and respect in which he was held by so many, both within the football community and beyond.”

Sports.title: Pocognoli’s aspiration for how Scotland must play is in danger of becoming unworkable
Sports.content:
The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments.

There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching in to the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. The meek nature of Scotland’s collapse in the 4-0 loss to a second-string Switzerland was lamentable. The Belgian’s assessment, with overpraise a key theme, raised eyebrows.

Pocognoli’s team scored five goals in six Nations League games, four coming against North Macedonia. They drew blanks in three fixtures. The concession of 10 depicts a team soft against set pieces and open play. Scotland have wingers who are not appropriately deployed because of dedication to a system. They have an obvious shortage of centre-backs yet Pocognoli picks three at a time. The midfield lacks balance. Not one player under Pocognoli’s watch is consistently excelling.

Pocognoli is obstinate in respect of his tactics. At club level this can work owing to daily work on a training pitch. Scotland are wedded to a 3-4-2-1 that fits too few of their players. There is no transfer window capacity to change that. Pocognoli’s insistence upon his “philosophy” sets off alarm bells. Although his English is strong, it is far from perfect, which raises questions about communication. Scotland do not look well drilled or clear in approach, which was plain in the unimpressive home win against North Macedonia even before the Switzerland debacle.

There is no detailed body of work to suggest Pocognoli can adapt or oversee improvement. He achieved great success in Belgium, winning the title at Union Saint-Gilloise, before a brief spell at Monaco. The Scottish FA’s deep faith in this 39-year-old, amid all manner of waffle about metrics and analytics, was on the basis of just over 100 games as a manager. It remains probable that the association erred in not sourcing a coach with dugout experience at a country of similar scale to Scotland. This always had the whiff of trying to be too smart by half.

The best Scotland sides are unapologetically horrible to play against, physical, energetic and direct. Shortcomings in skill are offset by attitude. Pocognoli’s version is the opposite on all fronts, ponderous and timid. The Tartan Army, hardly a ferociously demanding lot, have failed to demonstrate any excitement about Pocognoli.

This counts as no ode to Clarke. After seven years, change was required. It was the turn taken by the Scottish FA in implementing a new strategy that looks increasingly dubious.

Footballers are typically selfish beings. For now it suits the Scotland squad – and is fair – to state Pocognoli requires time and that they are behind him. Not only did the body language amid the unravelling in St Gallen suggest otherwise, those players are likely to adopt a different position if focus turns towards them. Scotland’s contingent is heavy on influential, experienced players.

There is no sense of the Scottish FA dispensing with Pocognoli at this point. Not only would such a move be premature, it would deliver an admission of failure that those running the governing body are never keen on providing. They enjoy the trappings and profile provided by the national team without anything like the adjacent accountability. They are assisted in this context by domestic football obsession within the country. There will be grumblings about Pocognoli for a brief period this week before the theme is placed into cold storage.

View image in fullscreen Scotland do not look well drilled or clear in approach, which was plain in the unimpressive home win against North Macedonia. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images

Next month’s Uefa 2028 qualifying draw, where Scotland will appear from pot three, carries intrigue and danger for Pocognoli. The assumption that Scotland will feature in the tournament is undermined by performances; England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland are co-hosting and a maximum of two spots are open for any of those nations who do not qualify. Not playing in a competition where games will be staged in Glasgow would count as a humiliation for the Scottish FA.

If Scotland face competitive games rather than friendlies in March, which will be determined after the draw, Pocognoli needs stark improvement. Without it, his paymasters would then have a decision to make while looking to keep Euro 2028 dreams alive. The situation is already that acute.

Pocognoli was not part of the Scotland party that landed in Glasgow from Zurich on Tuesday. His family have remained in Belgium. Alone with his thoughts on his journey home, Pocognoli must have pondered the harshness of his new environment. He has the sternest of challenges to douse legitimate background noise.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Jürgen Klopp hard-launches his Germany rebuilding project in style
Sports.content:
RIDING THE WAVE

Barely six weeks ago, Jürgen Klopp’s big home debut in the Germany dugout ended in a deeply frustrating 1-0 Nations League defeat to Greece – but the manager tasked with returning Die Mannschaft to relevance claimed not to care. “I’m completely unbothered,” Klopp trilled unconvincingly. “I’ve lost far more matches than I would have liked, but as long as you draw the right conclusions, a loss is ultimately a piece of information – no different from a win.” It was a quote straight out of the Pierre Sage playbook for unfussed continental coaches – and probably worried a few German FA suits, given Klopp had already threatened to quit at his own unveiling over potential media intrusion and criticism. “If you say tomorrow, ‘he’s [sh!t]’, tell me to my face and I’m out,” Klopp roared to trembling hacks in July. That imagined confrontation now looks unlikely to take place, because his Germany side are suddenly very good indeed.

If subsequent Nations League results – two wins over Serbia and a 0-0 draw in Greece – didn’t move the needle much, Monday’s 5-0 demolition of the Netherlands was different. This was the perfect night to hard-launch Klopp’s rebuilding project, with young talents pressing and passing relentlessly up front, forcing keeper Bart Verbruggen to gather his defenders for a chat in the Sunday League style. It didn’t help as Germany racked up four goals in 17 second-half minutes, leaving Klopp’s fellow big-name newcomer, Xavi Hernández, facing questions just days after they had smashed seven past Greece.

View image in fullscreen Just watch out for the guns. They’ll get you. Photograph: Odd Andersen/AFP/Getty Images

Klopp has packed his early squads with untested, overlooked talent and the approach is bearing fruit, with the newcomers Brajan Gruda and Derry Scherhant both on the scoresheet in Berlin. As an added bonus, he is also getting the best out of Florian Wirtz – a move that may achieve the unthinkable and make Klopp even more popular on Merseyside. “For at least the next three or four months, no one will be questioning the German national team,” Klopp cheered, showing a solid understanding of how international windows work. Gruda’s goal to make it 5-0 also edged Germany above their opponents on goal difference, meaning they will be seeded for the last eight, avoiding France and England.

Speaking of which, Klopp is not the only German coach riding a wave of vindication towards Euro 2028, flicking Vs at crowds of haters on the way past. Thomas Tuchel’s England side are further along in the process, and look more ready to land a major trophy than Germany – which, all in all, is a very weird sentence to write. While the mutual respect is strong between these two pulsing managerial minds, Tuchel has previously struggled in Klopp’s shadow, following the beloved coach at Mainz and Dortmund in the manner of a surly substitute teacher. Are their paths destined to cross again in a major final before long? It’s too early to say. But here’s one piece of information we can all agree on: Germany are back.

Join Scott Murray from 7.45pm GMT for hot updates from Wales 1-2 Portugal in the Nations League.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“The score is painful. I see a lot of good things in the way that we try to play. The result is heavy but the players gave everything. They enjoy playing like this” – an eye test suggests otherwise, but Sébastien Pocognoli is still trying to put a positive spin on Scotland’s 4-0 Nations League shoeing by a second-string Switzerland in St Gallen.

View image in fullscreen Lewis Ferguson apparently enjoying playing like that, earlier. Photograph: Romina Amato/Reuters

Nice to know where someone could, in theory at least, get some last-minute gifts for Christmas. Would make a change from a road atlas and oil this year” – Mike Turney.

Sports.title: Wiegman cites young talent as key to new England deal after calling up Goodwin
Sports.content:
Sarina Wiegman says the potential in England’s emerging young players helped convince her to extend her contract until the end of 2029’s European Championship.

The Lionesses head coach, whose previous deal was due to expire next year, gave first senior call-ups to the striker Isobel Goodwin and goalkeeper Katie Cox on Tuesday as she named her squad for December’s two-leg World Cup qualifying playoff against Ukraine.

Speaking to the media for the first time since she signed her new contract in October, Wiegman described the Football Association as “a trailblazer with the women’s game and a great federation to work for” and said: “I’m really happy with the team but also talents coming through, which is exciting, and there’s now some high potential, and hopefully these talents go from high potential to world-class players, if not already. And I hope to have a part in that, too, and have a contribution to that. While I’m talking about that, I’m getting excited.

“The majority of their development is happening [at their clubs] but when they come to our environment, I hope to have a little part of that contribution.”

The Dutchwoman has led England to three consecutive major tournament finals, lifting two European titles, since taking charge in 2021 on a deal to 2025. Asked whether she had expected that to become an eight-year stay, she said: “No. I thought: ‘Four years, that’s a long time.’ Then it became six years and that looks like it’s becoming eight years. I would never have expected all of the things that we have reached.”

Will she call it a day in 2029? “Well, I tend to think that’s the end point, but you never know! I don’t plan that far ahead. So let’s see where it gets to.”

Defenders: Lucy Bronze (Chelsea), Jess Carter (Gotham), Grace Fisk (Liverpool), Taylor Hinds (Arsenal), Maya Le Tissier (Manchester United), Esme Morgan (Washington Spirit), Poppy Pattinson (London City Lionesses), Leah Williamson (Arsenal)



Midfielders: Laura Blindkilde Brown (Manchester City), Grace Clinton (Manchester City), Erica Meg Parkinson (North Carolina Courage), Lexi Potter (Chelsea), Georgia Stanway (Arsenal), Ella Toone (Manchester United), Keira Walsh (Chelsea)
