Wiegman, whose latest 25-player squad includes 10 players with fewer than 10 caps, watched from the stands at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday as Goodwin scored for London City Lionesses with a terrific finish against Arsenal. She said of the 23-year-old: “We always knew she’s a huge talent [with] a high potential. We’re watching a lot of games over periods of time, all the time, so we [had] kept an eye on her anyway, but I think it also helped that she had that great goal and a great performance last Sunday.

“She has some different qualities. She’s really fast too. She can head – she showed that also in attacking set plays and defending set plays also – and she can score goals. Does she need to step up to the next level? Absolutely. But you can tell that she’s improving.”

Wiegman was unable to call upon several injured players, including Lauren James and Alex Greenwood. She included Manchester United’s Ella Toone, who was initially left out of September’s squad before being recalled for the playoff against Greece. Wiegman said of Toone: “She has impressed us really well. She responded really well. And going back to [her] club, she’s done well too. And that’s what has been fed back to me too.”

Cox is rare in getting an England call-up while playing in the second-tier WSL2. The 20-year-old is on loan at Nottingham Forest from Chelsea.

The Lionesses face Ukraine on neutral territory in Spain in the away leg on 1 December before playing them at Wembley four days later.

Sports.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
Sports.content:
“Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes.

The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material.

“There are two types of humans,” Jorge Valdano narrates, “Carlos Bilardo and everyone else.” Ricardo “El Gringo” Giusti recounts how he buried a sweet in the pitch before kick-off of every game, just one of the many cábalas the Argentina squad religiously followed under pressure from their obsessive manager. On the eve of the match with England, the players requested lighter shirts as the official ones were too heavy when drenched in sweat. Footage of women working at the squad hotel hand-stitching the numbers on to light T-shirts bought locally, shot by the players themselves with a handheld camera, conveys an intimacy in stark contrast to grainy archive material depicting British explorers in the South Atlantic.

View image in fullscreen A still from The Match, where Gary Lineker is watching footage of Diego Maradona scoring for Argentina against England. Photograph: Disney

Rather than run-of-the-mill talking head-style interviews with members of both teams, the interviewees are shot in monochrome, widescreen closeups, “like Roman statues”, as Cabral told the Guardian. Like monuments to themselves, the camera lingers on their eyes. What are they watching? We don’t know if they see what we see, if they are reliving the match, or seeing a cut of the actual film.

The documentary pivots around Diego Maradona’s two goals. I have long ceased to think of them as two separate goals. They are a single event, a handful of minutes when everything that is possible in football happened before our very eyes: the ugly, rule-breaking handball followed by the spectacular, beautiful gambeta. The film cleverly uses a sequence of stills taken by the Mexican photographer Alejandro Ojeda Carbajal to prove the handball, with a tongue-in-cheek nod to the paradox that they have been credited and licensed through the Englishman Bob Thomas ever since.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen A poster for The Match, a documentary that pivots around Diego Maradona’s two goals against England. Photograph: Disney

Films about football are hard to get right because football is a narrative form in itself. This one comes pretty close to being as good as it gets. Slick and elegant, if at times a little too glossy, The Match is an excellent piece of work filled with beautiful images, such as the crisp vintage radio illustrating soldiers listening to the game in the trenches. There are also newsreels of Margaret Thatcher and Argentinian generals at the height of the Falklands/Malvinas conflict; a score that includes Queen and giants of Argentinian rock such as Charly García. Nostalgia, history, and the backdrop of the war, handled with respect and sensitivity.

The perversity of Argentina’s military is reflected in images of an emaciated soldier spliced to the voice of a general who dismisses claims the troops were cold and starving: “They probably eat better than they did at home.” Lou Armour, a British veteran, explains he couldn’t see young Argentinians as the enemy. “We both suffered a tragedy,” Cabral says. “I’m interested in the human duality in which we go from killing each other to hugging each other.” Cabral asks when a match starts and when it ends, and also when a conflict does so.

Valdano reads Juan López y John Ward, a Jorge Luis Borges poem about the war, in Spanish. Lineker, sitting by his side, utters “very moving”, also in Spanish. English and Spanish coexist throughout the film, including in the scene showing a table football game in which John Barnes and Peter Shilton take on against Giusti, Óscar Ruggeri and Jorge Burruchaga. Burruchaga, the scorer of the winning goal in the 1986 World Cup final, cheers his opponent: “Vamos, Peter!”

View image in fullscreen A screengrab from the trailer of The Match, about the game during which Diego Maradona ‘scored’ twice. Photograph: Disney

An audience containing young people reacted to the documentary with a standing ovation at the London screening, where Shilton was the only cast member present. In Buenos Aires, the release of the documentary, which coincided with this summer’s World Cup, saw cinemas packed with young people. For a generation in England and Argentina who never saw the 1986 classic, almost everything in The Match is new.

The Match is in UK cinemas from 20 November

Sports.title: Janine van Wyk: ‘Our rooms were empty … no mattresses, no lightbulbs and not a drop of water’
Sports.content:
I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group.

As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it.

We felt unwelcome from the moment we arrived and we were not the only team to experience this. Nigeria exploited all avenues to play mind games with their opposition and to make them lose focus on the matches.

We arrived early in the morning at the Murtala Muhammed international airport in Lagos and faced our first test: how to retrieve our luggage. Only one carousel was working, which meant we had to wait a long time for our bags to arrive. We had a training session planned for later in the day and were all eager to get to the hotel, settle in and prepare for our first practice.

As we stepped out the airport doors, we looked for the bus that was to take us there, but we didn’t see one anywhere. As players, we were irritable and impatient, and starting to show it. Some of us were slumped on our bags, others had taken up residence on the pavement, and we were all cranky, especially as it took over an hour before a bus arrived.

Like in Mozambique a few years before, the bus was too small. Another 21-seater and we were 27 – 20 players and seven support staff, as well as all our luggage. Luckily, most of us had experience of how to squeeze in and so we knew the drill. We also had the advantage of our bags travelling in a smaller vehicle behind the bus, so the only challenge was fitting all the bodies in.

View image in fullscreen Janine van Wyk looks out from the window of a bus at one of her many Wafcons. Photograph: Courtesy of Janine van Wyk

Generally, we saw the lighter side of these things and laughed as some of us got comfortable on the floor and others had to make do with a teammate’s lap. But we lost our sense of humour when we realised we had no air-conditioning and the drive was going to last at least another hour. Some grumbling ensued, but we knew better than to complain at such an early stage, and it seemed that things would get better soon.

When we got to the hotel, the building that greeted us looked fairly new from the outside, with freshly painted walls and a manicured garden at the entrance. But when we walked through the doors, it looked as though the hotel was in the process of being renovated, and the outside was clearly the bit that had been made up first. It still looked like a decent place, so we weren’t too worried, and the smell of new paint and the sight of workers installing lights made us feel special as the first group of people staying in this hotel.

All of us were looking forward to being in our rooms and the chance to shower and relax before training. It was only when I saw maintenance workers carrying still-sealed mattresses to the rooms that it occurred to me that we were being put up in a hotel that was not fully ready for guests. I was only half-right. Actually, it was not ready at all.

When we got to our rooms, they were empty: no mattresses on the beds, no lightbulbs in the lamps and, worst of all, not a drop of water in the taps. This made us all a little worried, but we were told it would be sorted out as soon as we had finished our training. We did have lunch at the hotel, although by now I was suspicious of things and particularly of the spread of fish and chicken, and then left for training. At least that went smoothly, and we expected to get back to suitable accommodation. No such luck.

View image in fullscreen South African players celebrate a goal at the 2006 tournament, where they would go in to finish in third place. Photograph: Pius Utomi Ekpei/AFP/Getty Images

We returned to beds being made but still had no lights or running water. After a training session in extremely warm conditions, we were all dripping with sweat from head to toe and we had to make another plan. A few of our players spotted a river just outside the hotel and said they were going to go there to rinse themselves off. I thought they were joking.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

When I looked again, the players had stripped down to their tights and sports bras, wrapped themselves in their pristine white hotel towels with their toiletries in hand and were heading out the door. If I wanted to be clean, I realised, I had to join them. My hesitation was twofold: I had never washed in a river before and wasn’t sure whether it was hygienic, but I was also still quite young and didn’t want to expose my body in public. I had to get over my qualms quite quickly. Fortunately, we didn’t have to wash in the river again. No one knows how, but when we opened the taps the following day, the water gushed out.

With that kind of preparation, and Nigeria being as strong a team as they were, it was hardly a surprise that we lost 2-0. We experienced Nigeria’s off the field tactics first-hand. I did have one happy memory from the match, though. The Nigerian centre-back, Onome Ebi, who would go on to become the first African to play in six World Cups between 2003 and 2023, gave me her jersey. We both wore No 5 and she was the first international to give me her shirt. Given how much my Banyana Banyana jersey meant to me, I understood how special and symbolic this moment was, and I have stored it in my memory to this day.

This is an edited extract from 185: The Janine van Wyk Story is published by Karavan Press and available on Amazon in the United Kingdom.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino hints at raid for USMNT stars as key player teases future Manchester United transfers
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino has opened the door for United States players to join him at Manchester United in the future.

The Argentine has been announced as the new head coach at United on a two-and-a-half year deal, replacing Michael Carrick in the dugout.

2 Pochettino has teased the prospect of United States men's national team players signing for him at United Credit: Getty

Pochettino, formerly of Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea, is due to officially join the Premier League giants this week.

He will first take charge of the United States men's national team fixture against Haiti at 12am UK time, with his side heading into the second leg of the CONCACAF Nations League A quarter-final 6-0 up on aggregate.

Football has garnered increased interest in the United States in recent years, with Pochettino taking them to the last-16 of the 2026 World Cup.

Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun are among their star players, with Tyler Adams, Chris Richards and Antonee Robinson at Premier League clubs this season.

Could Pochettino sign USMNT stars at United?

With a move to United on the horizon, Pochettino was asked if he would work with the club to sign anyone from the USMNT squad.

"Now is not the time (to talk about it)," he said in a press conference. "I know that you asked the players before.

"All the good players always have dreams to reach the last level, and I think United is one of the teams that is in the last level.

"And it's a dream for many of the players but now, I think they need to be focusing on today, tomorrow's game, their clubs. I know, really well, for more than two years, every single player, and I think (they) are all players with an unbelievable talent.

"Of course, in the future, when that happens, we are going to pay attention in case, to make some decisions and pay attention to players that we know really well."

Juventus midfielder Weston McKennie is another of the USMNT's top stars and been linked with a move to the Premier League, where he made 19 appearances on loan at Leeds United in the 2022/23 season.

2 McKennie is one of the top players in their squad and believes big moves to a club like United for his teammates are inevitable Credit: Getty

He was also asked about the prospect of his international teammates joining Pochettino at Old Trafford.

To which he remarked: "Obviously, in his time here, I think he's grown to like this team and seen the quality that this team has to offer.

"I think it's a potential, we have a lot of guys on our team that are due to probably make moves soon, or within the next year.

"I think it's kind of inevitable but at the end of the day, you never know what's going on in a coach's mind and what players that he's actually looking for.

"But I think you could potentially see some of the guys from here being talked about to go to Man U, and potentially it happening."

Pochettino makes his United debut on Sunday when they travel to their rivals Liverpool in the Premier League.

Sports.title: UEFA facing £3.7bn row as 138 clubs launch explosive complaint over power of Europe’s elite
Sports.content:
UEFA facing £3.7bn row as 138 clubs launch explosive complaint over power of Europe’s elite

The Union of European Clubs (UEC) have launched a formal complaint against UEFA and European Football Clubs (EFC).

It could kickstart an investigation from the European Commission into the power struggle at the top of football in the continent.



3 UEFA have been hit with a formal complaint from UEC Credit: Getty

UEC's complaint takes aim at the perceived stranglehold maintained by UEFA and EFC on European football.

It forms part of their efforts to gain recognition by the governing body and dilute the power of the sport's elite.

The organisation have challenge a memorandum of understanding between UEFA and EFC.



As part of the agreement, which expires in July 2033, EFC is the 'sole body' representing European clubs.

This comes despite UEC having 138 members across 25 national associations, including 19 clubs from England.



As a result, the organisation filed a complaint to the European Commission on Monday.

UEFA complaint filed

However, it could take at least four months before a decision is made on whether or not to open an investigation.



The complaint alleges that the memorandum of understanding breaches two articles of the EU treaty.

It is claimed that the agreement goes against article 101, which bans anticompetitive agreements, and article 102 banning the abuse of a dominant position.

At present, clubs cannot join another cross-border association without the permission of UEFA and EFC.

3 UEC also claim a select group of clubs have decisive influence over Champions League access Credit: Getty



UEC general secretary and CEO of Croatian club Lokomotiva Zagreb Dennis Gudasic has issued a statement on the complaint.

Via The Guardian, he said: "The question is simple: who gets a say in the rules that shape every club’s future?

"Today, one association holds that mandate for all of Europe’s clubs, while most clubs have no effective voice in it.

"We are asking the commission to examine whether that is compatible with EU law, and to help open European football’s governance to the whole pyramid."



What are EFC and UEC?

The move comes with EFC closing in on 1,000 members, with 21 coming from England.

Those include Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur and West Ham United as 'ordinary' members.

3 PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi is chairman of EFC Credit: Getty

UEC feels EFC should not have an exclusive mandate on the governance of European football, with claims that clubs do not have equal voting rights within the group.



Of the 138 UEC member clubs, 59 are said to have asked for their membership status to remain private upon joining the group.

This is understood to be due to concerns over the potential for pressure to be applied to them.

During the last 18 months, UEC have proposed a number of measures in a bid to improve the flow of money to clubs below the continent's elite outfits.

They include a 'player development award' which would see five per cent of revenue from club competitions redistributed to teams whose academies have developed the players competing in the tournament.



UEC have also put forward a model for reinvesting media rights deals for continental competitions in domestic leagues around Europe.

Sports.title: Jeff Stelling offers solution for 3pm blackout in passionate monologue as Simon Jordan criticises Andy Burnham
Sports.content:
Premier League matches should be mostly played on Sundays, with EFL and lower league fixtures taking precedence on Saturdays.

That's a suggestion made by talkSPORT host Jeff Stelling, whilst Simon Jordan took aim at Prime Minister Andy Burnham for voicing his views on possibly removing the 3pm blackout across the United Kingdom.

4 A 3pm blackout has been instilled in English football for six decades, but there is constant talk on removing the rule Credit: Getty

Football matches cannot be broadcast on television from 2:45pm until 5:15pm on a Saturday as part of a rule that dates back to the 1960s.

It was introduced to encourage fans to attend games being played in the lower leagues but, with the majority of fixtures being scheduled a 3pm, only a handful can be televised at lunchtime or later in the evening.

Fans of Premier League clubs have expressed grievances over the rule with a view of it being outdated, given that numerous countries across the world can broadcast their matches but those in the UK cannot.

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters told talkSPORT earlier in the year that a decision on potentially ending the 3pm blackout could be confirmed before the conclusion of next season.

The current TV rights cycle runs until the end of the 2028/29 campaign, and so a removal of the watershed could take place from then onwards.

Should the 3pm blackout end?

However, Breakfast host Stelling detailed his concerns over what could happen if the blackout is dismissed, and proposed a solution that EFL and lower league clubs would also benefit from.

"I read a brilliant piece, it was first written in 2023 and it's been updated in The Athletic. People out there, I know if you're a Premier League fan, you'll say, 'Lower league games are not going to be affected because the 3pm kick-offs in the Premier League will be Hull against Fulham, that sort of thing', with all due respect.

"But once this goes through, if it goes through, what is to stop things changing? For instance, this season, Chelsea against Liverpool, that's a 12:30pm kick-off, Chelsea against Manchester United was a 12:30pm kick-off, Newcastle against Arsenal is 5:30pm, City against Chelsea is 5:30pm.

"What's to stop the powers that be making those games, the big games, three o'clock kick-offs? Then see what affect it has on the lower league sides. There is a solution presented in this article as well, and it's this - don't have any Premier League 3pm kick-offs, and then it doesn't affect the other leagues at all.

"Play them at 12:30pm and 5:30pm or, here's a better idea, play them all, or virtually all of them, on Sundays.

4 Stelling has backed clubs in the EFL and lower leagues and called for a schedule change to suit all parties Credit: talkSPORT

"Make Sunday the Premier League day, and then the EFL and all the lower leagues below that, they've got their day on Saturday, the Premier League have got the field to themselves on a Sunday."

Burnham has also expressed worry over the prospect of ending the 3pm blackout as he said, via the BBC: "I would urge a bit of caution because it does protect the income of lower-league clubs.

"If you have effectively wall-to-wall Premier League football at any time, it takes away perhaps the incentive to go and watch the football league or non-league.

"So I think it has to be considered carefully. I'm not going to take the pure consumer view here. I'll take the health-of-football approach to this particular issue."

However, former Crystal Palace owner Jordan claimed that the Prime Minister is not well-informed on the subject and that politicians in general must have an understanding of it before commenting.

"Is he right, or is he playing to the crowd on this?" asked White and Jordan host Jim White. "He, you, I and everybody else knows that if you kick off games live on the tele at 3pm, attendances would suffer."

4 Jordan has criticised PM Burnham for weighing in on the 3pm blackout debate as he believes his argument does not have substance Credit: talkSPORT

"What's that based upon then? That's based upon empirical data that was created 50, 60 years ago, 70, 80 years ago when the factories started to open at a certain time and close at a certain time.

"Of course, the expectations were that people had a certain viewpoint about watching live games when television rights became more prevalent. Is there any empirical data to support this?

"The EFL are the argument about this. It's not the Premier League, the Premier League have got 98 per cent occupancy, they don't care about whether the watershed comes down at 3pm, they want to broadcast their games and give the broadcasters more money so the game can be redistributed.

"You can't have it always, you cannot ask the Premier League to redistribute... and then there's barriers. If they want to go to a 3pm watershed and take it away, and the idea is that, somehow, watching a Premier League game detracts from going to watch a lesser-than game, there might be some substance to that.

"But what are you getting in exchange for it? What are you getting for that? Because you're not giving it up for nothing. If you're getting far more than you're giving then, surely to God, the Prime Minister would be well-served in immersing himself in some of the detail.

"And the detail about his ridiculous observations about lifting the drinking scenario (ban), he doesn't know what he's talking about. It's wonderful that you're a man of the people, it's wonderful that you're trying to be connected to people, and I prefer politicians to be connected than not connected.

"But I'd also prefer them to have substance in what they're saying. I don't think there's any substance in most of the things that Lisa Nandy utters, and she's the head of the DCMS (Department for Culture, Media and SportDepartment for Culture, Media and Sport).

"When they wade into sport, irrespective of what particular colour of the party it is, whether it's the Conservatives, whether it's Labour, whether it's that clown college of Liberal Democrats, or the Green Party, or whatever other village idiots we've got that participate in our politics.

4 A decision on whether the 3pm blackout will be removed is expected to be made in the next couple of years Credit: Getty

"If they get involved in sport, know what you're talking about, and if you're going to talk about the 3pm barrier coming down to broadcast, what are you asking for?

"You're asking the Premier League to redistribute a big bag of money. Are you going to get more money being redistributed if you don't drop the 3pm watershed, or are you going to get less? So, understand what you're talking about..."

"He keeps on wading in with things," Jordan added on Burnham. "And it's wonderful, but populist decision-making that, at the end, has very little substance to it.

"I don't like politicians anywhere near sport, because I think that they only ever harness it and utilise it to create a relationship with the voting fan."

White pointed out that Burnham is an avid, match-going Everton fan, who demonstrates his passionate support of the club.

"There's nothing wrong with him being that," Jordan insisted. "Keir Starmer was a man of the people going to watch Arsenal, another ideologically aligned buffoon.

"The fact of the matter is, is that there is no necessity to wade into a subject matter without really being informed because if you asked him, 'What is it that you think you're losing? You're losing attendances, what is that based upon? And do you realise that, in order to get the Premier League to redistribute more money which is going to be existentially more important to the EFL, that they need this as a trade-off?

"'Oh do they?' 'Yeah, so why are you wading into something that you don't know? Because if the EFL clubs are going to get a huge amount more money from the Premier League clubs, because the Premier League clubs get something as a trade-off, wouldn't that be a better way to go for English football?'

"'Oh, I suppose so,' so why don't you shut up and get the facts then, rather than grandstanding?"

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney says he considered suicide during time at Man United
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney says he considered suicide during time at Man United

Wayne Rooney has revealed that he considered taking his own life as he struggled during his time Manchester United.

The Man United and England icon, who is one of the nation's most beloved footballers, admitted having suicidal thoughts.

3 Rooney has revealed that he contemplated suicide during his time playing for Man United as he struggled with the pressures of his career Credit: Getty

Rooney became a Premier League superstar in an instant, with him breaking onto the scene as a 16-year-old for Everton.

He went on to join United and ended his career with the Red Devils as their all-time top goalscorer, winning five league titles, the Champions League, Europa League, FA Cups and three League Cups.

The 41-year-old eventually retired in 2021 and has since become a leading pundit on TV screens, building a post-playing career.

But, despite Rooney seemingly living the dream, he has actually been through some incredibly tough times over the years.

Help at hand If you are struggling, you can call the CALM helpline anonymously between 5pm and midnight 365 days a year on 0800 58 58 58. The Samaritans are also there to help on 116 123 any time, day or night.

Rooney admits he contemplated suicide

Speaking on the Life at the Midpoint podcast with Gabby Logan, Rooney spoke openly and honestly about his struggles.

He bravely admitted that amid the pressures of his career he struggled with alcohol and considered suicide as he hid away from his son Kai.

When asked about his 'rock bottom', Rooney said: "When I was drinking, I would lock myself in my house for two days and just drink.

"This is probably in my best part of my career playing wise. I would have a couple of days off and I'd sit in a games room and drink for two days and I'd get up and in the morning I'd have training.

"I couldn't deal with all the pressures of everything. The pressure of football I was alright with...I made stupid choices when I was younger off the pitch, and I really struggled to deal with it all."

He added: "I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with.

3 Rooney has opened up on his troubles during the height of his career, as he shut himself away and drank for days Credit: Getty

"I didn't want Kai seeing me like that, so that's why I'd hide away as well.

"I got to a place where you're contemplating suicide. I just didn't want to be around anyone. I didn't want to see people in the streets. I didn't want to go into shops.

"I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else, I really struggled with it."

What else has Rooney said on his struggles?

Rooney, who is currently featuring on the new series of I'm A Celebrity Get Me Out of Here, also revealed more details on his issues.

He tried to hide his problems and dark thoughts, praising wife Coleen for sticking by his side through his life's lowest point.

"You don't want to show any weakness to anything really, so you try to mask it," Rooney went on to explain.

3 The Man United and England icon admitted that he would hide his issues, but his wife Coleen knew, helping him through the extremely tough period Credit: Getty

"Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man, if you like, for doing that."

He continued: "I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because when I look back I was probably at the height of my career, I've just had a young son, I've just been married.

"It should be the happiest point in my life and it wasn't.

"It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking.

"Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it."

Sports.title: Predict 6: Win £50k this weekend in talkSPORT’s free to play Premier League predictor game

Sports.title: Simon Jordan has perfect reaction to Sol Campbell describing himself as an icon
Sports.content:
Simon Jordan has perfect reaction to Sol Campbell describing himself as an icon

Simon Jordan was unable hide his smile as he listened to ex-Arsenal and Tottenham defender Sol Campbell label himself an 'icon'.

It is 25 years since Campbell made one of the most controversial transfers ever by joining the Gunners after departing Tottenham as a free agent.

5 Campbell made one of the most controversial transfers by joining bitter North London rivals Arsenal on a free from Tottenham in 2001 Credit: GETTY

5 He was set to become a legend at Tottenham before he left, leading to huge backlash and abuse coming his way from fans Credit: Getty

The former England centre-back came through the youth ranks at White Hart Lane and was on his way to becoming a club legend.

He played over 300 times for his boyhood side, building a reputation as one of the best in the Premier League and captaining the club to League Cup glory in 1999.

However, in 2001, the 52-year-old made the one move that a Spurs player should never make by signing for Arsenal. - having previously insisted he would pen a new deal.

His decision to do so, despite plenty of interest from elsewhere, led to huge amounts of backlash and abuse, with 'Judas' banners held aloft in the stands on his return to face his old side with the Gunners.

Bottles were also thrown at him amid many chants coming from the stands, while an effigy of the defender was burned on a lampost.

And to speak about the well-known backlash he went through, and still faces to this day, Campbell joined Piers Morgan's Football Uncensored alongside Jordan.

What has Sol Campbell said of backlash he has received?

Morgan said the abuse he received was 'ferocious and nasty', with the ex-England international saying it was worse than that, admitting that he doesn't understand why younger fans hate him too.

"I think it was beyond that, it was almost criminal some of the stuff and very cleverly worked out as well," Campbell said.

"Of course I have (apologised). The main thing is, some people feeling hurt and things like that. Some weren't even born at the time and feeling something, that was a bit bizarre for me as well.

"I get maybe someone maybe 35 or 40 plus, but I've apologised from time to time...

5 Jordan instantly looked baffled,side-eyeing Morgan, after Campbell labelled himself an icon while talking about the abuse he faces from Spurs fans

"I'm not going to apologise for the quality football, how I moved on England, moved myself on, helped Arsenal win loads of stuff.

"You know, I was an icon. And I loved to challenge, a bit too much, with the nastiness."

Jordan can't hide reaction to 'icon' claim

Campbell's self titling as an icon instantly drew a smirk from talkSPORT's Jordan, who quickly side-eyed Morgan.

He then chuckled as Campbell continued talking before having to intervene and point out why he had lost his composure.

"I'm laughing at the idea that someone else should be describing you as an icon rather than doing it yourself," Jordan commented.

Campbell won two Premier League titles as a player and was part of Arsenal's Invincibles season, playing over 500 top-flight games.

5 The talkSPORT host couldn't help by smile as he chuckled about the ex-defender's confident comment

'The one place you don't go to is Arsenal'

Jordan later discussed the viral clip of him and Morgan chatting with Campbell about his controversial transfer on talkSPORT.

And the co-host broke down why the Tottenham fans were so furious with the four-time FA Cup winner's move to Arsenal amid his continued confusion.

He said: "This industry that is fueled by emotion, driven by emotion, that creates this remarkable opportunity for people to be indexed to a football club that they live vicariously through...

"Was it constructive emotion? You can have emotions, but only emotions that people feel are acceptable?

"You can't have it both ways, you can't thrive and create huge opportunities for yourself in this industry... and not expect that there's a consequence for what people perceive to be a major slight to them."

"The situation with Sol is people will see the way media-facing perspective was orchestrated... Sol ran his contract down and walked out of the door after supposedly promising Tottenham that he would sign a new contract and left on a free transfer," Jordan added.

5 Campbell was a success at Arsenal, but Spurs fans have detested the former centre-back ever since he made the transfer Credit: Getty

"These players go around telling you they love the club they play for, kiss the badge, die for it, and the supporters believe that as it means so much to them, they don't understand it doesn't mean so much to the players.

"He was a product of the academy and the one place you don't go to is Arsenal, that's why they feel that way."

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino urged to follow Kyle Walker advice with favourite Man United star
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino finally gets to work with Marcus Rashford - and a new position could be what the England star needs to return to form.

The 54-year-old was confirmed as the new Manchester United manager last week after he departed his role as USMNT head coach.



3 Pochettino arrives at Old Trafford with plenty to sort Credit: AFP

The Argentine succeeds Michael Carrick, who was sacked by the Red Devils last Thursday following a disastrous start to the season.

The ex-Tottenham and Chelsea boss was in the running for the Old Trafford gig in 2022, only for Man United to instead hire Erik ten Hag.

However, despite missing out on the post, Pochettino made it clear months later what a huge fan he was of academy graduate Rashford.



What did Pochettino say about Rashford?

“I’ve always liked him, I knew of his process because I was in England, but I think he’s a great player,” he said at the Qatar World Cup.

“He just needs the confidence and for himself to believe, to put him at the top level. The quality is there for him.”



Four years later, Rashford is waiting for a manager to help return him to the form he last showed at Man United under Ten Hag.

The 29-year-old, who scored 14 goals in 49 appearances on loan at Barcelona last season, is yet to find the net for the Red Devils since his summer return.



Rashford has since missed United's past six games with a troublesome hip injury, but could be available for Pochettino's first game - away to rivals Liverpool on Sunday.

And European football expert Andy Brassell has reiterated what Kyle Walker saod in calling for the 78-cap international to switch from his favoured left wing role to become a fully fledged centre forward.

3 Rashford has less than two years remaining on his United deal Credit: Getty

Rashford to play as a striker

Walker said on Drive in October: "I like him on the left. I think he would probably be more effective though, through the middle."



Now, Brassell has said that position change could come about under Pochettino, given the scarcity of quality at the top end of attack.

Benjamin Sesko has been ruled out until 2027, with Bryan Mbeumo deputising out of position during the latter weeks of Carrick's reign.

On Rashford, Brassell said: "I think it's difficult for him going into the season knowing he's not desperately wanted anywhere.

"I think we saw a few little bits near the start of this season where he was obviously applying himself very well in training.



3 Once one of United's most exciting stars, Rashford is yet to rediscover his top form, in part due to injury, since returning from Barcelona Credit: Getty

"And we saw a few good bits at the beginning of this season," he continued during an exclusive interview with talkSPORT.com.

"I guess the question is where Pochettino might use him because it seems that the centre-forward horse has almost bolted now.

"Barcelona brought him in as a player on the wide left to give cover, mainly to Raphinha. And he did that really well.



"I think he developed into that role brilliantly. Even when he wasn't a starter, he managed to contribute in a really, really good way.

"But I think when you look at Manchester United and where the holes are in the squad at the moment, it must be worth a go playing him at centre forward.

"It feels as if they don't really have that presence there at the moment. So, yeah, I wonder if it might be worth revisiting."

Sports.title: Man City sanctions facing major delay with punishment this season now touch and go
Sports.content:
Any sanctions for Manchester City could be subject to a lengthy delay with at least two further hearings expected if their appeal fails.

That's according to football finance expert Stefan Borson as the club wait to fight their case against the guilty verdict imposed on them in September by an independent commission.



4 A hearing into City's appeal against their guilty verdict of financial charges will be held in December Credit: Getty

City have been found guilty on all charges in relation to financial rule breaches in the Premier League from 2009 to 2018, which includes the artificial inflation of their revenue by £900million in that period.

An appeal has been launched and its hearing is set to take place next month, although any possible sanctions are expected to be handed down to City in 2027 if they are unsuccessful.

The club claim to have a 'comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence' that supports them in their case.



Premier League rivals have called for any sanctions to be applied this season but, as Borson explained on White and Jordan for talkSPORT, this is not guaranteed.

What is the latest on City's appeal hearing?

Borson said: "My understanding is that there has been no sanction hearing, so it's not as if the hearing has taken place with the independent commission but they're holding back the release of the decision, it's just that they haven't yet sat down and had the pitching of their cases, that will come after the appeal.



"So that looks like one of the uncertainties that we had about the process has now been cleared up. We'll have the appeal in December, it will definitely be days.

"The question is whether it'll be five, ten days. If it is starting on the 12th, let's say, of December, which is probably the last day it could start if it's mid-December, there's not a big window there because people are not working after about the 23rd in the legal world.



"There's probably only five to ten days that it could take for an appeal which is fairly short, I think, for an appeal of this magnitude, and certainly points to there being limited, if any, new evidence and no re-hearing of any witness evidence.

"So what they'll be doing is going through legal arguments and barrister submissions in respect of what's in that very big document that we haven't seen: the unredacted decision."

When asked about a timeframe for possible sanctions to be revealed or imposed, Borson explained: "So, we'll have the hearing. It's then unclear under the rules, because we don't know which rulebook we're working to.

4 Borson has warned that there could be further hearings to come as part of the appeal process against sanctions Credit: AFP



"But let's say 30 to 45 days, I think pretty much minimum, before we get a decision of the appeal. Now, the appeal usually would take much longer to give its decision, usually months, but it may be that the parties have agreed some kind of expedited decision, just to try and squeeze this all into this season.

"At that point the Premier League or City, probably City, decide to challenge aspects of the appeal decision under Rule X arbitration.

"Now, there's only very limited ways in which they could do that, but that could again set up another hearing, probably with another 30-day delay before the hearing starts, then the hearing itself, and then another delay for a decision from that Rule X hearing, which may follow.

"Only at that stage could City challenge anything at the High Court level, and even then it's only on very limited grounds.



"The point I'm trying to make is that a lot of the speed of the sanction, if City are unsuccessful on appeal, depends on whether they end up appealing under Rule X and whether the timetable has to shift out further, awaiting decisions."

On whether City will know their fate this season, he added: "I think it's going to be touch and go now. It will depend... let's say City lose the appeal and decide they have no grounds to challenge anything about the appeal.

4 Whilst City are unlikely to be fully successful in their appeal, some aspects of the charges could be challenged Credit: Getty

"In that scenario, we probably will move quite quickly to the first stage of the sanction, which is the independent commission who, clearly, are very against City, we know that from the thousand pages or whatever it is that they've written up, so they are going to come in very hard on City.



"City then will appeal the sanction. It's very unlikely the Premier League would but City will appeal the sanction. I think in almost any scenario, City will appeal the sanction. So, at very least, if City lose the appeal on liability from December, there's still two hearings remaining."

What could City be successful in appealing?

Although Borson believes City have a low chance of being completely successful in their appeal, he pointed out which charges they may be able to challenge as he said: "I think they may pick off the big bits, that's what they're going to try and do, definitely.

"They have definitely got a good chance, I think, in relation to the UEFA charges, which don't look right because the Premier League has not gone after all of the teams that breach UEFA - Aston Villa, Chelsea, everybody else - so it does look like they may have overreached there.

"City may succeed on this designation of a sham, but then there is a fallback position because the independent commission have got an alternative case on that.



"So, I think City are more likely to pick off bits. Let's say City did win on everything... look, the parties are at war, I think. We see that from some of the press yesterday."

Premier League makes plea to rival clubs

As per The Times, the Premier League have asked clubs to provide legal protection for chief executive Richard Masters and four other board directors should City sue them.

On this, Borson commented: "Ordinarily, companies would say to their directors, 'Don't worry about being sued, we'll pay, so unless you've done something seriously wrong...'

4 Premier League clubs have been asked to offer legal support for Masters and his colleagues if City decide to sue Credit: Getty



"Obviously if it's a criminal thing or if it's an FCA (Financial Conduct Authority) sanction, they won't pay for things like that, but if it's for ordinary course, somebody didn't like the actions that you took in business, usually the company would pay.

"It turns out that somehow the Premier League, like the EFL (English Football League) have got a very old style indemnity within their articles of association which are the rules of the company association.

"And it means that in theory, the directors are exposed personally to pay defence costs if they're sued personally by a third party, and that could include Etihad or Etisalat in this situation."

Sports.title: Gary Neville launches surprise defence of Diogo Dalot and names the THREE defenders Mauricio Pochettino should sell before Man United boo boy
Sports.content:
Gary Neville launches surprise defence of Diogo Dalot and names the THREE defenders Mauricio Pochettino should sell before Man United boo boy

Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.

The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.

But as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take over at Old Trafford, Neville urged the new manager not to immediately expel the defender, despite his drop-off in form.

'I think if he was in a decent back four he'd be alright,' Neville told Stick to United co-host Mark Goldbridge on Tuesday. 'But he's got a shocking back four alongside him.

'Positionally he's not great. He could be better on the ball. He could be better at everything he does. Of course he could. I just think he's such an easy target, Dalot. I honestly do.'

Neville admitted that sometimes he listens to his fellow Man United-supporting friends deriding Dalot and wonders 'are they watching something that I don't see?'

Gary Neville has defended Man United star Diogo Dalot - arguing that he has team-mates who are far weaker

The Portugal international has come in for heavy criticism from supporters this season

But in his opinion, there are three defenders that he would let go in the 'first wave' of changes in Manchester.

'I'd be getting (Noussair) Mazraoui well gone before him,' he continued. 'I'd be getting (Lisandro) Martinez gone well before him. I'll be getting (Matthijs) De Ligt gone well before him.

'(De Ligt has) got one big problem. He doesn’t play football. If a player is injury prone and doesn't play football, just because he hasn't played doesn't mean to say that he should go above a player who's played every single week and he's throwing his hand up. You want someone who's actually reliable and play. De Ligt has to go. De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui.'

Another stalwart in the team that Neville was keen to have a second chance under Pochettino was Luke Shaw.

'He will keep Shaw because he knows him and he'll probably get the best out of him. The problem with Luke is injuries,' he added. 'So he'll have to manage him. So he'll have to bring a left back in. But let's just say who he'll keep.

'He'll keep Shaw. He'll keep (Harry) Maguire because he'll trust him and he'll think that he's basically a soldier and someone who can do a job for him.

'He'll keep (Leny) Yoro because I think he'll think "I've got something there that I can work with". (But) I think he's a little bit gangly, all over the place right now. And he looks like he's going to slip every time. He's got that sort of Bambi-on-ice (look).

'Physically what will happen is with Yoro, he'll go one way or the other. I like the fact he's been brought into the French team. It tells me sometimes you just have got to connect the dots and think, "okay, well, if they think he's good, then we must be missing something here because we're not seeing it yet, are we?".'

Neville went on to suggest that Yoro was lacking the connection within his body that Premier League rivals such as Jeremy Jacquet are already able to harness – something Sir Alex Ferguson had identified in Rio Ferdinand when he was at West Ham.

Like Ferdinand, Neville backed Yoro to flourish as he taps into that connection and improves his strength and stability.

'So Yoro he will keep: Yoro, Maguire and Shaw I think he'll keep and I think he'll keep Dalot. To start with,' Neville said. 'He'll have to bring in three defenders to go above them. Let's be clear. He'll have to bring in three defenders.

'Mazraoui I would lose, De Ligt I would lose because he's injury prone. Martinez 100 per cent. 100 per cent. 100 per cent.'

As well as struggling for form this season, Martinez has been a challenging presence in the Man United squad this term, boldly calling out the Man United hierarchy during a firebrand interview last month.

Neville was more interested in new head coach Mauricio Pochettino despatching Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt

Lisandro Martinez has been an unsettled presence in the side this season and hit out at the club's recruiting last month

The Argentina star implied that he was disappointed with the club's recruitment strategy over the summer, and was forced to hold clear-the-air talks to smooth his return to the side.

Neville added that he would send Ayden Heaven on loan to get experience in the lower divisions to 'build' his ability up, as it was borderline 'unfair' to be 'putting him in' the side at present.

But not all of the changes can come quickly for Pochettino, who has little time before taking charge of Man United against Liverpool at Anfield this weekend.

'First wave, end of the season,' Neville clarified of what he believes Pochettino's plan for change will be. 'No, he can't get rid of (them all) in January.

'He has to bring one or two defenders in January if he can. But he can't get rid of all those in his first wave. He's only got one month till January.'

The drawn-out process of sacking Carrick began last week when Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada flew to Monaco for talks with co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer ownership group.

While his future was on the chopping block, Carrick held training sessions at Carrington before the axe finally swung last Thursday.

Pochettino was appointed days later and gave a tearful farewell press conference ahead of his penultimate game with the United States national team on Saturday.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he told the press. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay. I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'

Sports.title: Tearful John Daly opens up on $1.65m gambling binges, how his fiancee 'saved his life'... and what 'p***es him off' about Trump's second term
Sports.content:
Golf legend John Daly fought back tears as he detailed losing $1.65 million on one night in Las Vegas, how he was rescued by his fiancee, and why he was left 'p***ed off' in the wake of the midterm elections.

The 60-year-old is one of golf's most colorful characters. He won two major championships but is perhaps better known for his garish outfits, his booming drives, his diet and his annual pilgrimage to Augusta for meet-and-greets during the Masters.

During a remarkable life, Daly has battled alcoholism, cancer and sepsis - following a spider bite - and undergone more than a dozen surgeries in the past decade.

He has compared himself to 'Lazarus' and one observer once claimed that over 18 holes, Daly put away 21 cigarettes, 12 Diet Cokes and six packets of M&Ms.

The American has now appeared on Fox's Hang out with Sean Hannity, where he detailed - among other things - a night in Las Vegas in 2005, when he went on a million-dollar gambling binge.

Daly hit the casinos following the WGC-American Express Championship, when he lost to Tiger Woods in a sudden-death playoff after three-putting from 15 feet.

Golf legend John Daly fought back tears during an interview on Fox with Sean Hannity

Daly, seen here smoking at the 2023 Open Championship, remains one of golf's cult heroes

'I love him... as a human being, as a father, as a family guy,' Daly said of President Trump

Daly grew emotional as he credited his partner of two decades, Anna, for 'saving his life'

'I told my caddie and I told everybody: "Look, man, I should have won that damn tournament. I don't want this money. I'm going to go to Wynn and play the $5,000 slot machine. And if I win, I win. If I don't, I don't,' he told Hannity.

Daly earned $750,000 by finishing second in the tournament but he ended up losing $1.65 million over five hours. 'When you're pulling $5,000 a pull, it doesn't take long,' he said.

The golf legend also paid tribute to Donald Trump and railed against his political opponents in the wake of the midterm elections, when the Republicans were on the wrong end of a blue tsunami.

'I love him. Love him as a human being, as a father, as a family guy, and the most powerful man in the world trying to protect America,' Daly said.

'He's already got his life set and money. He doesn't care about money. Not at all, actually. Now let's take the other side of that.

'The other side, and you know who I'm talking about, all they care about is filling their pockets.

'And that just really p***es me off. They're going to spend two years trying to impeach him, [Secretary of War] Pete [Hegseth], trying to impeach everybody.

'And what I don't understand is the people voted for these people with no policies.'

The 60-year-old wore Hooters-themed trousers during the second round of The Open in 2023

Daly's two major wins came at the 1991 PGA Championship and the 1995 Open Championship

During the interview with Hannity, Daly grew emotional as he credited his partner of two decades, Anna Cladakis, for 'saving his life.'

'When you find peace with your heart and you find somebody like Anna, 20 years I've been with her, and you're at peace with your life,' he said.

'She was going through a tough time. I was going through a really tough time.

'But when you get someone like her homeschooling your child, taking care of me, doing things that no woman would ever do for me, I mean, she saved my life.'

Sports.title: Man United Confidential: Mauricio Pochettino to be given money to spend in January as club target recruits in THREE positions, surprise at popular coach's sacking and latest on JJ Gabriel's move to Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Man United Confidential: Mauricio Pochettino to be given money to spend in January as club target recruits in THREE positions, surprise at popular coach's sacking and latest on JJ Gabriel's move to Real Madrid

Mauricio Pochettino’s whirlwind arrival as Manchester United’s new head coach has left little time to work out where he will live – but a key factor in that decision will be his beloved dog Sansa.

Pochettino will leave the TQL Stadium in Cincinnati after the USA’s game against Haiti in the early hours of Wednesday morning and go straight to the airport to catch an eight-hour flight to Manchester on board a private jet paid for by United.

The club will also provide him with somewhere to live as he settles into the new job and finds a more permanent residence.

The 54-year-old, who also has a home in Barcelona, is said to have lived just outside London when he was Tottenham manager and then spent the entirety of his 18-month spell as Paris Saint-Germain boss in a luxury hotel.

Pochettino lived in Knightsbridge while he was in charge of Chelsea, and revealed that he enjoyed getting feedback from fans while out on his daily 90-minute dog walks with Sansa.

He named the Rhodesian Ridgeback after a character from Game of Thrones and has even given the dog her own Instagram account.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of the US national team for the final time in the early hours of Wednesday morning, then head straight to Manchester on a private jet

Pochettino (pictured with his son Maurizio) will have to find accommodation which suits his dog Sansa, a Rhodesian Ridgeback (Source: Instagram/pochettino)

Describing the difficulty of Spurs playing on a Saturday night in 2018, he said: ‘At 7pm, I am normally on my sofa with my dog Sansa watching the Spanish league because they start at 7.45pm, or France because Ligue 1 starts at 8pm, or Italy, or different games.

‘It will be so strange for my dog. Not for me but my dog. “Where is my dad?” she is going to say. She is beautiful and I am in love with her.’

The living habits of United bosses have varied over the years. Sir Alex Ferguson, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Ruben Amorim favoured Wilmslow and Alderley Edge, David Moyes remained further afield in Lytham, Louis van Gaal and Erik ten Hag chose Hale, and Jose Mourinho famously spent 895 days at the Lowry Hotel in Manchester (where dogs can stay for an additional £30).

Maur the merrier

United have no plans to change the timings for Wednesday’s training session, even though Pochettino and four of his backroom team may not arrive at Carrington until the early afternoon.

The private jet carrying the Argentine, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott should touch down from Cincinnati around noon.

An advance party of three more coaches – Pochettino’s assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, and his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino – have been in Manchester since Sunday after they were released early by the US Soccer Federation as a gesture of goodwill following the 6-0 first-leg win over Haiti in the quarter-finals of the North American equivalent of the Nations League.

They took training on Tuesday as United’s players continue to report back from international duty, and will also oversee the session on Wednesday morning after United decided not to reschedule it so Pochettino could be present.

The Argentine will be firmly hands-on from Thursday, though, as he prepares for his first game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Pochettino, who will speak to club media shortly after his arrival before conducting his first press conference on Friday, has faced Liverpool 19 times in his managerial career, losing 11 games, drawing five and winning three.

Pochettino's assistant Jesus Perez (right) has been in Manchester since Sunday and took training on Tuesday

Strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya - the first woman to be part of United's backroom staff - will travel with Pochettino to Manchester following the Haiti game

Dosh for the new boss

Pochettino will inherit a team in the relegation zone – which could even be bottom of the Premier League by kick-off on Sunday – and it’s understood he will be given modest funds to improve his squad in the January transfer window.

United are in desperate need of a left back and a striker, having failed to sign cover in both positions in the summer.

One potential target may be US centre forward Folarin Balogun who has prospered under Pochettino but only started once for Monaco this season after a summer move to Everton fell through. United sources say the new head coach will have input in the weeks ahead before a clearer plan emerges.

United also want a centre back after Confidential revealed last week that Fulham’s Calvin Bassey and Nathan Collins, of Brentford, are two options being considered.

It’s possible that one of those deals may have to be a loan, however, with United’s delicate financial situation set to be spelt out in black and white when the results from the first quarter of the financial year are released on Thursday.

Although Pochettino is going to have money for new players, United will have to be smart in their transfer dealings and spend wisely.

In the short term, Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford may be available again for the first time in more than a month against Liverpool.

However, there is a concern over Patrick Dorgu who was deemed to be unfit for international duty with Denmark, even though he returned to action for Michael Carrick’s final game after a month-and-a-half out with a hamstring injury and headed a stoppage-time equaliser in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Fulham's Calvin Bassey (right) is among the centre-back options United are considering

Marcus Rashford may be available for the first time in more than a month against Liverpool

Travesty for Travis

It was the departure of Travis Binnion, rather than Carrick, that raised the most eyebrows among figures working in football over the past few days.

Agents and first-team players privately described their surprise at seeing Binnion – a long-time academy figure before stepping up to the first team to help Darren Fletcher as interim and then Carrick – leave the club.

United have cleaned house for the arrival of Pochettino’s backroom team, and Binnion was one of those who paid the price.

A popular figure in the dressing room, Joshua Zirkzee, Benjamin Sesko and Kobbie Mainoo are among the players who are known to have enjoyed working with Binnion.

Despite stepping up to the first team, where he would watch matches from the press box alongside United’s team of analysts, Binnion remained in contact with numerous academy player representatives to ensure their development was progressing as planned.

Binnion, who first arrived in 2019 as an Under 16s coach and progressed to the Under 18s, Under 21s and then head of player development and coaching, isn’t expected to be out of the game for too long though.

Agency sources believe rival Premier League academies will move quickly to recruit him, with Everton seen as one potential landing spot. United’s former academy head Nick Cox is now Everton technical director and has already recruited Dave Hughes and Tom Curtis, who worked under Binnion at United.

A popular figure in the dressing room, Joshua Zirkzee, Benjamin Sesko and Kobbie Mainoo are among the players who enjoyed working with Travis Binnion (pictured)

Stay or go – you decided!

Your responses to our 36-man Manchester United squad audit have made for interesting reading over the last week.

Confidential pored over the first-team squad, as well as numerous rising stars in the academy, that Pochettino and his staff will quickly have to run the rule over.

While some of the voting went as expected – your votes demonstrated an overwhelming desire among the fanbase to see Noussair Mazraoui, Diogo Dalot, Shaw and Harry Maguire leave this summer – there were a few surprises.

Many voted for captain Bruno Fernandes, who just recently rejected a second contract extension offer, to be moved on, along with Rashford. Amad Diallo and summer signing Andrey Santos are two who divide opinion, but both made the cut.

Check out the full squad audit HERE to see how others voted and leave your own verdict!

Real deal for JJ

Confidential understands JJ Gabriel’s representatives held fresh talks with Real Madrid at the club’s training ground on Monday as a move to the Santiago Bernabeu edges ever closer.

Now that Gabriel has officially announced a partnership with Epic Sports Agency, his agent Ali Barat is leading negotiations and has been at Real’s Valdebebas headquarters along with the 16-year-old and his family.

The player and the Spanish giants are hoping to get a move over the line, even though United currently own Gabriel's registration for the season and continue to play hardball.

JJ Gabriel's representatives have held fresh talks with Real Madrid as his move to the Bernabeu edges closer

Fergie supports ‘evil’ Eric

Eric Cantona and Sir Alex Ferguson will reunite next month at a special screening of the Frenchman’s new documentary.

Cantona: Flower of Evil won rave reviews in France and is now heading to the UK, with a one-night-only panel featuring Cantona and Ferguson at Aviva Studios in Manchester on December 7.

The documentary film digs deeper into how Ferguson channelled Cantona’s brilliance and honed his explosiveness – a trait that had seen him branded ‘unmanageable’ in France. Tickets range from £156 all the way up to £1,000. You can purchase them here.

Sports.title: Declan Rice agrees new five-year Arsenal contract: Star to join Bukayo Saka as Gunners' highest-paid player at over £350,000-per-week... with goalkeeper David Raya set to sign long-term deal to stay too
Sports.content:
Declan Rice agrees new five-year Arsenal contract: Star to join Bukayo Saka as Gunners' highest-paid player at over £350,000-per-week... with goalkeeper David Raya set to sign long-term deal to stay too

Declan Rice has agreed a new five-year deal at Arsenal that will run until the summer of 2031 - with goalkeeper David Raya set to join him in committing his future to the club.

The England midfielder is expected to sign the new contract soon, which is set to put him alongside Bukayo Saka as Arsenal's top earner. Saka is on a deal worth over £350,000 a week.

And Raya, 31, is understood to have agreed a deal in principle to extend his terms. Both players' existing deals expire in 2028.

Rice joined Arsenal in 2023 for £105million from West Ham and has established himself as the fulcrum of their midfield, helping steer them to the Premier League title last season.

The 27-year-old played 55 games in all competitions last season as the Gunners reached their first Champions League final since 2006, but lost out to Paris Saint-Germain.

His contract talks have been ongoing from at least March and are now finalised.

Raya joined Arsenal from Brentford on loan in the same summer, and signed a permanent deal a year later.

Declan Rice has agreed a new-five year deal at Arsenal that will run until the summer of 2031

David Raya has agreed a deal in principle to stay on, with his current deal expiring in 2028

Rice had confirmed a new deal was close over the weekend when speaking on international duty with England.

'I've been extremely lucky that I've managed to play at such a consistent level throughout my career.

'I've always been stable in the clubs I've been at.

'A new contract is hopefully on the horizon soon.

'I'm extremely lucky that I'm at a club like Arsenal, where my manager [Mikel Arteta] and my team-mates put so much energy in me.

'I'm extremely lucky I don't have to think about that stuff.'

Sports.title: South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus slapped with SIX-MATCH BAN over controversial 'match-fixing' tirade
Sports.content:
South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has been handed a mammoth six-match ban with immediate effect after World Rugby cracked down on his shock ‘match fixing’ press conference claims.

Ahead of his team’s Nations Championship clash with Ireland in Dublin on Sunday, Erasmus launched into a tirade to journalists on Monday. It came on the back of his team’s 21-19 loss to France.

Erasmus claimed the officials in that game in Paris had missed 17 knee-drop tackles committed on his side, suggesting that such incidents amounted to ‘match fixing’ and ‘manipulation of the game’.

He also predicted Ireland No 10 Sam Prendergast would escape a ban after being cited for a hip-drop tackle against Fiji and be available to face his double world champion Springboks. ‘The TMO doesn’t come in once. I’m not saying he’s wrong. I’m saying if he didn’t see it. It must be a technology problem,’ said Erasmus.

‘If he saw it and he decided not to act on it, is that not match-fixing? Is that not interfering with the outcome of a game?’

World Rugby, the game’s governing body, immediately launched an investigation and on Tuesday, confirmed they had hit Erasmus with a tough sanction. It means he will miss the Ireland game and his team’s Nations Championship finals weekend clash with an opponent yet to be determined as well as four more matches in 2027.

World Rugby said: ‘The sanction follows a review of wide-ranging comments made by Erasmus at a media conference this week concerning officiating during the Springboks’ Nations Championship match against France last Friday.

Rassie Erasmus will miss the rest of the Nations Championship after his tirade

'An independent panel imposed the sanction under World Rugby’s match official abuse sanction process which provides a clear, consistent framework for addressing public criticism of match officials, particularly comments that may undermine the integrity of individuals or the sport, or fuel online abuse.

‘Having considered the comments which related to the match TMO, the panel determined the comments suggest that match officials acted with bias/prejudice or deliberately influenced the outcome of a match. A reasonable person would conclude the conduct constituted an unacceptable attack on the credibility and competence of the match officials.

‘In respect to the sanction, the panel determined the conduct clearly amounts to disrespecting the authority of the match officials by impugning their integrity.

'Therefore, the panel reviewed a number of elements of the commentary including the timing and reach of the statements, combined with the allegations of bias or bad faith, and found the comments attracted a six-match automatic suspension.’

Erasmus has a poor past disciplinary record which would no doubt have played a part in his latest ban. After targeting the Australian referee Nic Berry during the 2021 British & Irish Lions tour of South Africa, Erasmus was suspended for two months.

South Africa said in a statement they are requesting a full misconduct hearing for Erasmus so that he can ‘contextualise his comments and assure the panel it was not his intention to allege any match official had acted with ulterior motives.’

The Springboks added that they trusted ‘such a hearing could be expedited considering the seriousness of the charge and will not make any further comment until the hearing could be completed.’

Sports.title: Chelsea's Malo Gusto named 'biggest disappointment of the Zidane era'... and Liverpool's £123m man Bradley Barcola 'lacked accuracy and composure' in damning verdict on France's Premier League stars
Sports.content:
Chelsea's Malo Gusto named 'biggest disappointment of the Zidane era'... and Liverpool's £123m man Bradley Barcola 'lacked accuracy and composure' in damning verdict on France's Premier League stars

The French media have come down hard on a number of Premier League players in the national team after less than impressive displays under new coach Zinedine Zidane.

Over the break France scraped a 2-1 win against Turkey in the Nations League but only after an unexpected 3-1 loss to Italy at the San Siro.

And among the team's most glaring underperformers – according to some observers in France – were Chelsea's Malo Gusto, Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert and Liverpool's £123million summer signing Bradley Barcola.

French outlet RMC Sport was particularly critical of the pair, with journalist Alexandre Jaquin describing Gusto as 'probably the one who disappointed the most during this second international window of the Zidane era'.

Jaquin added: 'Fielded in Italy despite little playing time with Chelsea, the right-back completely fell into the San Siro furnace.

Malo Gusto struggled has been under fire from the French media after a string of poor performances under Zinedine Zidane

The honeymoon period is over for Zidane, according to French media

'Overwhelmed by his opponents' energy and little helped by Michael Olise's lack of defensive defense, the former Lyon player lived a nightmare in Lombardy, notably conceding a penalty. A match quickly erased from his memory.'

RMC was not much kinder to Barcola as well, concluding: 'The Liverpool winger was one of the few to start both matches in November. But in the end, it didn't really take off, neither in Italy nor against Turkey.

'Sometimes on his left flank, sometimes in a false nine, the former PSG supersub was often imprecise in his final moves. Like his failed one-on-one against the Turks, the Lyon native lacked accuracy and composure to make the opposing goal tremble.'

Even newcomer Adrien Truffert was not afforded some sympathy as Jaquin said: 'After a rather satisfying debut in October, the Bournemouth left-back benefited from the trust of Zinedine Zidane, who played him in Italy. But despite his efforts, the Cherries player delivered a very mixed performance.'

This recent criticism adds to growing dissatisfaction in France with the overall state of the national team under Zidane.

Liverpool's £123million man is yet to make a major impact for club or country so far this season

Journalist Walid Acherchour made his feelings known on the After Foot programme, saying: 'Zidane hit a wall of reality with this second international break... I found the attitude of some individuals against Turkey to be very poor.

'In the second half against Italy and in the match against Turkey, how do you manage without the ball when you're being torn apart in midfield? Zidane will have to work on all these questions.'

Acherchour closed by saying bluntly: 'The honeymoon is over.'

After an ultimately disappointing World Cup in which the French were again by Spain in a major semi-final – following their Euro 2024 exit – long-term manager Didier Deschamps left after 14 years in charge.

Legendary midfielder Zidane succeeded him in the summer and has already led France to the top of their Nations League group – but some of his players may have to go much further to win over their critics.

Sports.title: Top jockey Nico de Boinville escorted off racetrack after death threat following defeats on two favourites
Sports.content:
Top jockey Nico de Boinville escorted off racetrack after death threat following defeats on two favourites

Jockey Nico de Boinville was given extra security and escorted off a racetrack in West Sussex after receiving a death threat on the back of a poor result.

The 37-year-old was beaten in two races that he was favourite to triumph at Plumpton with even-money shot Ginolo, who finished fifth, and Ionian, who came third in the 2m1f handicap chase despite being favourite.

After, security raced onto the course to drag him away, which came as a surprise to the jockey.

'After the first race yesterday the security at Plumpton – they're very good, top-level people who dealt with the Brighton bombings and things like that – came in and dragged me out,' he told Racing HQ. 'They said there's been a threat called in to me, so I needed security for the rest of the day.

'The threat came into the yard and then the PJA and then BHA, and then it gets called through to the racecourse. It's the trials and tribulations of being a jockey.

'It's bizarre. I'm going to work like everyone else and you don't expect that. I feel sorry for whoever it was and I hope they get the help they need. It was probably because I got beat.'

Jockey Nico de Boinville was given extra security after receiving a death threat on Monday

The former Cheltenham Gold Cup winner has enjoyed vast success in the sport, riding 18 Cheltenham winners in total.

He struggled to replicate that success on Monday but will be back on the horse on Wednesday when he heads to Ffos Las to ride Old Park Star in his chasing debut.

Old Park Star represents one of De Boinville's Cheltenham successes, having taken the six-year-old to victory in the Supreme Novices' Hurdle last season.

Sports.title: Tiger Woods, 50, confirms stunning return to golf after wild two years of DUI drama, rehab and multiple surgeries
Sports.content:
Tiger Woods has confirmed he will make his long-awaited return to golf at next month's Hero World Challenge.

The 15-time major champion has not played a PGA Tour event since he missed the cut at The Open in 2024 at Royal Troon.

Since then, Woods has been beset by injuries and legal struggles. He ruptured an Achilles tendon and had a sixth and seventh back surgery before being arrested on suspicion of DUI earlier this year.

But on Tuesday, it was confirmed that Woods will tee it up at the Hero World Challenge, the tournament he hosts, which kicks off in the Bahamas on December 3.

Rickie Fowler and Gary Woodland were also added to the 20-player field, which includes the likes of Scottie Scheffler and Xander Schauffele.
