Relatives of two Trinidadians killed in a strike filed a similar suit in January over a strike that President Trump announced last year.

World.title: Cash Hidden in Forests? Hungary Goes After Corruption Under Orban
World.content:
Hungary’s new anti-corruption agency made an eye-catching splash last week when it released photographs of a table piled with bank notes worth nearly $20 million. The money, the agency said, had been found hidden in forests and farm buildings during a hunt for funds stolen during the long tenure of the country’s former prime minister, Viktor Orban.

This week, Hungary’s new leader, Peter Magyar, announced that the stacks of cash photographed by the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office, a new agency set up as part of what he calls “operation cleansing fire,” were just the “tip of the iceberg.”

To display the full volume of money ransacked by corrupt officials before Mr. Orban lost a general election in April, Mr. Magyar told Parliament on Monday, “You would have to put 10,000 tables next to each other.”

In his telling, the total amounts to more than 60 trillion Hungarian forint (more than $180 billion) — a staggering, and so far unproven, sum in a small Eastern European country whose total spending on defense last year was around only $5 billion.

World.title: Prince William Brings Climate Prize to India, in an Electric Rickshaw
World.content:
It was a royal chariot for the moment.

But when Prince William pulled up to the promenade in the Indian coastal city of Mumbai behind the wheels of a three-wheeled electric rickshaw, with Catherine, Princess of Wales, as his passenger, it was another point he was making. His argument was that the solutions to some of the most pressing environmental challenges, such as clean air, could come from scaling up technology that already exists.

That this year the heir to the British throne has brought his six-year-old Earthshot Prize, which aims to promote creative solutions to the climate crisis, to India seems fitting. This country, with its 1.4 billion people, is a frontier for both the devastating impact of an increasingly erratic climate (more than 80 percent of the region around Mumbai is in drought), and the search for ways to mitigate that impact.

The prize’s five winners were announced at a ceremony hosted by the Indian filmmaker Karan Johar. Each will receive one million pounds, about $1.3 million.

The organizers also hope to offer wider benefits to the winners, in the form of recognition and a connection to business and political leaders.

World.title: Congo Ebola Outbreak: How Fear and Mistrust Drive Community Spread
World.content:
Gorette Mbusi stood on her doorstep and wrestled with a question. Should she let her grandson be taken to the hospital?

Health workers had come to her village, in the eastern part of the Democratic Republic of Congo, to implore her to let them take the young man to a specialized Ebola facility in the nearby town of Nizi. But she was wary. She had already lost two family members, including her daughter, who had been transported to the hospital and then died.

Now, her grandson was sick.

“I don’t know where this sickness is coming from that is killing my family,” she said. “I feel abandoned.”

Ms. Mbusi’s dilemma reflects a central challenge for health workers as they struggle to contain the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record — how to stop people from passing the disease to loved ones at home.

World.title: Tracking China’s War of Words Against Japan
World.content:
When China’s leader, Xi Jinping, met with President Trump at the White House earlier this fall, the two leaders toasted to friendly relations.

But in private, Mr. Xi offered Mr. Trump a stark warning about Japan, a U.S. ally, according to two officials briefed on the talks, who requested anonymity to discuss private conversations. Mr. Xi told Mr. Trump that Japan’s recent military buildup threatened to destabilize Asia, the officials said, and that Mr. Trump should be cautious about working with Japan’s prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, describing her as a “militarist.”

The warning from Mr. Xi was part of a broader effort by China to isolate and undermine Japan after Ms. Takaichi said last year that Japan could be forced to defend Taiwan in case of a Chinese invasion. China considers Taiwan, a self-governed democracy that lies just 69 miles from Japan’s westernmost island, part of its territory.

World.title: From Failed Businessman to Accused Plotter in the Killing of Haiti’s Leader
World.content:
He claimed to be a Florida doctor and pastor, but there is no record of him having a U.S. medical degree or leading a church.

He filed for bankruptcy, but his problems really began when he started promoting and broadcasting plans to become Haiti’s president, calling himself the country’s savior and boasting that he had the backing of the U.S. government.

Now, Christian Emmanuel Sanon is on trial in Miami, accused by federal prosecutors of conspiring to kidnap or kill the last elected president of Haiti, Jovenel Moïse, who was assassinated in his bedroom in July 2021.

In court, Mr. Sanon, dressed in a suit and tie, has the bearing of a statesman. But prosecutors say the 67-year-old Haitian American was nothing more than a con man.

World.title: Ukraine Attacks Kerch Bridge Linking Russia to Occupied Crimea
World.content:
For years, Ukraine has had a bull’s-eye on the only bridge linking the occupied Crimean Peninsula to Russia.

After Moscow used Crimea as a springboard to launch its all-out invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Kyiv bombed the bridge that year with explosives hidden in a truck. The next year, Ukraine attacked it with unmanned naval vessels. Two years after that, it dispatched covert operatives to try to bring the bridge down by planting explosives on undersea support pillars.

The 12-mile-long structure, the Kerch Strait Bridge, survived it all, a powerful if scarred symbol of Moscow’s control of Crimea, which Russia illegally annexed in 2014. But before dawn on Tuesday, Ukraine struck its biggest blow yet, sending a significant section of the bridge into the sea after a series of drone and missile attacks.

In a statement about the bridge, the Ukrainian military command said, “Russia built a myth around it as a symbol of Crimea being ‘Russian forever.’”

World.title: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
World.content:
Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making.

Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge has collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Moscow's war effort.

The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before" and that Russian President Vladimir Putin had been briefed on the overnight attack.

Elsewhere, Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges - key crossings over the Dnipro River - had been closed after Russia hit Ukraine's capital overnight.

The Southern bridge partially reopened on Tuesday, Klitschko said.

Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good.

While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight.

The Crimean Bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and illegally annexed Ukraine's southern peninsula in 2014.

The $3.6bn (Â£2.7bn) piece of infrastructure is widely seen in Russia and Ukraine as Putin's personal pet project: His close tycoon friend Arkady Rotenberg built it, and then Putin personally opened it by driving a lorry over it in May 2018.

World.title: How the attack on Crimean Bridge unfolded
World.content:
Moscow uses Crimea as a military base, with airbases, troop concentrations, training grounds and artillery stockpiles. From there it also carries out strikes on the rest of the country and resupplies its troops in southern Ukraine.

The attack comes after a summer of frequent strikes on Crimea, dictated by Ukraine's stated goal of cutting the peninsula off from Russia. At the time, Kyiv vowed to turn the Crimean Peninsula "into an island".

Now - although it is too early to speak of a complete blockade of Crimea â the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis has increased significantly.

There is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions. However, Ukraine has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar, which has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo.

Moscow can also still utilise the ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited - and anything on the Black Sea has become vulnerable to attack. Resupplying Crimea by sea is risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area.

In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge - particularly its enormous arch - may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for ports in the Sea of Azov, including the occupied cities of Mariupol and Berdyansk.

Away from the operational value of the damage to the bridge, the symbolic significance remains.

In 2018, Putin triumphantly drove over the bridge representing the unification of Russia and Crimea in a Russian-made truck. That section of the road now lays on the seabed.

Nearly five years since he launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Putin continues to wreak destruction on Ukraine's civilian population, but his most prized symbols of power are increasingly threatened by Kyiv's reach.

World.title: Jensen Huang pushes Nvidia comeback after board rejects pressure to reinstate ex-boss
World.content:
Jensen Huang said he would be "honoured" to return as the boss of tech giant Nvidia, in his first public comments since his shock resignation.

"I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely," Huang said on X, days after reports he had extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy.

But he said he had an "outpouring" of calls from company employees, investors and others calling for him to return as CEO of Nvidia.

As the BBC reported on Monday, Nvidia's board is not considering bringing him back to lead the company.

The prospect of Huang returning at this point looks unlikely.

The company's board is investigating his conduct, which includes an alleged affair with an Nvidia executive.

The AI chip giant is set to report its financial results later on Tuesday, during which the company's interim chief executive, Collette Kress, may address the situation with Huang.

Beyond the internal Nvidia investigation, Huang's affair with a woman suspected of being an asset for Beijing is set to see the billionaire questioned before multiple committees of US lawmakers in the weeks ahead.

The Nvidia founder said he had "made serious mistakes in my personal life".

Nonetheless, Huang's statement appeared to show some hope he would be able to move past the major corporate scandal.

Huang said people have continued to "reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics".

"If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO," Huang added.

Many technology executives in recent days have praised Huang's role in the artificial intelligence boom. A petition began circulating online over the weekend calling for his reinstatement at the company.

Yet, by Monday, many executives were not openly calling for Huang's return.

Brad Gerstner, a major tech investor who knows Huang personally and also holds a significant stake in Nvidia, last week wrote an open letter saying that Nvidia could consider Huang's reinstatement.

On Monday, Gerstner said during an event hosted by Semafor that his letter had been misunderstood and the investigation into Huang's conduct needed to run its course.

While Gerstner questioned the facts around Huang's departure, he added: "I don't know to what degree he misled the board. If I was on a board I would take that very seriously. Let's be clear no one is above the law."

World.title: Trump lands in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents
World.content:
President Trump has arrived in the Philippines' capital on the first leg of a trip to Asia, which will end in a meeting in China with its President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin.

A red carpet was rolled out for Trump as he walked off Air Force One in Manila. A band played one of his favourite songs, Y.M.C.A., before he was whisked away by helicopter to a hotel.

Trump's first meeting at the Asean Summit was with America's partners in the Quad - India's Narendra Modi, whom he described as a "very tough man", Japan's Sanae Takaichi, who "may be even tougher", and Australia's Anthony Albanese.

"Our countries are the four corners of the free, open, stable, prosperous Indo-Pacific," the US president said.

"We have outstanding relationships and co-ordinate closely... my phone is always open," Trump added.

Many countries in South East Asia have been hit hard by Donald Trump's tariffs and his war on Iran - but their exports to the US rose 30% last year thanks to the AI boom for which the region manufactures many of the components.

The US is hoping to draw more countries here into its "Pax Silica" tech and AI ecosystem, and away from China.

But China's huge influence in this region cannot easily be challenged, and certainly not in the few hours Trump is in the Philippines.

After an overnight stay in Manila, the US president will fly to Shenzhen in China to attend a summit of Asia Pacific leaders and have nuclear talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.

Asked if he would also be open to a one-on-one meeting with Putin, Trump said: "If it's available, I would".

World.title: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
World.content:
After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths.

The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months.

Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, announced that Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles elimination status, attributing the resurgence in the region to persistent "gaps in vaccination".

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was committed to "regaining measles elimination status" by expanding access to vaccines.

The US has seen 5,400 cases of measles this year alone, with 10 measles-related deaths, the most the country has seen since the 1990s.

The measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. The extremely contagious virus can be fatal, and some patients can experience long-term complications including encephalitis and immune amnesia, which resets the immune system, leaving it with only limited ability to respond to new infections.

The US recommends two measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) shots for children between ages one and six, which is 97% effective in protecting against the illness.

PAHO, a group within the World Health Organization, revoked the US's measles-elimination after determining that the virus had circulated nonstop for more than a year.

"These figures are a serious warning for our region," PAHO's director Barbosa said at a news conference on Tuesday. "Measles is resurging globally amid persistent gaps in vaccination."

He added that Canada, which lost its status of having eliminated measles last year after seeing several large outbreaks, has made strides this year to interrupt transmission.

Daniel Salas, the executive manager of immunisations at PAHO, said that the US and others who lost elimination status would be required to submit corrective action plans outlining how they would attempt to improve vaccination rates.

US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr Kennedy has attempted to make a series of sweeping changes to US vaccine recommendations and policies. The vaccine sceptic has also frequently cast doubt on the safety of MMR shot, as vaccination rates have declined across the US in recent years.

Kennedy has argued that the rise in measles cases started before he took the helm at HHS and that neighbouring countries have also seen more infections.

Responding to Tuesday's announcement, the CDC said the agency and its partners were "committed to stopping measles outbreaks, protecting Americans, and regaining measles elimination status".

"Together, we will encourage MMR vaccination, expand access to vaccines, and help communities close gaps in protection," the agency said.

CDC Director Erica Schwartz said the measles elimination designation was not what protected Americans.

"Vaccination does," she said. "We know where transmission is occurring and we've invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach those communities."

The UK, Spain and Austria were among European nations that lost their measles-free status earlier this year, along with countries including Russia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

World.title: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
World.content:
A Palestinian woman in her 70s has been shot dead, and several other people wounded, in a village in the occupied West Bank where Israeli settlers recently moved in, the Palestinian health ministry says.

There are conflicting accounts of what happened. Local Palestinians said there was an attack by settlers in part of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho, which is meant to be under the full control of the Palestinian Authority.

According to the Israeli army, there was a Palestinian car-ramming attack on an Israeli vehicle. It said rocks were then thrown at the Israelis, who opened fire in response. It did not mention the fatal shooting of a woman.

There have been high tensions in the area since a group of settlers recently set up a new outpost.

They moved into eight houses in the village on 4 November after buying them, they have said, in a secretive operation. The properties are in an area where Israel retains full security control.

All settlements are illegal under international law.

World.title: 'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge
World.content:
The alarms warning of a ballistic missile threat went off just before 23:30 on Monday in Kyiv. Moments later came the boom of explosions.

Once again, the main bridges over the broad River Dnipro that cuts through the city were the target and this time the Russian missiles hit what they wanted.

Close to one end of the Pivnichnyi (Northern) bridge there is a large crater and in the pouring rain, water now rushes through it to the river below. Chunks of tarmac and metal are scattered around.

At its broadest point, the jagged hole is about eight metres wide.

The crossing is closed to all traffic apart from the occasional fire engine or police car passing at high speed. By contrast, nearby roads are jammed with cars and trucks, forced to take long detours.

Anyone in a hurry to move around this city has to walk, or cycle, across the bridge, picking their way through the wreckage. In the miserable weather, that also means getting very wet.

Masha and her family moved to a flat next to the bridge because they had been living by a power plant that kept getting hit by Russian missiles.

Last night, she was in the kitchen of their new place when the Russians struck the bridge. She thought her windows would be blown out of their frames by the explosions.

"It was really scary. We had no idea they'd hit here so much. It's like we're cursed," Masha told me, describing grabbing her child and running into the corridor for protection.

But somehow, she still managed to sound cheerful.

"It's difficult, but we're used to it. And we try to take the positive from everything. Like: we survived today! So we can be happy about that."

World.title: Indian woman gang-raped while pregnant in 2002 'heartbroken' after two perpetrators bailed
World.content:
The article has details that some readers may find disturbing

A pregnant Muslim woman who was gang-raped and saw 14 family members murdered during the 2002 Gujarat riots has spoken of her "pain, shock and disbelief" after two of her rapists were recently granted bail.

Bilkis Bano said in a statement that she heard about the top court order through press reports and vowed to fight back.

The freed men are from a group of 11 convicts - part of a Hindu mob - serving life terms for the attack on Bano.

All the men were also freed in 2022 after a Gujarat government order. That decision, and the celebrations as they left prison, caused global outrage. In 2024, the Supreme Court overturned the order.

In a short three-page order dated 28 October, the Supreme Court granted bail to Bipinchand Kanaiyalal Joshi and Pradip Ramanlal Modhiya and suspended their sentences while their petition challenging a 2017 Bombay High Court order is being heard.

The judges explained that the early release was because the two convicts "have been under incarceration for a period of more than 17 years" and "that one of the appellants has a severe handicap".

On Tuesday, Bano's lawyer Shobha Gupta told the BBC that the news of Joshi and Modhiya's release had left "Bilkis heartbroken".

"She has to restart her battle for justice. She had no information that this case was coming up in the Supreme Court. What is troubling for us is that every time something like this happens, we worry that it could affect her faith in judiciary."

World.title: I’ll release N40m to every ward monthly if elected – YPP presidential candidate
World.content:
The presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party (YPP), Peter Agada, has pledged to release N40 million to each of Nigeria’s 8,809 wards every month if elected president in the 2027 general election.

Mr Agada, an architect, said the funds would serve as seed capital for grassroots development, adding that his administration would prioritise making each ward economically independent and promoting balanced economic growth across the country.

He made the pledge on Monday while appearing on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he discussed his plans for the country if elected president.

The presidential candidate also promised to involve local professionals in executing infrastructure projects, saying his first task after inauguration would be to engage professionals to develop a master plan for each ward.

He said each ward would have a target of engaging 350 people, including architects, engineers, town planners, road construction workers, artisans, doctors and nurses.

“Like I said, every ward has a 350 person target. Now, this 350 persons as architects, engineers, town planners, road construction people, artisans, doctors, nurses. So you see, by the time you’re done setting up these ward areas and putting in that funding, because we are sending in about N40 million from our sources.

“We’re sending in N40 million to these wards every month as seed capital. You have now set up a system, an economic system that can grow on its own and make that ward an independent ward for development,” he said

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) cleared 18 candidates for the presidential election scheduled for 16 January 2027.

Some of the other presidential hopefuls aside from Mr Agada include President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC), who is seeking a second term, Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Peter Obi of Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Sandy Onor (PDP), Omoyele Sowore (AAC), former Cross River Governor Donald Duke (PRP), and Adewole Adebayo (SDP).

Criticises Tinubu’s borrowing

Mr Agada also criticised President Tinubu’s borrowings, promising that his administration would rely less on foreign loans than the incumbent government.

The presidential candidate said he was not opposed to borrowing but argued that the current administration was borrowing excessively. He added that his government would focus on reducing project costs rather than accumulating more debt.

To achieve this, he proposed establishing a National Council on Procurement to monitor the costs of government projects and ensure proper documentation.

“I would not borrow as much as they’re doing. I don’t have a problem with borrowing, all right? They are borrowing too much, and I would save costs rather than borrowing. I’ve always been an advocate for setting up the National Council on Procurement,” he said.

The YPP candidate also alleged that several projects undertaken by the Tinubu administration had been overinflated, referencing the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway as an example.

He said his administration would address the practice by ensuring proper monitoring of project costs.

Tinubu’s borrowing plans

The Tinubu administration, like its predecessor, has continued to rely on domestic and external loans to finance government projects, with several borrowing requests submitted to and approved by the National Assembly.

In October, President Tinubu sought the National Assembly’s approval to proceed with the processing of external loans worth $20,517,755,901 and €1,045,083,643 under the 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan.

In November, the president withdrew the request and instead requested approval for a new external borrowing plan of $7.7 billion to partly finance the 2026 budget deficit.

The request came about five months after the National Assembly approved a $516.3 million loan from Deutsche Bank AG to finance the construction of the Sokoto–Badagry Superhighway, a flagship infrastructure project under the administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

The loan has a tenure of nine years, including a grace period of up to three years, with an interest rate capped at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange’s Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) plus 5.3 per cent annually.

The facility is backed by insurance from the Islamic Corporation for the Insurance of Investment and Export Credit, the insurance arm of the Islamic Development Bank.

In March, the National Assembly also approved a $6 billion external borrowing plan for the federal government.

Of the amount, $5 billion was to be sourced from First Abu Dhabi Bank to support the national budget, while a $1 billion export finance facility from the United Kingdom, arranged by Citibank, was earmarked for the rehabilitation of Tin Can Island Port and the Lagos Port Complex.

President Tinubu has repeatedly defended his administration’s borrowing decisions, arguing that loans are necessary to finance critical infrastructure and other development projects.

In April, he said his administration would continue to borrow whenever necessary, insisting that borrowing should not be viewed negatively.

Mr Tinubu spoke at the State House during a meeting with Plateau State leaders led by Governor Caleb Mutfwang and the APC National Chairman, Nentawe Yilwatda.

“If we have to borrow, we borrow. Borrowing is not leprosy, we just have to work hard to be able to pay for it,” the president had said.

World.title: 2027: Senate condemns attack on Tinubu’s convoy, asks INEC to disqualify candidates linked to violence
World.content:
The Senate on Tuesday called on the Nigeria Police Force to investigate the circumstances surrounding recent incidents of political violence, particularly attacks on presidential candidates and their supporters, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The upper chamber urged the police to identify and publicly expose the sponsors of the attacks and prosecute those responsible.

The lawmakers condemned attacks on presidential candidates, including the one on President Bola Tinubu’s convoy at the Shehu Shagari Central Mosque in Garki, Abuja, last Friday. They urged the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, to investigate the incidents.

The Senate made the resolutions while debating a motion on the urgent need to address the rising incidents of political violence, intolerance and attacks on political leaders and their supporters.

The motion was sponsored by Abdul Ningi (ADC, Bauchi Central).

Presenting the motion, Mr Ningi said the persistent attacks on presidential candidates, campaign rallies and other forms of political violence had grave implications for national security, democratic participation and the peaceful conduct of the 2027 general elections.

He recalled the attack on President Tinubu’s convoy last Friday, shortly after the president observed Jumu’ah prayers at the mosque. The departing convoy was reportedly attacked with stones and other dangerous objects, damaging vehicles and injuring security operatives.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Ningi also referenced the attack on Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and other political stakeholders during a political gathering in Edo State.

He further mentioned the violent disruption of a political procession involving supporters of the NDC and the Obidient Movement in Asaba, Delta State, on 7 November 2026, which reportedly left one person dead and five others injured.

The senator also listed the reported attack on the convoy of Atiku Abubakar, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), in Sokoto State.

He expressed concern that failure to promptly investigate and prosecute the perpetrators and sponsors of political violence could embolden further attacks, deepen political divisions and threaten the peaceful conduct of the 2027 general elections.

He therefore urged the Senate to call on relevant security agencies to conduct thorough, impartial and transparent investigations into the incidents, identify the perpetrators and their sponsors, and ensure their prosecution in accordance with the law.

Debate

Ali Ndume (APC, Borno South), who seconded the motion, described the attack on President Tinubu’s convoy as an embarrassment to the country rather than the president.

“What we need to do as a Senate is to stand up strongly against any form of violence. Last week, what happened to Mr President is not an embarrassment against the president; it is an embarrassment to Nigerians. On a Friday, in a Mosque, it is wrong,” he said.

Mr Ndume said the president’s democratic disposition had prevented a harsher response to the incident, adding that the 78 people reportedly arrested could have faced a different fate if the president had a military mentality.

He warned that political violence could escalate if not addressed promptly and called for restrictions on the carrying of dangerous objects during campaigns.

“During campaigns, the police should ban any harmful equipment; anybody who is caught with knives or sticks should be prosecuted,” he said.

Mr Ndume also called for special courts to prosecute offenders during political campaigns.

Kawu Sumaila (APC, Kano South) proposed an amendment to reduce the period given to the Senate committees assigned to examine the matter to submit their report from four weeks to one week.

Mr Sumaila, however, disagreed with the proposal to establish special courts at campaign grounds, arguing that political candidates should also be held accountable when their supporters are found carrying dangerous weapons.

“I align myself with the recommendations of the motion. But it is across all parties. You see candidates with police escorts and thugs. Let the candidates be prosecuted if their supporters are found with dangerous weapons,” he said.

Abba Moro (PDP, Benue South) said existing provisions of the Electoral Act could be used to address electoral violence, urging security agencies to enforce the law.

“We have various sections in the Electoral Act to tackle election violence. We need to urge the security agencies to prosecute,” he said.

Mr Moro warned that failure to address the situation could endanger the electoral process and discourage citizens from voting.

“If this is not nipped in the bud, then certainly, our election and electoral process will be in danger. It will cause voter disenfranchisement; voters will be so scared even to vote; what then will become of our democracy?” he said.

Babangida Hussaini (APC, Jigawa North-West) urged the Senate to direct the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to disqualify candidates linked to political violence ahead of the elections.

Binos Yaroe, the senator representing Adamawa South, proposed an additional prayer urging state governors and political candidates to allow opposition parties access to public facilities for political activities, particularly campaign rallies.

The Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, then put the motion and the amendments to a voice vote, and most lawmakers supported them.

After the debate, Mr Akpabio urged the federal government to direct the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, and other relevant security agencies to strengthen security arrangements for political leaders, candidates, supporters and political gatherings nationwide.

He also called for effective early-warning and rapid-response mechanisms to prevent political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The Senate President mandated the Senate Committees on National Security and Intelligence, Police Affairs, and the Independent National Electoral Commission to engage relevant institutions and report to the chamber within four weeks on measures to prevent political violence and safeguard the 2027 general elections.

Mr Akpabio also directed INEC to implement relevant provisions of the Electoral Act to prevent further incidents of political violence.

Political violence

Since the commencement of campaigns some months ago, there have been increasing violent attacks on campaign rallies, town hall meetings and other political gatherings organised by parties seeking the mandate of the people.

PREMIUM TIMES recently documented a series of reported incidents of political violence, particularly those involving presidential candidates and opposition parties, since campaigns officially began in August, and their implications for the 2027 general elections.

World.title: State Police: Reps confirm unanimous approval by 36 state assemblies
World.content:
The House of Representatives has welcomed the unanimous approval of the proposed establishment of State Police Services by all 36 State Houses of Assembly, describing the development as a major milestone in efforts to decentralise policing and address Nigeria’s security challenges.

The House said the approval exceeded the constitutional requirement for state legislatures to pass a constitutional amendment, paving the way for the proposed legislation to be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the spokesperson for the House, Akin Rotimi, said the Clerk to the National Assembly (CNA), Kamoru Ogunlana, had confirmed that all 36 state assemblies had endorsed the Constitution Alteration Bill seeking to establish state police.

According to Mr Rotimi, the unanimous approval represents 100 per cent endorsement by the state legislatures and exceeds the minimum requirement of 24 state assemblies stipulated under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution.

Mr Ogunlana, in his confirmation, said the bill had met the constitutional and administrative requirements for transmission. Still, the National Assembly leadership had briefly delayed the process to allow wider consultations and consensus among the states.

“Following the completion of the verification process by my Office, the Bill is set for transmission to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, for His Excellency’s assent,” he said.

He described the unanimous endorsement as an unprecedented demonstration of cooperation between the National Assembly and state legislatures, as well as between the executive arms of government at the federal and state levels.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The House said the development reflected the collective efforts of both chambers of the National Assembly, the 36 state assemblies, governors and other stakeholders involved in the constitutional amendment process.

It also credited the House Committee on Constitution Review, chaired by Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu, for its sustained work toward securing approval.

The proposed amendment is expected to provide the constitutional framework for states to establish and operate their own police services, potentially changing Nigeria’s current centralised policing structure.

Backstory

The current proposal is contained in the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, which seeks to establish State Police Services and related matters.

Both chambers of the National Assembly passed the proposed amendment before transmitting it to the 36 State Houses of Assembly on 16 September for consideration and approval.

Under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, an amendment to the Constitution requires the support of at least two-thirds of all members of each chamber of the National Assembly and approval by resolutions of not fewer than two-thirds of the State Houses of Assembly.

With 36 state legislatures in the country, the proposal therefore needed approval from at least 24 assemblies to satisfy the constitutional requirement.

The CNA had initially asked state legislatures to communicate their decisions within 30 days, with the period ending on 15 October. However, the deadline was administrative, not constitutional

On 3 November, Mr Ogunlana announced that 28 state assemblies had approved the proposal, exceeding the required threshold. He said his office had verified the resolutions and accompanying Votes and Proceedings submitted by the state legislatures.

READ ALSO: Reps panel gives NSCDC boss 24 hours to explain alleged abuse by mining marshals

The Senate subsequently gave the six outstanding assemblies until 15 November to communicate their decisions, allowing more states to participate in the process.

The proposed amendment would replace the existing single-force arrangement with a dual policing structure comprising a Federal Police Service and State Police Services.

Under the proposed framework, governors would appoint Commissioners of Police for their respective states, based on recommendations from the National Police Council and subject to confirmation by the relevant State Houses of Assembly.

After unanimous approval, the CNA said the verified bill was ready to be transmitted to the president.

World.title: 2027 elections: TikTok, NUJ train over 300 journalists to tackle misinformation
World.content:
TikTok has partnered with the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) and Code for Africa to train more than 300 media professionals ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections.

The training, held across Lagos, the Federal Capital Territory, Ogun, and Oyo, focuses on information verification, responsible election reporting and journalists’ understanding of TikTok’s content ecosystem.

TikTok outlined measures it said it had introduced to address election misinformation, deceptive behaviour and AI-generated content during the Lagos training on Tuesday.

Nigeria’s presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for 16 January 2027, while the governorship and state House of Assembly elections will follow on 6 February.

Journalist training

TikTok said its partnership with the NUJ and Code for Africa was intended to help journalists understand emerging trends in digital journalism and identify misleading information during the election period.

Philip Nwosu, Vice Chairman of the NUJ Lagos State Council, said journalists had a responsibility to provide credible information, particularly during elections.

“This training, delivered in partnership with TikTok Africa, is timely as we prepare for the forthcoming general election, as it will strengthen journalists’ understanding of digital platforms, responsible content creation, information verification and emerging trends in online journalism,” Mr Nwosu said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He added that continuous training would help media professionals improve the quality and credibility of their election coverage.

Election information centre

TikTok also announced the launch of an in-app Election Centre developed in partnership with the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and DUBAWA, a verification and fact-checking platform.

The centre will provide information about voting, election dates and other electoral processes. It will also direct users to resources explaining how to identify misinformation.

According to TikTok, the centre includes an artificial intelligence media literacy hub containing guidance on identifying AI-generated material and using AI tools responsibly.

INEC’s Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Victoria-Eta Messie, said access to credible information was important to voter education and public understanding of the electoral process.

“We strongly believe that this initiative will assist in countering harmful misinformation, disinformation and fake news,” she said.

Election task force

The platform said it had established an election task force comprising specialists in election integrity, cybersecurity, misinformation, deceptive behaviour and platform safety.

It said the team would work with moderation technology and local-language moderators to enforce its community guidelines during the elections.

TikTok’s Global Integrity Programmes Lead, Lorenzo Andreozzi, said collaboration with electoral authorities, fact-checkers and civil society organisations was necessary because digital platforms could not address modern information challenges alone.

He said TikTok would continue working with INEC, DUBAWA and other organisations familiar with Nigeria’s information environment.

TikTok said it had applied election-integrity measures during more than 300 elections worldwide.

Misinformation and deceptive accounts

Under its existing policies, TikTok said it would remove false claims about voting procedures and accounts impersonating politicians, electoral bodies or news organisations.

Where an election-related claim cannot be verified immediately, the platform may attach an unverified-information label, warn users before they share it, and prevent the content from appearing on its “For You” recommendation feed.

TikTok said it works with more than 20 fact-checking organisations accredited by the International Fact-Checking Network globally. In Nigeria, it works with Code for Africa to assess potentially misleading claims.

According to the company, more than 210,000 videos were removed between April and June 2026 for violating policies covering civic and election integrity, misinformation and harmfully misleading AI-generated content.

It said more than 99 per cent of the affected videos were removed before users reported them. The statement did not specify whether the figure applied exclusively to Nigeria or across TikTok’s global operations.

AI-generated content

TikTok said creators must label AI-generated content uploaded to the platform.

It also uses content credentials, invisible watermarking and an AI-generated-content toggle to identify or label synthetic media.

The company said more than five billion videos had been labelled through these tools and technologies, although it did not provide a Nigeria-specific breakdown.

The measures come amid growing concern that realistic AI-generated audio, photographs and videos could be used to misrepresent candidates, public officials or electoral events.

Political advertising prohibited

TikTok restated its prohibition on paid political advertising, including paid promotions by content creators for candidates or political parties.

It said accounts belonging to politicians and political parties could not advertise or access monetisation features. Such accounts are also required to activate two-step verification.

The platform, however, permits recognised election-management bodies to advertise voter-information messages, including details about registration, polling and participation.

TikTok also said it removed more than four million videos in Nigeria for various violations of its community guidelines during the second quarter of 2026.

According to the company, 98 per cent were removed before users reported them, while 91.7 per cent were taken down within 24 hours.

World.title: COP31: How Nigeria can turn household solar systems into investment opportunities – Lagos Carbon CEO
World.content:
In this interview with PREMIUM TIMES on the sidelines of the ongoing United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Türkiye, Ibukun Adebayo, Chief Executive Officer of Lagos Carbon, discusses opportunities in Nigeria’s growing solar energy market and how the country can leverage renewable energy certificates to mobilise investment, expand solar generation and strengthen its clean energy industry.

Excerpt:

PT: Could you share your thoughts on the ongoing conversations about the opportunities and challenges surrounding Nigeria’s solar boom?

Mr Adebayo: I’m the CEO of Lagos Carbon. I spent 30 years in the City of London, working on solutions that we can bring back to Nigeria. Our main challenge right now is the slow pace of energy decarbonisation. However, the opportunity before us is to monetise existing solar installations through carbon credits and Environmental Attribute Certificates (EACs) to fund greater solar generation. Today, an amazing opportunity exists through a certificate called an International Renewable Energy Certificate (I-REC), which measures one megawatt-hour of power generated from a renewable energy source, primarily solar.

If you put solar on your roof today, you can generate carbon credits and EACs from your installation, which can be sold. Unlike carbon credits, which have requirements around permanence and additionality, EACs are relatively straightforward. The Nigerian national renewable energy market offers a higher redemption value. This means that when you achieve a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, the value you can realise from selling the certificate can be higher than what you might get from carbon credits.

PT: What do you think we need to do to implement this in Nigeria and make it work across households? How can Nigerians, particularly those who have already installed solar systems, benefit?

Mr Adebayo: Aggregating solar installations within a particular vicinity or locality creates the economies of scale needed to generate one megawatt-hour of renewable energy, which can then be sold. The benefits can be shared among participating communities. Revenue from selling EACs or International Renewable Energy Certificates can be distributed among community members. Therefore, even if households have individual solar installations, they need to aggregate them. That is the solution.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

PT: In terms of policy, there have also been discussions about Nigeria’s abundant mineral resources, which could be used to manufacture solar systems, batteries and other components. What is your view on the direction Nigeria is taking, particularly regarding its existing policies?

Mr Adebayo: Nigeria has made progress in establishing a national carbon market framework. In October last year, Nigeria made a significant development in positioning itself within the global carbon market, particularly in relation to Articles 6.2 and 6.4 of the Paris Agreement. However, the challenge remains the same: we do not have enough electricity. We need to mobilise funding to add solar capacity. Monetising energy certificates is one of the fastest ways to achieve this. We need to let the market work within the appropriate policy framework.

PT: There are also concerns about affordability and people’s ability to access some of the materials and technologies needed to develop these systems. Do you have anything to share on that?

Mr Adebayo: Yes. There are discussions around developing local manufacturing capacity for solar panels, inverters and all the components that make up the solar industry. Of course, that will cost money and require significant investment. However, what should concern us most is the end user. The problem we are trying to solve is not simply how to build a manufacturing industry. It is how to provide electricity that supports economic growth, job security and individual development.

That is the key. What we are saying is that by selling energy certificates collectively as communities, we can create an opportunity that has never existed before. It will help create a bottom-up approach to mobilising investment in the industry you just mentioned. We should take advantage of this opportunity because, for the first time, we have a mechanism that can help make it possible.

PT: Some people have raised concerns about false climate solutions. They argue that carbon markets and similar mechanisms could distract from addressing the climate crisis. There are also concerns about potential land grabbing and the impact on local communities. On the other hand, some stakeholders believe carbon markets and trading are the way forward. Nigeria has also introduced a carbon market framework. What is your position on this?

Mr Adebayo: We have to decide on our priorities. Our priorities should include how we use our land, economic growth and the economic opportunities available to us. For me, we must start with economic opportunity. Everything else should fall into place around that. Markets and climate finance can help achieve those goals.

There are international organisations and European corporations with an annual demand of about $32 million for emissions reductions, which they can purchase from Nigeria, Lagos, any other state or even internationally. That presents an opportunity for Nigeria to access carbon and climate finance. Why do they do it? If I am a European corporation looking to offset my emissions, I could buy carbon credits through the European trading system at $18 per credit. Alternatively, I could buy a Nigerian environmental certificate or carbon credit for $10. In either case, I am supporting the same reduction in atmospheric carbon emissions. It does not matter whether I purchase the credit in London or Lagos; the environmental benefit is the same, and the people providing the opportunity to offset emissions receive the investment. Why not bring that finance into Nigeria? Why not allow that money to support solar development and strengthen our economy?

PT: We also see Nigeria importing more solar panels and other equipment. What do you think we need to do differently in this regard?

Mr Adebayo: I am agnostic on that issue. What matters to me is ensuring that solar supply meets solar demand. As you know, the Middle Belt states have significant potential for solar generation. We are talking about thousands of megawatt-hours of electricity, yet Nigeria’s requirement runs into several gigawatts. We need this electricity to support the industry. Industry is often described as the engine room of Nigeria’s economy, but we do not have enough power to keep the lights on. We need to decide whether we want to become resource nationalists, worrying about foreign participation, or ensure we have sufficient, good-quality, and affordable electricity to support economic growth. That is not a question for me to answer. I would rather put that question to the authorities.

PT: Finally, what is your message regarding solar adoption and the sustainable use of solar energy systems in Nigeria?

Mr Adebayo: Because of our geographical location, we are blessed with approximately 8,700 hours of solar potential annually. That is an astonishing resource. If we learn to harness it properly, it could be more valuable to us than our oil and gas combined. We should make solar energy accessible to the masses and find ways to develop Nigeria’s solar industry. This will help reduce our reliance on fossil fuels, making the planet and our country much cleaner and greener.

PT: Thank you for your time and for sharing your thoughts on this important issue with us.

World.title: Experts urge more local content to unlock Nigeria’s $8.5 billion solar potential
World.content:
As Nigeria’s adoption of solar energy systems continues to grow amid unreliable electricity supply and rising petrol and diesel prices, energy experts have called for increased local manufacturing, affordable financing, and stronger regulation to unlock the sector’s economic potential.

They also urged the government to invest in skills development, battery storage, recycling infrastructure and nature-friendly solar projects to ensure that the country’s transition to clean energy delivers economic benefits without creating new environmental challenges.

The experts made the call at an event organised at the Nigerian Pavilion on the sidelines of the ongoing 31st session of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Türkiye.

The discussion, themed “Just Transition: Unlocking Nigeria’s Solar Opportunities,” was part of activities marking the conference’s thematic day on Ocean, Seas, Nature and Land Use – Rio Synergy, on Tuesday.

Speaking at the event, David Michael, Executive Director of the Global Initiative for Food Security and Ecosystem Preservation, said Nigeria had the raw materials and human capacity to develop a domestic solar manufacturing industry but remained heavily dependent on imported technologies.

He said the country could leverage its mineral resources to manufacture solar panels, batteries and other components, while creating educational opportunities to equip young Nigerians with the skills required across the solar value chain.

“Solar is not just an energy opportunity; it is an industrialisation, investment and economic transformation opportunity for Nigeria,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Michael said the opportunity extended beyond deploying solar panels to include local manufacturing, mineral processing, battery storage, job creation, improved agricultural productivity and regional exports.

He argued that Nigeria needed to transition from importing solar solutions to producing and exporting clean-energy technologies.

Mineral resources and manufacturing opportunities

Mr Michael identified 12 minerals that Nigeria could leverage to develop its solar technology industry, including silica, lithium, copper, aluminium, iron ore, graphite, manganese, nickel, cobalt, tin, zinc and silver.

He explained that these minerals have applications across the solar value chain, from producing photovoltaic cells and solar panel frames to battery storage, electrical connections, and mounting structures.

Silica, for instance, is a primary raw material for producing silicon used in crystalline solar cells. Lithium and graphite are also key components of batteries that store electricity generated by solar systems.

Copper is used in electrical cables, wiring, connectors and inverters, while aluminium and iron ore can support the production of solar panel frames and mounting structures.

He identified several states with reported deposits of these minerals, including Nasarawa, Kogi, Plateau, Kaduna, Bauchi, Zamfara, Niger, Osun, Ekiti and Benue.

According to him, developing these resources could reduce Nigeria’s dependence on imported solar components while creating jobs and strengthening its industrial base.

He also called for the establishment of local solar panel, inverter, battery and component manufacturing and assembly industries.

Market opportunities and agricultural applications

Mr Michael said Nigeria’s solar market extended beyond its domestic borders, pointing to the significant electricity access gap across West Africa.

He cited figures indicating that West Africa accounted for 33 per cent of the 565 million people without access to electricity in sub-Saharan Africa in 2023, representing approximately 185 million people.

He said this presented an opportunity for Nigeria to position itself as a regional manufacturing and distribution hub for solar technologies.

He also identified agriculture as another major area where solar investments could deliver economic benefits.

According to him, expanding solar-powered irrigation, cold storage, refrigeration and agro-processing could improve agricultural productivity, reduce post-harvest losses and strengthen food security.

He further called for the establishment of solar technology training institutions to develop a skilled workforce of technicians, installers, engineers, entrepreneurs and maintenance professionals, particularly among young people and women.

Nigeria’s solar investment potential, he added, runs into billions of dollars.

He cited International Finance Corporation estimates identifying up to $8.5 billion in commercially viable solar investment opportunities by 2030, while broader distributed renewable energy opportunities exceed $18 billion over the next decade.

Government promises enabling environment

Also speaking, Olamide Fagbuji, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Climate Technologies, said the government was working to create an enabling environment for private-sector investment in the renewable energy sector.

He referenced Nigeria’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0, describing it as a robust framework for advancing the country’s climate commitments.

He also highlighted the Electricity Act, which gives state governments opportunities to participate in electricity generation and distribution.

Mr Fagbuji said expanding solar adoption would require significant financing, especially because many Nigerian households need reliable, sustainable electricity.

He, however, stressed the need for innovative financing models that would make solar systems more affordable and accessible to households and businesses.

On the environmental implications of increased solar adoption, he said the government was working towards developing policies on the recycling and management of solar waste under the extended producer responsibility framework.

He noted that private-sector participation would be important in addressing the growing waste challenge associated with solar technologies.

On the development of solar mini-grids, Mr Fagbuji said projects needed to meet specific requirements, including appropriate land-use arrangements and benefit-sharing strategies.

Affordability, quality concerns threaten adoption

Meanwhile, Gloria Bulus, Executive Director of Bridge That Gap Initiative, identified affordability as a major barrier preventing communities from adopting solar energy systems.

Responding to a question on the challenges limiting adoption, Ms Bulus said the problem went beyond access to solar panels, noting that the cost of batteries and other components remained a major concern for many households.

“For communities, it is not about the solar panels; it is about the affordability of the panels and batteries,” she said.

She argued that the government could play a significant role in addressing the affordability challenge and improving access to solar technologies, particularly among underserved communities.

Ms Bulus also warned against deploying solar infrastructure in ways that could create additional environmental problems.

She called for nature-friendly approaches to land use, stressing that efforts to address Nigeria’s electricity challenges should not come at the expense of ecosystems.

“While we are trying to address electricity problems, we must not use it to cause another problem,” she said, advocating the adoption of nature-friendly models.

Similarly, Joseph Ibrahim, Nigeria Campaign Director of the Secure Energy Project, said solar adoption had increased significantly over the past decade. Still, concerns about affordability, product quality and after-sales services continued to undermine public confidence.

He said some consumers who adopted pay-as-you-go financing arrangements had complained that their solar systems stopped functioning after about six months.

According to him, such experiences risk discouraging households and communities from investing in solar energy.

“When that happens, consumers lose faith in solar systems,” he said.

Mr Ibrahim called for stronger quality standards for imported solar products and more effective regulation of installers to protect consumers and ensure that systems meet required performance standards.

He also advocated locating solar manufacturing facilities near universities to help students gain practical experience and better understand solar technologies.

He said closer collaboration between manufacturers and academic institutions could help build the technical expertise required to support Nigeria’s emerging solar industry.

Balancing energy access with a just transition

Nigeria’s growing interest in solar energy is partly driven by persistent electricity shortages, limited access to the national grid in many communities and rising costs of alternative energy sources following the removal of the petrol subsidy.

For many households and businesses, solar systems have become an alternative for maintaining electricity supply and reducing dependence on petrol- and diesel-powered generators.

However, the experts stressed that expanding adoption alone would not guarantee a just energy transition.

They said affordability, local economic participation, consumer protection, environmental safeguards and access to technical skills must remain central to Nigeria’s solar development strategy.

They argued that without deliberate investments across the value chain, the country risks becoming an expanding market for importsrted technologies rather than a major producer of clean-energy solutions.

World.title: South Africa summons Nigerian High Commissioner over livestream controversy
World.content:
The South African government has summoned the Nigerian High Commissioner to the country, Femi Fani-Kayode, over the diplomatic row surrounding Nigeria’s alleged exclusion from the live broadcast of the credentials presentation ceremony.

South African media reported that the Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) summoned Mr Fani-Kayode and reprimanded him over his conduct after the ceremony.

According to a statement issued Tuesday, DIRCO chairman Zane Dangor told Mr Fani-Kayode during the meeting that his comments breached diplomatic convention.

Mr Dangor was reported to have pointed out that Article 41 of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations required diplomatic agents to conduct official business with host countries through the ministry of foreign affairs.

However, Mr Fani-Kayode, in a post on X, described the meeting as “cordial” and “constructive.”

He said concerns about the weekend’s events were discussed, and noted that he hopes to strengthen ties between the two countries.

“Mutual concerns regarding our bilateral relations and the events over the weekend were discussed. We look forward to building on the outcome of this meeting and further strengthening the long- standing bilateral relations between Nigeria and South Africa which are founded on mutual respect, friendship and co-operation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The diplomatic spat between South Africa and Nigeria began last Friday after Mr Fani-Kayode, through his social media handle, accused the South African presidency of cutting off the live stream during his speech at the Sefako Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Pretoria, where he presented his credentials to President Cyril Ramaphosa.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that Mr Fani-Kayode, also accredited to Lesotho and Eswatini, made it clear that he was the only one of the 15 Ambassadors given the stage to speak whose live stream was cut off.

Following, the South African Presidential Spokesperson, Vincent Magwenya, accused Mr Fani-Kayode of misrepresenting the facts, saying the event was live-streamed by the South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC), whose operations are not controlled by the presidency.

READ ALSO: 17 killed in separate South African mass shootings

The Nigerian High Commission joined the exchange and accused Mr Magwenya of trying to heighten diplomatic tension between the states by “adding fuel to the fire.”

Speaking on the situation, the SABC said it live-streamed the event and that the presidential team had no influence on its editorial process.

It also said it regretted Mr Fani-Kayode’s refusal to grant an interview about his protest to President Cyril Ramaphosa.

Relations between Nigeria and South Africa grew tense after a new wave of xenophobic violence broke out in April and has since been linked to the death of at least 12 Nigerians.

Mr Fani-Kayode, first deployed to Germany, said he asked to be redeployed to South Africa because it was more “proximate to my political thinking when it comes to foreign affairs and a pan-African vision.”

World.title: Fountain of Life board names interim leader, insists Jimmy Odukoya’s ouster
World.content:
The group of trustees that announced Jimmy Odukoya’s removal as Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church has named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as the church’s interim spiritual and administrative leader.

In a further statement sent to PREMIUM TIMES on Tuesday afternoon, the trustees maintained that their resolution removing Mr Odukoya remained in force despite a rebuttal published on his Instagram page and the church’s official social media account.

The statement said Mr Okpaise would oversee the church pending consultations and other processes leading to the appointment of a substantive leadership structure.

“The Board has further resolved that the interim spiritual and administrative leadership of the Church be entrusted to Pastor Rotimi Okpaise,” it read.

The trustees did not state whether Mr Okpaise was the person allegedly chosen by the church’s late founder, Taiwo Odukoya, to succeed him.

Board insists on removal

The group said it had previously asked Mr Odukoya to step down before resolving at a meeting held on 16 November that he would no longer be recognised as Senior Pastor.

It said its decision followed a review of the church’s succession arrangements, unresolved governance concerns and what it described as moral and doctrinal controversies.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Accordingly, having previously called upon Pastor Jimmy Odukoya to step down, the Board, at its meeting held on 16 November 2026, resolved that Pastor Jimmy Odukoya is no longer recognised as Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, with immediate effect,” the statement read.

“He is required to step down forthwith from the office and all functions of Senior Pastor.”

The trustees said the interim arrangement was intended to restore peace and rebuild trust while the church addressed its leadership crisis.

Succession recording

The latest statement provided more details about the recording at the centre of the dispute.

According to the trustees, Mr Odukoya told the board after his father’s death that the late cleric had handed the church’s leadership to him. The board said it relied on that representation when it appointed him Senior Pastor in 2023.

It alleged, however, that Taiwo Odukoya had asked Jimmy to record a video in December 2021 in which he identified a different person as his preferred successor.

The board said Pastor John Odukoya witnessed the recording, which was not shown to trustees until late December 2025, about four years after it was made and more than two years after Taiwo Odukoya’s death.

“Its existence and contents were not disclosed to the Board at the time it deliberated upon and approved the appointment of Pastor Jimmy Odukoya as Senior Pastor,” it said.

It argued that the omission denied trustees access to information that could have influenced their 2023 decision.

However, the statement again withheld the identity of the person the late founder allegedly chose. It also did not disclose who eventually presented the video to the board or where it had been kept.

Social media dispute

The trustees also alleged that the church’s official social media channels had been taken over by Mr Odukoya or people acting on his behalf without the board’s authorisation.

They said the platforms had been used to circulate an “inaccurate and misleading” account of the dispute and warned that posts currently appearing on them did not represent their position.

“The Board is taking appropriate steps to restore the Church’s official communication channels to proper and authorised control,” the statement added.

The allegation followed a statement published jointly on Mr Odukoya’s verified Instagram page and the church’s official Instagram account earlier on Tuesday.

The statement rejected his removal and said the announcement came from a group called “Concerned Members of the Board.”

It alleged that those trustees had been asked to resign on 14 March over repeated violations of the church’s constitution and founding principles. According to the statement, one of them subsequently resigned.

It maintained that Mr Odukoya remained the duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees, having been unanimously appointed in September 2023.

Still unsigned

In its latest response, the group seeking Mr Odukoya’s removal advised members and the public to recognise only statements “issued and signed for and on behalf of the Board of Trustees” as the church’s official position.

However, the copy sent to PREMIUM TIMES did not bear the name or signature of any individual trustee. It ended with “For and on behalf of the Board of Trustees, The Fountain of Life Church.”

The rival statement published on the church’s social media account was also unsigned and did not identify the trustees who authorised it.

Neither side has disclosed the current number or identities of the church’s trustees or published the constitutional provisions upon which it based its claim to authority.

Backstory

The leadership dispute became public after a statement sent to PREMIUM TIMES earlier on Tuesday announced Mr Odukoya’s removal.

The group behind the announcement said a recently presented recording showed that Taiwo Odukoya had chosen another person to succeed him. It claimed Jimmy was expected to assist the chosen successor with administrative matters and lead the church’s youth ministry.

It also raised concerns about Mr Odukoya’s remarriage and its public blessing, describing them as contrary to the church’s teachings and the values of its founders.

Jimmy’s sister, Tolu Odukoya-Ijogun, confirmed to PREMIUM TIMES that the first document was a valid statement from the board but declined to comment further.

The church was founded in 1992 by Taiwo and Bimbo Odukoya. Bimbo died in a 2005 Sosoliso plane crash in Port Harcourt, while Taiwo died in August 2023.

World.title: Fountain of Life board reaffirms Jimmy Odukoya’s removal, names Okpaise interim leader
World.content:
The Board of Trustees of Fountain of Life Church has reaffirmed its decision to remove Pastor Jimmy Odukoya as senior pastor, appointing Pastor Rotimi Okpaise to oversee the church’s interim spiritual and administrative leadership.

The board said the interim arrangement would remain in force pending consultations and the completion of processes for appointing a substantive leadership structure in accordance with the church’s constitution and established procedures.

The latest decision comes amid an escalating leadership and succession dispute between the board and Jimmy, son of the church’s late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, who had earlier rejected his removal.

In a statement on Tuesday, the trustees insisted that their November 16, 2026 resolution withdrawing recognition of Jimmy as senior pastor remained valid.

The board also alleged that individuals linked to Jimmy had taken control of the church’s social media platforms without its authorisation and were using them to publish what it described as inaccurate and misleading accounts of the dispute.

“The Board stands by its earlier statement in its entirety, and its resolution of 16 November 2026 remains in force,” it said.

The trustees explained that the decision followed a review of the church’s leadership and succession arrangements, as well as what they described as longstanding governance concerns and current doctrinal and moral controversies.

They said Jimmy had previously been asked to step down before the board resolved to withdraw its recognition of him as senior pastor with immediate effect.

“He is required to step down forthwith from the office and all functions of Senior Pastor,” the statement added.

The board said the decision was intended to create an atmosphere conducive to restoring peace, rebuilding trust and resolving the church’s leadership and governance challenges.

It stressed that the action was not motivated by vindictiveness, humiliation or personal condemnation but was considered necessary to protect the church’s spiritual heritage, institutional integrity and public reputation.

The trustees also warned that statements appearing on the church’s social media platforms should not be regarded as official positions of the board.

They said only statements issued and signed on behalf of the board should be recognised as official, adding that steps were being taken to restore the church’s communication channels to authorised control.

Background to succession dispute

Providing details of the succession disagreement, the board said Fountain of Life Church had built its reputation over three decades on biblical truth, sound doctrine, spiritual integrity and Christian leadership under its founding pastors.

It said responsibility for ensuring an orderly leadership transition rested with the board following the death of Taiwo Odukoya in 2023.

According to the trustees, Jimmy had informed them, and subsequently the congregation, that his late father had handed the leadership mantle to him.

The board said it relied on that representation when it appointed him senior pastor in accordance with the church’s constitution and the succession arrangements it understood to be in place.

However, it disclosed that a video recording made by Taiwo in December 2021, in which he expressly identified his preferred successor, was not presented to the board until late December 2025.

The recording, which the board said was witnessed by John Odukoya, Taiwo’s older son, did not identify Jimmy as the preferred successor.

It further claimed that the recording was not disclosed when it considered and approved Jimmy’s appointment as senior pastor.

“The fundamental issue, therefore, is not simply the identity of the person appointed, but whether the board’s decision was reached on the basis of full, accurate and transparent disclosure of all material information relevant to the succession process,” the trustees said.

The board maintained that it could not remain indifferent while, in its view, the church’s spiritual heritage, institutional integrity and public reputation faced continuing erosion.

World.title: ECOWAS court president seeks improved justice delivery, harmonised judicial standards
World.content:
By Innocent Anaba

The President of the Community Court of Justice of the Economic Community of West African States, ECOWAS, Justice Charlyne Brumskine, has called for stronger institutional collaboration, harmonised judicial practices and improved justice delivery across the West African sub-region.

Brumskine made the call while declaring open the Court’s 2026 Judicial Retreat in Niger State, Nigeria.

She described the five-day retreat as an important opportunity for judges and judicial support staff to review existing practices, address emerging institutional challenges and develop strategies for improving the administration of justice.

The ECOWAS Court president said the retreat was taking place at a critical stage in the institution’s development, following the adoption of a harmonised legal framework under Supplementary Act SA.1/12/25, the deployment of the Electronic Case Management System, ECMS, and the commencement of the implementation of the Court’s Strategic Plan 2026–2030.

She noted that the first strategic goal of the plan was to guarantee timely and impartial justice.

According to her, the developments require clear and harmonised institutional standards to ensure that the Court’s legal framework, technological infrastructure and judicial practices work together effectively.

“Our task this week is to build on that foundation, consolidate the best practices and experiences, and improve upon the standards where needed,” she said.

Brumskine stressed the importance of collaboration among the Judges’ Chambers, the Registry, the Research and Documentation Department and other support departments, noting that effective judicial administration depended on the collective efforts of all units.

“It is our collective responsibility to build a Court whose standards, systems and procedures consistently support judicial independence, efficiency, accountability and public confidence,” she added.

Earlier, the acting Deputy Chief Registrar of the Court, Mrs. Marie Saine, outlined the objectives and expected outcomes of the retreat.

She said the overall objective was to adopt harmonised standards, guidelines and working procedures to promote the effective and efficient administration of justice.

Saine identified the adoption of standardised judgment templates, a judgment-drafting style guide and quality-assurance procedures, as well as the establishment of an Editorial Committee, among the key objectives.

Others include strengthening legal research support and collaboration between the Judges’ Chambers and the Research and Documentation Department.

She said the retreat would also consider the 2027 judicial calendar, external court sessions, guidelines for virtual sittings and priorities for further development of the Electronic Case Management System.

The review and determination of Instructions to the Chief Registrar and Practice Directions are also expected to form part of the deliberations.

Saine added that participants would develop an implementation framework with clearly assigned responsibilities to ensure that recommendations from the retreat were effectively executed.
