World.title: ¿Cuál es el mejor seguro en un mundo amenazado por el clima? Aquel que se adelanta al riesgo
World.content:
La detección y prevención de inundaciones o incendios está transformando el papel tradicional de las aseguradoras, que ya no esperan a que se produzca un siniestro para proteger a sus clientes. Así está adoptando Allianz este nuevo paradigma

Una breve comprobación mental: si un cañería pierde agua, lo primero en lo que pensamos, casi invariablemente, es “¿esto lo cubrirá el seguro?”. La misma asociación salta ante un buen número de desastres más o menos cotidianos: un local inundado por un temporal, ganado que perece por un incendio, cosechas perdidas por una granizada… En estas ocasiones, así está grabado en nuestro imaginario, el seguro entraba en escena después del siniestro, cuando tocaba evaluar los daños y compensar las pérdidas. Hoy, en un mundo marcado por una amenaza climática cada vez más compleja e ingobernable, este paradigma está cambiando. La mejor manera de proteger algo es anticiparse a todo peligro posible para lograr que se mantenga a salvo, sin daños.

Esta ambición es, todavía, un ideal al que tender, pero ya existen proyectos que dan tanta importancia a la prevención del riesgo como a la respuesta ante el mismo. Así lo entiende Olivia Loewe, directora de Corporate Affairs y Sostenibilidad de Allianz España: “La prevención está dejando de verse como un coste para entenderse como una inversión. Igual que hemos interiorizado hábitos de salud o de seguridad vial, necesitamos seguir avanzando en una verdadera cultura de resiliencia climática”. Más cuando las pérdidas globales por catástrofes naturales alcanzaron los 284.000 millones de euros en 2024, en datos de la compañía aseguradora, de los que solo 137.000 millones estaban asegurados.

Rastrear el fuego

Entonces, ¿cómo anticiparse a los fenómenos climáticos extremos, en principio tan inabordables por su magnitud? La respuesta, para Allianz, está en el uso de la tecnología y el conocimiento, la vía para identificar (y desactivar) riesgos antes de que se conviertan en desastres. Imaginemos un incendio forestal recién declarado. Mientras los equipos de emergencia supervisan su evolución, algo que se hace desde hace años, hay otra información decisiva que ya se puede recabar: qué viviendas, negocios o personas podrían encontrarse en la trayectoria del fuego. Y así prevenir a la ciudadanía y, llegado el caso, actuar antes de que las llamas alcancen una zona habitada.

Las cuatro grandes áreas de la prevención Informar para anticipar. Ante la dana de octubre de 2024, Allianz activó anticipadamente su protocolo especial de eventos meteorológicos y envió más de 50.000 SMS preventivos a clientes de las zonas con mayor riesgo de afectación, tanto en la Península como en las Baleares.



Fotos: ISTOCK El fuego, bajo vigilancia. Allianz ha puesto en marcha en España, junto a Satellites on Fire, un sistema de monitorización satelital que permite seguir la evolución de los fuegos casi en tiempo real e identificar a los clientes que podrían verse afectados. Así, es posible activar protocolos de prevención y comunicación antes de que las llamas lleguen a viviendas o zonas empresariales. La naturaleza también protege. Tras los daños de la dana, Allianz y WWF impulsan un proyecto de restauración ecológica en el río Mijares. El objetivo es recuperar ecosistemas fluviales capaces de contribuir a regular el agua, absorber mejor los episodios extremos y reforzar la resiliencia del territorio. Ríos más sanos como defensa frente a futuras inundaciones. Sin distracciones al volante. El estudio SWIPE. TAP. CRASH., del Allianz Center for Technology (AZT), analiza los riesgos de la distracción al volante en la era del coche digital. Presentado en el Allianz Motor Day 2026, el trabajo analiza más de 34.000 accidentes, pruebas de eye-tracking (seguimiento ocular), simulaciones de conducción, estudios científicos y encuestas internacionales para entender mejor el problema y ayudar a prevenirlo.

Esta es la esencia del sistema de monitorización de incendios que Allianz ha puesto en marcha en España junto a la startup tecnológica Satellites on Fire. La solución, que ya se usa, combina tecnología satelital e inteligencia artificial para seguir prácticamente en tiempo real la evolución del incendio y combinar esa información con la localización de los clientes que potencialmente podrían verse afectados.

El proyecto cobró total dimensión este verano, en el que se produjeron más de 45 grandes incendios forestales y se quemaron más de 220.000 hectáreas. Allianz, en este escenario de emergencia, realizó más de 1,2 millones de comunicaciones preventivas a clientes expuestos, generó 728 notificaciones de incendios y verificó 126 activaciones de planes de respuesta, con un equipo de 15 profesionales dedicado a supervisar y gestionar las alertas.

La iniciativa es la materialización española de la herramienta internacional Global Risk Assessment, pensada para que un usuario consulte, en tiempo real, los riesgos climáticos de su dirección, un análisis que bebe de proveedores de información meteorológica de todo el mundo. Este proceder supone un cambio significativo en la relación entre aseguradora y cliente, explica la compañía, ya que ahora el primer contacto no tiene por qué producirse después del siniestro; puede llegar cuando todavía hay margen de protección.

Barreras y avisos ante danas

En el caso de las danas, la mejor manera de amortiguar sus consecuencias es preparar el territorio. O el río, más concretamente. Esa es la lógica del proyecto de restauración ecológica que Allianz ha impulsado junto a la asociación no gubernamental WWF en el río Mijares (Teruel, Aragón), tras los daños ocasionados por la dana de Valencia de 2024.

La iniciativa busca recuperar ecosistemas fluviales degradados y reforzar su capacidad natural para resistir episodios meteorológicos extremos. Una idea de sobra conocida, pero no por ello lo suficientemente explotada. La naturaleza –como demuestran los tejados vegetales o los terrenos inundables, por ejemplo– es una de las mejores defensas naturales ante las inundaciones. Por eso, recuperar la salud de ríos como el Mijares redunda en una mayor capacidad para absorber el exceso de agua de un temporal.

Ninguna aseguradora, sea como sea, puede impedir que se produzca un fenómeno meteorológico extremo. Pero sí puede, como ya hace Allianz, servirse de información cada vez más fina y precisa para que sus clientes tomen medidas preventivas lo antes posible. Es lo que sucedió en octubre de 2024, cuando Allianz, ante la dana que se acercaba, activó anticipadamente su protocolo especial de eventos meteorológicos y envió más de 50.000 SMS a clientes en las zonas de mayor peligro.

En una segunda fase, con el desastre ya consumado, la compañía reunió a 300 agentes y corredores de las zonas más perjudicadas, reforzó su red de peritos y habilitó canales específicos de información y asesoramiento. La prevención, en este caso, equivalió a una reacción más rápida y a una respuesta posterior más efectiva y ordenada. Es decir: anticipación para un mayor margen. Y seguros para el durante y el después de un siniestro, pero sobre todo para el antes.

Comprender el porqué de los accidentes y formar en educación financiera El 79% de los conductores españoles cree que las tecnologías incorporadas en el coche incrementan las distracciones al volante, según un informe de Allianz. CEDIDA ALLIANZ Allianz ya aplica esta nueva lógica a riesgos cotidianos. En movilidad, por ejemplo, la compañía investiga las causas de los accidentes para evitar así que se repitan. Lo hace en el Allianz Center for Technology, un laboratorio que ha analizado más de 34.000 accidentes en su estudio SWIPE. TAP. CRASH., en la relación entre las pantallas táctiles y los dispositivos digitales y las distracciones al volante. El 79% de los conductores españoles considera que las tecnologías incorporadas a los vehículos han incrementado los despistes en carretera, entre otras conclusiones del informe. Por otra parte, los riesgos financieros, en auge desde que los procesos bancarios se han ido digitalizando, es otro de los campos que aborda Allianz en materia de prevención. Más aún cuando en España, según una encuesta de Allianz Research, solo 17% de la población tiene un nivel alto de educación financiera. Para paliar este déficit, y en consecuencia para aumentar la protección frente a fraudes, Allianz impulsa Finances4All, un programa dirigido a formar a más de 640 jóvenes en situación de vulnerabilidad financiera, y Allianz School for Life, una plataforma digital gratuita con contenidos sobre ahorro, inversión, deuda y prevención del fraude.

World.title: Fallece una cría de rorcual común de seis metros de largo en una playa de Cabo de Gata
World.content:
El animal, que apenas tenía unas semanas de vida y se encontraba muy débil, ha muerto cuando los especialistas le practicaban la eutanasia porque no tenía ya opciones de supervivencia en el mar

Era una cría y se cree que tenía apenas unas pocas semanas de vida, pero medía ya seis metros de largo. Un ejemplar de rorcual común (Balaenoptera physalus), el segundo animal más grande del planeta después de la ballena azul, quedó varado en la noche de este lunes en la playa de San José, en el municipio de Níjar (Almería, 33.319 habitantes), en pleno corazón del parque natural Cabo de Gata. Un grupo de activistas y personas voluntarias han cuidado del mamífero durante toda la mañana, hasta que a primera hora de la tarde ha sido asistido por especialistas del Centro de Gestión del Medio Marino (CEGMA) ubicado en Algeciras (Cádiz), que tenían previsto practicarle la eutanasia, aunque ha fallecido justo después de que fuese sedado para que no sintiera dolor.

Varios testigos han explicado que ya vieron que había algo flotando en el agua junto a una de las playas de San José en la noche del lunes, pero con la oscuridad pensaron que sería un tronco. Este martes, con las primeras luces del día, han comprobado que se trataba de un animal y han avisado sobre las ocho de la mañana al CEGMA gaditano, único organismo que tiene autorización para atender a los cetáceos varados. Con un viaje por delante de más de cuatro horas en coche para los especialistas, un grupo de personas voluntarias vestidas con neopreno han atendido al rorcual durante la espera. La tarea principal ha sido mantener húmeda su piel y cubrir al animal con toallas y telas mojadas para evitar que la exposición directa al sol le provocase quemaduras. También han acudido hasta la playa agentes de Medio Ambiente de la Junta de Andalucía y personal del Ministerio de Transición Ecológica.

El personal del CREA llegó a mediodía hasta Cabo de Gata. Y sobre las tres de la tarde han dispuesto todo para practicar la eutanasia a la cría, que no tenía posibilidades de supervivencia por sí misma. El protocolo indicaba sedar primero al animal para que después no sufriera, y ha sido justo después de ese primer pinchazo cuando ha fallecido, sin llegar siquiera al definitivo. En un primer reconocimiento, los expertos han comprobado que el rorcual tenía un pequeño mordisco en la cola, algunos parásitos en la piel y se encontraba en un estado de extrema delgadez. “Quizá se fue quedando atrás de la manada y ha acabado en la playa agotado por el cansancio”, cuenta Marcos Diéguez, vecino de San José y miembro de Ecologistas en Acción. “O puede que haya sufrido un impacto con alguna embarcación, sufra alguna enfermedad o haya tragado plástico, aunque no es habitual cuando todavía es lactante”, añade Diéguez.

El animal ha sido trasladado hasta el puerto de San José, donde pasará la noche hasta que mañana se le practique una necropsia y se tomen pruebas para conocer la razón de su muerte, para aportar así información relevante para la investigación y conservación de la fauna marina en el Mediterráneo. Durante el año 2025, la consejería de Sostenibilidad y Medio Ambiente de la Junta de Andalucía, a través del Servicio de Emergencias frente a Varamientos de Mamíferos y Tortugas Marinas, realizó un total de 43 necropsias de ejemplares varados en el litoral andaluz.

“Actuación correcta”

“La actuación ha sido la correcta”, explican en la organización Equinac, que hasta el pasado mes de febrero era la encargada de atender estos varamientos en las playas de Almería. “Reintroducir un animal así es mandarlo a una muerte muy cruel. Cuando una ballena depende de su madre para sobrevivir no la puedes lanzar al mar de nuevo para que muera de hambre y agonice. Es como un cachorro de león si lo sueltas en la sabana solo”, subrayan desde la entidad.

Fuentes ecologistas lamentan que el cetáceo haya tenido que sufrir durante toda la jornada a la espera de la llegada del personal del CREA de Algeciras, cuando hasta principios de este año —y durante los 30 años anteriores— la propia asociación Equinac tenía autorización para atender a los cetáceos y las tortugas marinas que quedasen varadas en la costa almeriense. Según informó la entidad el pasado mes de febrero, la Junta de Andalucía no renovó la concesión para ese servicio a la empresa Almerimar, que contaba con instalaciones para la recuperación de los animales, donde trabajaba el personal. “Equinac en estos años ha cubierto el 100% de los avisos de varamientos en Almería de cetáceos y tortugas marinas, tanto vivos como muertos. No ha dejado ni un solo animal sin prestar ayuda, de lunes a domingo, a cualquier hora, cualquier día, todo por la única vocación de ayudar a estos animales”, afirmaban en un comunicado publicado entonces en sus redes sociales.

El rorcual común (Balaenoptera physalus) es el segundo animal más grande del planeta, solo por detrás de la gran ballena azul. Los ejemplares más grandes pueden llegar a medir hasta 27 metros y pesar unas 70 toneladas. Se los reconoce por su color gris pardo en la parte superior de su cuerpo y un tono blanquecino en la inferior. Se les puede ver en tanto en los polos como en latitudes tropicales, y en el mediterráneo están presentes, sobre todo, en su zona

World.title: Trump llega a Filipinas en plena pugna con China por la influencia en el Sudeste Asiático
World.content:
El presidente de EE UU se reúne en Manila con los líderes de Japón, India y Australia y los miembros de la ASEAN antes de viajar a Shenzhen, donde mantendrá un encuentro con Xi y Putin

El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ha aterrizado este martes en Manila, la capital de Filipinas, desde donde viajará mañana a Shenzhen, en el sur de China. En la capital tecnológica del gigante asiático asistirá el jueves a la cumbre de líderes del Foro de Cooperación Económica Asia-Pacífico (APEC) y participará en una reunión sin precedentes con el líder chino, Xi Jinping, y el ruso, Vladímir Putin. Antes de esa cita a tres, Xi y Trump mantendrán un encuentro bilateral. La tregua arancelaria entre las dos potencias expira el 10 de enero y Washington acaba de anunciar nuevas restricciones para limitar el acceso de las empresas chinas a los chips avanzados.

En Manila, el republicano ha abierto su visita a Asia con una reunión del Quad, el grupo que reúne a Estados Unidos, Japón, India y Australia y que sirve de contrapeso a la influencia de China en el Indo-Pacífico. Es el primer encuentro de sus dirigentes desde septiembre de 2024. “Tenemos una gran relación con estas personas y estos países”, ha dicho el estadounidense tras hacerse la foto de grupo. “Son estupendos y grandes amigos”.

Trump ha defendido la coordinación de los cuatro países para preservar un Indo-Pacífico “libre, abierto, estable y próspero” y ha anunciado que el año que viene el Quad celebrará su primer foro de líderes empresariales para llevar la cooperación económica “a un nivel completamente nuevo”. El republicano ha apuntado que el grupo cerrará varios acuerdos sobre minerales críticos para garantizar el suministro y evitar que alguno de sus miembros sea “vulnerable a la coerción de un solo proveedor lejano”. “Van a pasar muchas cosas”, ha adelantado, en referencia a la colaboración en materia de minerales críticos y tierras raras.

“Todos nuestros países llegamos muy tarde. Y ahora vamos muy por delante. Avanzamos a un ritmo que nadie cree posible”, ha añadido. También ha sostenido que Estados Unidos está acelerando la producción de tierras raras a niveles récord y que “alcanzará a China en diez meses”.

Trump ha anunciado que el Quad realizará unas maniobras con aviones de patrulla marítima (aún sin fecha) con el objetivo de “preservar la paz” — “Mientras nos reforzamos”, ha remarcado— y ha elogiado los ejercicios de guerra antisubmarina y de combate contra buques de superficie que realizaron a finales de octubre. Su anuncio llega dos días antes de reunirse en Shenzhen con Xi. Pekín recela de este grupo, en el que ve un intento de Washington de contener sus avances.

Preguntado por si Irán representa una amenaza inminente para Estados Unidos, el republicano se ha limitado a aseverar que, de ser así, “pagará un precio como jamás ha pagado ningún otro país”. Trump ha añadido que Washington se toma el asunto muy en serio. “Resulta que están muy locos. Por eso no pueden tener un arma nuclear”, ha zanjado.

De izquierda a derecha, la primera ministra de Japón, Sanae Takaichi; el primer ministro de la India, Narendra Modi; el estadounidense Donald Trump y el primer ministro de Australia, Anthony Albanese, antes de la reunión del Quad en Manila este martes. Carlos Barria (REUTERS)

Tras su encuentro con sus socios del Quad, el presidente estadounidense se ha incorporado a la última jornada de la cumbre de la Asociación de Naciones del Sudeste Asiático (ASEAN) para participar en una sesión especial con el bloque y cenar con sus mandatarios. Trump busca estrechar lazos con los mismos países a cuyas importaciones puso aranceles en 2025. Filipinas y Tailandia aprovecharán su visita para tratar de rebajar esos gravámenes.

El líder de EE UU ha firmado un acuerdo comercial con el primer ministro tailandés, Anutin Charnvirakul, que ha calificado como “una victoria increíble”. Bangkok eliminará todos los aranceles a las importaciones estadounidenses y suprimirá importantes barreras a las importaciones de vehículos, dispositivos médicos, productos farmacéuticos, etanol y carne de ave.

En el banquete, Trump ha comenzado su discurso alabando “el nivel de popularidad” de los líderes de la ASEAN y su “fantástico trabajo gobernando”. “Estoy aquí hoy porque Estados Unidos está profundamente comprometido con el éxito, la soberanía y la prosperidad de nuestros amigos y socios”, ha manifestado. Trump también los ha instado a trabajar intensamente en “minerales críticos, tierras raras e imanes” y, dirigiéndose a los presentes, ha añadido: “Alguno de ustedes dirá ‘voy a hacerle caso’ y va a ganar mucho dinero”.

China, que es el principal socio comercial del bloque, ya había movido ficha con la ASEAN: el primer ministro chino, Li Qiang, anunció el lunes que la ampliación del acuerdo de libre comercio entre China y la ASEAN entrará en vigor el 1 de diciembre. El año pasado, el intercambio entre ambos superó el billón de dólares, de acuerdo con datos aduaneros chinos.

Antes de la llegada del presidente estadounidense, Japón y la ASEAN expresaron en Manila su preocupación por la “coerción económica” y se comprometieron a reforzar sus cadenas de suministro. En el caso de Tokio, la presión viene principalmente de Pekín. Desde enero, Japón afronta restricciones chinas a la exportación de determinados productos de doble uso (civil y militar). La medida llegó dos meses después de que la relación bilateral saltara por los aires a raíz de unas declaraciones de la primera ministra japonesa, la ultraconservadora Sanae Takaichi, en las que planteó que, en caso de que se produjese un bloqueo chino de Taiwán, estaría justificado que su país desplegase las Fuerzas de Autodefensa.

El Gobierno chino, que reclama la isla autogobernada como parte irrenunciable de su territorio, tachó aquellas palabras de injerencia y sigue pidiendo una rectificación. Takaichi también viajará a Shenzhen para asistir a la APEC, pero, de momento, todo indica que no se reunirá con Xi.

Este martes, Pekín también ha utilizado la expresión “coerción económica” para denunciar las nuevas restricciones de Washington a la venta de chips avanzados. “Llega incluso a interferir sin razón en el comercio y la cooperación tecnológica normales de China con otros países, y a reprimir de forma injustificada el desarrollo de las industrias chinas de alta tecnología”, ha aseverado el portavoz de la Cancillería, Guo Jiakun.

La norma estadounidense, cuya publicación oficial está prevista el jueves (el día en el que se entrevistarán Xi y Trump), exigirá licencias para determinados envíos de chips avanzados a Singapur, Tailandia, Malasia, Indonesia y Brasil. Washington busca cerrar una vía de acceso indirecto de esa tecnología a China a través del alquiler de capacidad de cómputo en centros de datos en terceros países. La medida llega en pleno escrutinio sobre Megaspeed, la empresa con sede en Singapur bajo sospecha de haber desviado chips de Nvidia a China.

Trump desembarca en el aeropuerto Ninoy Aquino para asistir a la cumbre ASEAN-EE UU en Pasay City, Gran Manila, este martes. Eloisa Lopez (REUTERS)

El miércoles, antes de partir hacia Shenzhen para la cita APEC, Trump será recibido con honores por el presidente filipino, Ferdinand Marcos Jr., cuyo Gobierno busca que Washington rebaje el recargo del 12,5% que también aplica a productos filipinos. La otra cuestión que pesa sobre la visita es la seguridad en el mar del Sur de China, donde los guardacostas chinos y filipinos protagonizan choques recurrentes en torno a arrecifes en disputa.

Desde que llegó al poder en 2022, Marcos ha estrechado la alianza militar con Estados Unidos, después de que su predecesor, Rodrigo Duterte, apostara por un acercamiento a China. En 2023, el Gobierno filipino amplió de cinco a nueve las instalaciones militares filipinas a las que pueden acceder las tropas estadounidenses. Algunas podrían servir de apoyo logístico si Washington decidiera intervenir en un conflicto en el estrecho de Taiwán. Estados Unidos mantiene relaciones no oficiales con Taiwán y le vende armamento para su defensa. Para China, la isla es su principal línea roja. “Estoy seguro de que [Xi] sacará el tema [en la bilateral]. Yo no lo haré”, ha expresado Trump.

La gran incógnita sigue siendo si Trump tendrá su ansiado reencuentro con el líder supremo de Corea del Norte, Kim Jong-un, con quien lleva tiempo queriendo retomar el contacto. Se vieron por última vez en 2019, después de tres cumbres que no arrojaron resultados. Antes de salir el lunes de la Casa Blanca, Trump volvió a plantear la posibilidad de verse. Preguntado por dónde tendría lugar esa cita, Trump respondió que en China: “Puede que venga [a la APEC]. No lo sé. Depende del presidente Xi”. Este martes, el portavoz del Ministerio de Exteriores, Guo Jiakun, ha dicho que carece de información al respecto. A su llegada a Manila, Trump ha dicho que “le gustaría” que fuera Kim quien se pusiera en contacto con la delegación estadounidense. “Veremos qué pasa”, ha repetido.

World.title: Amancio Ortega vuelve a apostar por Chicago: compra un bloque de viviendas de alquiler por 180 millones
World.content:
El empresario multimillonario Amancio Ortega vuelve a apostar por el mercado inmobiliario de Chicago. El fundador de Inditex ha adquirido un edificio llamado The Sinclair de 390 viviendas de alquiler en el lujoso barrio de Gold Coast por 200 millones de euros (alrededor de 180 millones de euros, al cambio actual), tal como adelantó el medio estadounidense CoStar y confirman a CincoDías fuentes conocedoras de la transacción. Se trata de una de las mayores operaciones en la conocida como Ciudad del Viento en los últimos años.

Precisamente, Ortega es el gran dinamizador de ese mercado a través de su vehículo inversor Pontegadea. Solo hace dos meses se conocía que también había adquirido el edificio One North Wacker, un rascacielos de oficinas de 50 plantas en pleno Loop (distrito financiero), por el que desembolsó 550 millones de dólares, alrededor de 490 millones de euros.

La transacción, además, viene a confirmar el interés de Ortega por el mercado estadounidense y también por diversificar en activos de vivienda de alquiler de lujo en los últimos años. Pontegadea adquirió en 2023 el edificio de viviendas de alquiler de 727 de West Madison Street por 232 millones de dólares (alrededor de 212 millones de euros, al cambio de entonces). Además, en esa ciudad cuenta con el hotel Eurostars Magnificent Mile en River North, que compró por aproximadamente 65 millones en 2019.

El edificio The Sinclair ahora adquirido por Pontegadea cuenta con 35 plantas e instalaciones y servicios como piscina exterior, spa, barbacoa, gimnasio, estudio de yoga, conserjería de 24 horas, garaje y cocina común, entre otros. El inmueble pertenecía a la promotora Fifield Cos, quien lo construyó en 2017 y había encargado recientemente a la consultora JLL su venta. El barrio donde se encuentra, Gold Coast, es el más exclusivo de la ciudad y alberga un gran número de boutiques de lujo.

Edificio The Sinclair de Chicago.

El mercado de EE UU

Ortega realizó en julio otra operación residencial en EE UU, concretamente en Boston, donde se hizo con una torre de vivienda de lujo para alquiler -llamada The Kensigton- por 234 millones. El conjunto de todas las adquisiciones en vivienda de alta gama para alquilar en el mercado estadounidense alcanza en los últimos años los 1.350 millones invertidos.

El fundador de Zara es una de las personas más ricas del mundo, con una fortuna de 151.300 millones de dólares (137.600 millones de euros), y ha utilizado históricamente los multimillonarios dividendos procedentes de Inditex, grupo del que controla el 60% del capital, para crear su enorme cartera inmobiliaria durante los últimos años, que supera una valoración de 21.000 millones. La huella en EE UU es muy extensa, donde cuenta con edificios de oficinas, tiendas, viviendas en alquiler o almacenes logísticos.

Precisamente, en logística realizó la que es su mayor adquisición inmobiliaria, ya que en 2022, a través de la filial Ponte Gadea Compass compró a la inmobiliaria Realty Income siete naves logísticas por 905 millones de euros en los Estados de Texas, Pensilvania, Wisconsin, Carolina del Sur, Virginia y Tennessee. Estos almacenes tenían en común largos alquileres a inquilinos de renombre como Amazon, Nestlé, Fedex o Home Depot.

También en EE UU, en 2022, se hizo con el rascacielos de viviendas de lujo para alquiler en el número 19 de Dutch Street, en pleno distrito financiero de Nueva York, cerca del World Trade Center.

World.title: Las webs de Ikea, Zoom y HSBC sufren un ciberataque para robar criptomonedas e infectar a los usuarios de iPhone
World.content:
El audio de esta noticia utiliza una voz sintética generada por Inteligencia Artificial y podría tener algunas inconsistencias.

Los sitios de algunas de las grandes empresas se han visto atacados a través de la plataforma Optimizely para distribuir código malicioso

Algunos de los sitios web más visitados del mundo, entre ellos los de Zoom, HSBC, Equifax, CNN, Salesforce e Ikea, se han visto comprometidos en un intento de robar criptomonedas e infectar iPhones con códigos maliciosos, según denunciaron el lunes investigadores de ciberseguridad de la plataforma Report Uri.

Scott Helme, experto en seguridad, explicó en un informe que el pasado 16 de noviembre se distribuyó un código JavaScript malicioso a los visitantes de los sitios web de 178 organizaciones de diversos sectores a través de Optimizely, una plataforma de optimización de sitios web. El software malicioso sustituía las direcciones de monederos de criptomonedas por la de los atacantes, robaba datos de tarjetas mientras los usuarios introducían sus datos de pago, cookies y capturas de pantalla de los usuarios e instalaba código de explotación en dispositivos con iOS.

La empresa de ciberseguridad HudsonRock aseguró asimismo haber encontrado indicios de que los visitantes de estos portales recibieron código malicioso durante su navegación. Reuters no pudo determinar de inmediato si el código fue utilizado con éxito en todos los casos ni el alcance de los posibles ataques resultantes. No obstante, el informe de los investigadores confirma el robo de criptomonedas mediante transacciones verificadas hacia las direcciones controladas por los atacantes.

Salesforce informó de que estaba investigando cambios no autorizados en los scripts (secuencia de comandos) de Optimizely y que los había desactivado como medida de precaución. Equifax también investigó el incidente y dejó de utilizar Optimizely. La compañía aseguró que no había encontrado pruebas de que sus sistemas hubieran sido manipulados.

Optimizely, Apple, Zoom, HSBC, CNN e IKEA no respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios realizadas por Reuters.

World.title: VVD will support tax plan in Senate as cabinet avoids collapse
World.content:
All three coalition parties will support the cabinet’s tax plans for next year in the Senate, ending the stand-off that began last week when the right-wing VVD rejected its own finance minister’s budget settlement.

Senate group leader Tanya Klip confirmed that the party intended to vote in favour when the plans are debated on December 7.

The votes of the nine VVD senators, together with coalition partners D66 and CDA and the left-wing opposition parties Pro and Volt, will be enough to pass the bill.

The fiscal package was thrown into disarray last Thursday when the right-wing liberal VVD voted against it in the lower house, triggering a weekend of crisis talks and speculation that the government was about to collapse.

VVD leader Dilan Yesilgöz called the minority coalition a “failed experiment” after the other coalition parties negotiated a deal with Pro and Volt to raise an extra €1 billion in income tax by increasing the tax rates on assets and savings.

Yesilgöz said her party had been wrong-footed by the amendment, which she called a “bad deal for the Netherlands”, and suggested D66 and CDA appeared to prefer a coalition with the left-wing Pro.

Weekend negotiations

But after three days of discussions behind closed doors on the Zwaluwenberg estate outside Hilversum and in the Catshuis, the prime minister’s official residence, the three parties agreed to carry on in government.

Prime minister Rob Jetten admitted at a press conference that he had been “too optimistic” about the chances of doing a deal with opposition parties on both left and right on the tax plans and said internal disputes within the coalition had had the “upper hand”.

Sybrand Buma, the former CDA party leader and vice-chairman of the Council of State who chaired coalition talks between the parties after last year’s election, will lead a new round of talks designed to improve relations between the government and parliament.

The cabinet will also come up with measures to help small and medium-sized businesses during the talks next year on the budget for 2028, Jetten said, in what was seen as a concession to the VVD.

The coalition parties said in a statement on Monday night that trust had been restored following the acrimonious budget debate last week, which led to D66 and CDA passing the tax plan with support from two fringe parties on the left.

But opposition leaders were sceptical of Jetten’s claims. Pro leader Jesse Klaver said: “The cabinet needs to set a course for itself and make choices”, otherwise “we’ll be back where we started”.

Joost Eerdmans, of the right-wing JA21, said the VVD had been right to demand a change of course, but commented: “We will find out in practice if we actually get a right-wing correction”.

World.title: Want to start really speaking Dutch? Read on…
World.content:
For so many internationals who have already taken Dutch language courses, their journey stops somewhere after heavy beginner grammar courses and before speaking truly takes hold.

Whether that’s due to book-focused courses, complicated grammar or futility and fear that you’ll never be able to get that guttural g sound right, life goes on and Dutch takes a back seat.

It’s for just that reason that NedLes, a homey Dutch school in Amsterdam Oost, developed its intensive, 2-week conversation course for those with at least an A2 level who want to start speaking Dutch in their daily lives.

“People want to stabilise their language level and feel confident enough to speak,” says Renske Berns, co-owner of NedLes.

Conversational boost

“Think of it as a conversational boost,” adds co-owner Welmoed Nijhout, speaking from their sunny and spacious office nearby the Oosterpark.

The intensive course immerses students in Dutch for 10 days, with two hours spent in class speaking and about four hours of preparation per class that you can do at home, at the school (on its sunny porch weather permitting!) or at the nearby public library.

“They’re not joking when they say intensive,” says Angely Diaz, an agile coach who moved to the Netherlands from Honduras in 2019. “You really have to commit to it, and I appreciate that. I’ve lived here for seven years already and really want to make progress this year. And NedLes is the only place I’ve found that really focuses on just talking, talking, talking!”

Podcasts

The small classes of 10 people maximum do that by starting off listening to a Dutch podcast, which students then discuss throughout the lesson. They also talk about daily topics, meaning you can carry what you’ve practiced with you outside the classroom and into the real world. There are no books used in class. (Yes, you read that right!)

“I can listen to podcasts more easily,” says Diaz of her progress since taking an intensive course. “But more than anything, it helped my self-confidence when speaking Dutch, to start the conversation in Dutch and resist switching to English.”

Student Stephen F., a classical musician from Toronto who moved to Amsterdam earlier this year with his husband (also a NedLes student!), agrees. He’s taken two intensive NedLes classes so far.

Muscle memory

“Both of them have helped me be less afraid to talk out loud in Dutch,” he says. “In class, I can speak well enough to be understood, but with mistakes. I still don’t get through many interactions in public that stay completely in Dutch without me or the other person switching to English, but when it does happen, I feel quite happy about it.”

And compared to other Dutch courses he’s taken online or at different schools, he says what he likes about NedLes is that “it doesn’t get bogged down in grammar rules, so you practice speaking more”.

“It’s a more organic way to learn than only following rules without getting the muscle memory of applying them,” adds Diaz. “And the teachers are very supportive and make the class engaging, fun, and most of all, a space to learn Dutch. Unlike other schools, they didn’t switch to English when we were confused but spoke in basic Dutch to make sure we understood. I appreciate that, because that’s how it goes in the real world!”

The next intermediate intensive course begins December 7, with another one following early in the new year. At only €625 a course, NedLes makes learning to speak Dutch affordable. What better holiday gift to give yourself than one that keeps on giving?

World.title: NL persistently falling short of obligations to disabled people
World.content:
People with disabilities in the Netherlands are structurally disadvantaged and lack the same opportunities as everyone else in daily life, according to the first report on how the country is meeting its obligations under the UN disability rights convention.

The convention, which the Netherlands ratified in 2016, commits governments to making sure people with disabilities can take full part in society, from work and housing to education and transport.

The public health institute RIVM, which carried out the monitor, said there was more attention for the more than two million people in the Netherlands with a disability than in the past. But it found persistent gaps in work, income and online access, the RIVM’s director Marith Volp told broadcaster NOS.

Some 36% of people with disabilities have a paid job, compared with 65% of people without, Volp said. People with disabilities also earn less on average, are more likely to live close to the poverty line and more often rent social housing rather than own a home.

Most Dutch websites and apps do not meet the rules on digital accessibility, the report said, although national government and council websites have more than commercial ones. Polling stations are also often a problem. Between 2022 and 2024, only 2% to 10% of the stations that councils had labelled accessible passed an independent test, NOS said.

Volp also said the RIVM saw a risk of social isolation, with people with disabilities facing barriers to playing sport and going to the cinema or theatre.

There has been some progress, however, with more people with disabilities in work than before, and more getting assistive home equipment. Public transport has also become more accessible, with fewer height differences at bus stops and more guide lines for blind people.

But much remains unclear because the information available is fragmented, the RIVM said. It made recommendations for better measurement so that policy can be adjusted.

The Netherlands ratified the convention in 2016, and in 2024 it published a national strategy with goals on work, housing, income, education, care, transport, culture, sport and safety. The cabinet aims to bring the position of people with disabilities into line with the convention by 2040. The RIVM will report every year until 2029.

In June, the Netherlands Institute for Human Rights (CRM) said the country was failing to keep its promises. In its survey of 1,800 disabled people, 35% said they worried about not having enough money in the future.

World.title: List of PFAS pollution sites “contaminated with errors”
World.content:
A list of sites contaminated with PFAS “forever chemicals” is riddled with mistakes, according to the local authorities who are responsible for overseeing the clean-up.

The government identified 57 sites that represent an “unacceptable risk” to the local environment because of high levels of PFAS chemicals, which are widely found in household and industrial waste.

But a survey by NOS of the 12 provinces and 29 local councils that manage the sites, at least half the locations are on the list even though they are not high-risk or the level has not been established.

Experts who spoke to NOS said the list was symptomatic of the chaotic way the government has handled PFAS pollution, and warned that while some locations are wrongly on the list, other places with high pollution levels were probably being overlooked.

The government in The Hague has compiled the list based on surveys of councils and provinces. The information gathering exercise is due to be completed in 2030.

But many authorities said there were administrative problems with the surveys. Groningen’s replies have not been included because they not submitted in the format required by the ministry, while Zuid-Holland said the “definition was not yet known”.

Schiphol not listed

Six of the 57 locations were recorded as having “no unacceptable risk” while another 20 were listed as “not yet known” and in five cases no data was recorded.

Some sites that are known to be major users of PFAS chemicals are absent from the list, including Schiphol airport, which Utrecht University professor and expert in toxicology Chiel Jonker called “one of the largest PFAS locations in the Netherlands where polluted water is pumped out”.

PFAS chemicals are widely used in packaging and products such as products such as shampoo, food packaging, cosmetics and paint.

Known as “forever chemicals” because they take an extremely long time to break down, they have been linked to some types of cancer, hormone disorders and damage to the immune system.

Hans Slenders, of the PFAS Expertise Centre, told NOS that the national government needed to take responsibility for tackling PFAS pollution. “The problem is much too complicated to be solved locally,” he said. “The ministry must take the lead.”

World.title: Jetten admits mistakes as VVD ministers back tax plan
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten has admitted that he was “too optimistic” in his quest for broad support for his budget plan, which culminated in last week’s coalition crisis. The VVD ministers in the cabinet will now defend the tax plan that the party’s MPs voted against last week.

“We realise we have tested the patience of the whole country,” Jetten told a press conference on Tuesday morning, adding that financial decision making had been taken too lightly.

Jetten said the relationship in the coalition had been damaged. “We want to turn the page,” he said, “but it’s not as if we can put everything behind us.”

“Political intervention”

Deputy prime minister Dilan Yesilgöz, who called the minority cabinet a “failed experiment” on Friday, did not use the phrase when asked repeatedly at the press conference whether that was still her view.

On Wednesday she had said that if her coalition partners in the centrist D66 and the Christian Democrat CDA would rather form a coalition with the left, they should just say so.

She wouldn’t say whether the right-wing liberal VVD had won the “political reset” it had demanded. Instead, she called the appointment of Sybrand Buma to advise the coalition a “political intervention”.

“You want to go in a certain direction together,” she said. “We hope Mr Buma can lay the foundation for that. That could be structural agreements, partial deals.”

Buma, a former CDA leader who was informateur during the talks that led to the coalition last winter, has a month to help the cabinet agree a financial framework with opposition parties before budgets are drawn up, rather than fighting over them afterwards.

Business package

The tax plan, which shifts €1 billion from income tax to wealth tax, will not change this year, the Telegraaf reported. In return the coalition has promised a package for small and medium-sized businesses. The details won’t be worked out until spring.

Asked whether VVD senators would back the plan, Yesilgöz said that was up to the senate. The senate debate is provisionally set for December 7 and MPs are expected to debate the crisis on Wednesday.

World.title: More than half of Dutch students struggling with finances
World.content:
Students in the Netherlands are increasingly seeking financial support help from organisations set up to alleviate poverty, a survey by the hardship charity Armoedefonds has found.

Three-fifths of organisations said they had experienced an increase in applications, while the budget information agency Nibud said more than half of young people were struggling to make ends meet.

Earlier research by the Armoedefonds found that one-third of support agencies knew of young people who were unable to start or finish a study course because of financial problems.

Spokeswoman Lotte Meerhoff said discussing financial hardship was still a taboo for many young people.

“It’s good that more young people are seeking help, but it shows again how many young people are struggling with financial problems,” she told NOS. “And that can really affect your future in a negative sense.”

Nibud said 54% of young people were having trouble with their financial situation, compared to 40% two years ago. NOS said it had heard of some students doing three part-time jobs to pay the bills.

Financial institutions are offering more help in the form of payment plans or subsidies for essential equipment such as laptops, but Meerhoff said political solutions were needed too.

“We have seen young people’s financial problems growing for years,” she said. “Limiting their ability to pay in instalments on credit, which the political parties are focusing on now, is not enough. Young people need to have more to spend, and that means raising the minimum wage and student finance.”

World.title: Registrations to vote in Senate elections double since 2023
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

More than 80,000 Dutch citizens living abroad have registered to vote in next year’s provincial elections, more than double the number that signed up in 2023.

The electoral commission set up a special electoral college for non-resident citizens four years ago following a campaign by the lobby group Stichting Nederlanders Buiten Nederland (SNBN).

People living on the Caribbean islands of Bonaire, Sint-Eustatius and Saba were also given a vote for the first time.

Foreign residents do not choose representatives for a provincial assembly, but their vote counts towards the make-up of the Senate, which will be indirectly elected by the 12 provinces in May.

So far 82,393 people have registered to vote in the 2027 election, which takes place on March 17, according to the city council in The Hague, which is responsible for the electoral college.

Eelco Keij, chair of SNBN, said he was “positively stunned” by the size of the response, with 10 weeks to go until registration closes. “It’s exciting that so many people from abroad are willing to participate in the democratic process, which also indicates that they felt left out before.”

Dutch citizens can register until February 3 through the council’s website.

Four years ago 37,173 foreign citizens signed up. GroenLinks won the largest share of the overseas vote with 18.5%, while D66 took 16.3%.

The Labour party (PvdA), which has since merged with GroenLinks to form Progressief Nederland, took 8.4%, giving the left-wing combined list more than a quarter of the vote.

Not all parties in parliament contested the vote: the far-right PVV, farmers’ party BBB, the ChristenUnie and Denk were all absent from the ballot paper in 2023.

Keij said he hoped the heightened interest from voters would persuade parties to take the expat vote seriously this time. “There are always remainder seats, so this could be a tipping-point number for parties that are active abroad,” he said.

The BBB became the largest party in the provinces and Senate, taking 19.2% of the overall vote.

World.title: Jetten cabinet survives crisis as coalition agrees to carry on
World.content:
Rob Jetten’s minority cabinet will stay in office after four days of crisis talks. The three coalition parties have agreed to patch up the row over the 2027 tax plan and keep going.

The centrist D66, right-wing liberal VVD and Christian Democrat CDA said on Monday night that “intensive talks” had brought about a “restoration of trust”, public broadcaster NOS reported. No other party will be brought into the coalition.

The government information service RVD announced the deal at around 10pm, after more than nine hours of talks at the Catshuis, the prime minister’s official residence in The Hague.

Debate demanded

Opposition leaders were quick to react to the news. PRO leader Jesse Klaver said it was “totally irresponsible” for the VVD to vote against its own cabinet’s tax plan. “The big question for the whole country is: do we still have a cabinet?” he said. He wants a debate in parliament.

The local authorities’ association VNG, backed by the logistics lobby Evofenedex and the property developers’ association Neprom, had already urged the cabinet to sort out its differences and serve its full term.

Ministers are holding an extra cabinet meeting on Tuesday morning to hear what exactly was agreed. Jetten and his deputy prime ministers, Dilan Yesilgöz (VVD) and Bart van den Brink (CDA), are expected to explain the deal afterwards. MPs are likely to debate the situation on Wednesday, after Klaver’s request.

The three parties have also brought in Sybrand Buma, vice-president of the Council of State and a former CDA leader, to help them reach working agreements with opposition parties on the budget. Buma will mainly advise and won’t be making deals himself, NOS reported, quoting sources in The Hague.

Tax deal row

The row broke out when D66 and the CDA made a deal with left-wing PRO and pan-European party Volt. The deal raises wealth tax by €1 billion and uses the money to cut income tax.

The VVD said the deal broke the coalition agreement. On Thursday its MPs voted against the whole tax plan, which scraped through with the smallest possible majority, 76 of 150 seats.

The next day Yesilgöz called the minority cabinet a “failed experiment” that needed a “fundamental reset”. Jetten said the parties had to have “fundamental talks” to make improvements on a substantive, political and personal level.

The leaders spent the weekend at the De Zwaluwenberg estate in Hilversum, then moved to the Catshuis on Monday. According to NOS, they discussed breaking up the coalition or carrying on without the VVD, but both options were later dropped.

The coalition has just 66 of the 150 seats in parliament, so it needs opposition votes in both houses to pass legislation. The senate is due to vote on the tax plan in the week before Christmas.

World.title: Poland’s central bank freezes constitutional court’s accounts amid leadership dispute

Poland’s central bank has frozen outgoing transfers from the bank accounts of the Constitutional Tribunal (TK), citing conflicting claims over who has the authority to manage the court following a disputed takeover by a group of judges backed by the government. The National Bank of Poland (NBP), which holds the tribunal’s accounts and is headed by a governor appointed under the former government, said it was not the bank’s role to determine which side was legally entitled to represent the institution. Narodowy Bank Polski wstrzymał realizację zleceń płatniczych Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. Powodem jest spór o to, kto jest uprawniony do reprezentowania TK i dysponowania środkami zgromadzonymi na jego rachunkach bankowych – poinformował NBP.https://t.co/KXwEBL6j9k pic.twitter.com/0h90bPdTLO — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) November 16, 2026 Last month, eight judges elected to the TK this year by the government’s parliamentary majority – but five of whom the opposition-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, has refused to swear in – took control of the court. They declared that the chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, and his deputy, Bartłomiej Sochański, both of whom were appointed to the TK under the former government, had been suspended for failing to fulfil their duties and launched disciplinary proceedings against them. Święczkowski denounced the move as an illegal “coup d’état”. He has been backed by the court’s other six judges, also appointed under the former government. A few days later, Święczkowski submitted a statement to the NBP identifying himself as the sole person authorised to manage the TK’s accounts. Later that week, after the newly elected judges held their first meeting and made several key decisions, the NBP said it had also received documents “indicating, in principle, other persons authorised to dispose of the funds held in the Constitutional Tribunal’s bank accounts”. Meanwhile, Święczkowski also issued a legal challenge against the TK takeover at the Supreme Court, which on 10 November issued a ruling revoking the order to suspend Święczkowski and Sochański. However, the validity of that ruling is disputed. Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, the judge who has claimed leadership of the TK, said that only the tribunal itself can decide on the issue. Disciplinary hearings for Święczkowski and Sochański are due to begin later this week. Święczkowski, nevertheless, sent the Supreme Court ruling to the national bank as evidence that he remained the person legally entitled to manage the tribunal. The dispute around Poland's constitutional court risks entrenching a system of legal dualism in which judicial authority depends on political allegiance rather than broad constitutional consent, writes @AleksSzczerbiak https://t.co/mtgutqSTQh — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 10, 2026 The NBP’s governor by Adam Glapiński, who was appointed under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government and is a longtime associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński. On Monday, the NBP announced that it would suspend all payment orders relating to funds held in the TK’s accounts, citing “a set of documents, which mutually cancel each other out”. “This means that payment orders are not executed, regardless of who initiates them,” the NBP said in a statement. “The National Bank of Poland has no authority to decide who is legally entitled to control the Constitutional Tribunal.” Finance minister Andrzej Domański criticised the decision, accusing the central bank of becoming embroiled in the political dispute. “The National Bank of Poland should safeguard its independence, including its political independence,” Domański said. He added that the government would “explore all available options” to secure funding for the TK and ensure that it can continue functioning. Justice minister Waldemar Żurek also condemned the NBP’s move, saying its “invocation of a non-existent document [the disputed Supreme Court ruling] to block funding for a constitutional body is…an attempt to protect an entrenched system”. Święczkowski expressed satisfaction that the NBP had denied access to the “usurpers” trying to take over the court but argued that he, as the legitimate chief justice, should be given control over the accounts, reports news website Onet. Prezes Narodowego Banku Polskiego próbuje paraliżować Trybunał Konstytucyjny, powołując się na rzekome orzeczenie Sądu Najwyższego z 10.11.2026 r.. Problem w tym, że ten papier wygląda jak wydany z pieczątką z ziemniaka, a w obiegu są już jego trzy różne wersje. Najpierw Bogdan… pic.twitter.com/7rWELZFIF0 — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 16, 2026 Recent events follow a decade-long crisis surrounding the TK. Since the current government – a coalition ranging from left to centre right led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk – came to power in 2023, it has refused to recognise the court’s legitimacy. That is because three of its judges were unlawfully appointed under the former national-conservative PiS government, which was widely seen to have brought the court under political control. As a result, Tusk’s government has ignored the TK’s rulings and, until this year, refused to even nominate new judges to fill vacancies that arose on the court’s 15-person bench. That changed in March, when the ruling coalition began filling the backlog of empty seats. However, Nawrocki has refused to accept the oath of most of those judges, citing concerns over how they were chosen or their qualifications. World.title: Kraków church holds mass for perpetrator of deadly attack just metres from where he shot victims
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! The historic St Mary’s Basilica in Kraków has hosted a holy mass for Michał Oksiński, the man who carried out the recent attack in the city and later died of injuries sustained in a shootout with police. The six people who died in the attack and more than a dozen who were injured were shot by Oskiński on the square where the church stands, some of them just a few metres from its doors. St Mary’s Basilica says that the mass is “an expression of the Christian faith in God’s mercy” and “in no way indicates justification for the crime”. On the afternoon of 7 November, Oksiński launched his attack on Kraków’s famous market square, which was packed with locals and tourists. He shot at random from his car while driving through the square and surrounding streets before police managed to bring his rampage to an end. Later that same day, the dead bodies of Oksiński’s parents and sister were found in his home. They had each been shot in the head while sleeping. Two days after the attack, Oskiński himself died in hospital. On Sunday, Łukasz Wantuch, a former city councillor, shared a photograph of an announcement that there would be “a holy mass for the late Michał Oksiński and the deceased members of his family” at the Roman Catholic St Mary’s Basilica on Monday morning. The church, built in the 14th century, is one of the most famous in Poland and dominates the skyline in Kraków’s historic, UNESCO-listed city centre. It stands on one corner of the market square, just a few steps from where some of Oksiński’s victims were shot. “I won’t hide the fact that I find this somewhat shocking,” wrote Wantuch. He noted that the announcement referred to the “blessed memory” (świętej pamięci) of Oksiński. However, that phrase is standard usage in Polish to refer to someone who has died (the equivalent ot the English “late”). “But perhaps that is what faith is about: praying even for a murderer,” added Wantuch. Among the more than 1,000 comments under his Facebook post, many agreed with that sentiment. “The whole of Christianity is based on forgiving the unforgivable,” wrote one. “I don’t think anyone needs God’s mercy more [than Oksiński],” said another. However, some others were critical of the fact that the mass was being held in that particular church among the dozens in Kraków. “It is the height of impudence that they’ll celebrate mass for him in the very church he murdered in front of,” wrote one commenter. Later on Sunday, St Mary’s Basilica issued a statement, signed by parish administrator Father Mariusz Słonina, saying that the holy mass “is a private initiative of one of the priests, not of St Mary’s Parish”. However, Słonina added that “praying for the deceased is an expression of the Christian faith in God’s mercy” and “in no way indicates justification for the crime, a lessening of the perpetrator’s responsibility, or a trivialisation of the suffering of the victims”. Local news service KR24 reported that uniformed police officers were posted outside the church for today’s mass while plainclothes officers were inside, with one of them right next to the altar. Three priests were present, including Słonina, who presided over the mass. Only around a dozen faithful were in attendance, with KR24 suggesting that many did not even seem aware for whom mass was being held. Separate private funeral ceremonies will take place for Oksiński, his parents and sister, who lived in the town of Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, about 160 km from Krakow. On Sunday, their family issued a statement asking the media to “respect the privacy, dignity and mourning of our family and loved ones”. Meanwhile, police and prosecutors continue to investigate the possible motive behind Oksiński’s attack, which they are treating as a terrorist offence. Last week, the justice minister said that there were “very strong traces of right-wing extremism” in the perpetrator’s online activity. Two police officers, Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański, who were seriously injured in the shootout that debilitated Okisński, have been recovering in hospital after undergoing emergency surgery. Poland has detained and charged three teenagers who are allegedly linked to “an international neo-Nazi network” and had been planning terrorist attacks, including with the use of homemade explosives. The arrests were announced on Monday morning by Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of the security services, who revealed that the suspects are Polish citizens. Two are aged 17 and one is 16. “The teenagers not only promoted Nazi and fascist ideology but had also already taken steps toward committing terrorist offences,” wrote Siemoniak. Funkcjonariusze @ABW_GOV_PL zatrzymali 3 obywateli RP, 16-latka i dwóch 17-latków, związanych z międzynarodowym środowiskiem neonazistowskim. ▶️ Nastolatkowie nie tylko propagowali ideologię nazistowską i faszystowską, ale podejmowali już działania zmierzające do popełniania… — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) November 16, 2026 The National Prosecutor’s Office revealed that the trio were “fascinated by the activities of an international neo-Nazi terrorist organisation…[that] has an ideology based on hatred against people of Jewish descent, immigrants, black people, the LGBT community, politicians and state security officials”. Though prosecutors did not name the organisation, they said that members of it have been involved in planning terrorist attacks in the United States, Germany and the United Kingdom. In some countries, including the UK, Canada and Australia, it has been outlawed and designated a terrorist group. Poland’s Internal Security Agency (ABW) had found that the three suspects’ online communication indicated “an interest in constructing explosive devices, modifying weapons and using such items to carry out terrorist activities”. During a search of the home of one of the 17-year-olds (named only as “suspect 1”), officers found chemicals that are precursors for the production of explosives. That suspect has also been charged with possession of a so-called pipe bomb, which prosecutors say he wanted to “transfer to a neo-Nazi terrorist group”. Suspect 1 was found to have discussed with the other 17-year-old, named as suspect 2, how to construct an explosive device and detonate it in a specific residential building where someone they knew lived. Suspect 1 had also “incited extremist behaviour and hate-motivated violence” in his online activity, while the 16-year-old, named as suspect 3, had “promoted fascist content” (a crime in Poland) and encouraged someone to assault another person based on their race. Each suspect has been charged with three crimes, relating variously to terrorist offences, possession or attempted production of explosives and weapons, promoting Nazism, fascism and racial hatred, and inciting others to commit violence based on racial differences. Prosecutors note that Polish law generally allows people to face full criminal liability from the age of 17. The two 17-year-olds have therefore been placed in adult pretrial detention, while the 16-year-old is being held in a juvenile facility. Śledztwo w sprawie neonazistów i planowanych aktów terroru kryminalnego Szczegóły w komunikacie: ⬇️https://t.co/dQpdgiTYJD — Prokuratura Regionalna w Gdańsku (@Prok_Regio_GDA) November 16, 2026 The arrests come in the context of recent concerns over radicalisation of young people in Poland. Earlier this month, a 24-year-old carried out a terrorist attack in the city of Kraków, killing six people by firing a rifle from his car. He had earlier killed his parents and sister in their home. In the aftermath of the attack, justice minister Waldemar Żurek revealed that investigators had found “very strong traces of right-wing extremism” in the attacker’s online activity, though he emphasised that the motive was yet to be determined. In the space of a few days last month, three knife attacks took place in Polish schools, resulting in one case in the death of a member of staff. Dozens of young people were arrested in the aftermath for making threats and/or possessing weapons. In September, the security services detained three teenagers accused of being part of online groups promoting neo-Nazism and violence. One of them has been charged with planning terrorist attacks on targets including a mosque and a school. Around a dozen public monuments in Poland, including one dedicated to the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, have been defaced with graffiti glorifying the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), a World War Two nationalist partisan group that was responsible for the massacre of Poles and Jews. Ukraine’s embassy in Warsaw has condemned the vandalism and blamed it on Russia, which has previously been accused by the Polish authorities of orchestrating provocative graffiti on monuments. W sobotę, 14 listopada, w Warszawie doszło do kolejnych dwóch dewastacji pomników. Napisy „Slava UPA” pojawiły się na Pomniku Bohaterów Getta przed Muzeum Historii Żydów Polskich POLIN oraz na Pomniku Żołnierzy 1 Armii Wojska Polskiego przy ulicy Andersa 13. To kolejna odsłona… pic.twitter.com/Y7NDsfpjxn — Miejski Reporter (@MiejskiReporter) November 14, 2026 The latest spate of vandalism was first reported in early November in the western city of Poznań, where three World War two memorials were painted with graffiti saying “Glory to the UPA” (Slawa UPA). While the UPA is remembered by many in Ukraine for fighting for independence from Moscow-imposed Soviet rule, in Poland it is primarily associated with leading the Volhynia massacres, in which around 100,000 Polish civilians, mostly women and children, were slaughtered as part of an ethnic cleansing operation. Local police in Poznań told the Gazeta Wyborcza daily that they were searching for a young man dressed in black who is believed to be the culprit, but have so far not been able to identify him. Similar graffiti was subsequently reported on seven monuments, including ones dedicated to Polish World War Two heroes and anti-communist protests that took place in 1970, in Gdańsk and Gdynia, neighbouring cities on Poland’s northern Baltic coast. On Friday, local police in Gdańsk confirmed that they had detained a 17-year-old Ukrainian on suspicion of “painting offensive slogans propagating hatred”. They shared blurred-out images of the suspect as well as cans of spray paint. He has been charged with promoting fascist ideology, incitement to violence and hatred based on nationality, and desecration of monuments. If convicted, he could face up to three years in prison. Previously, on Tuesday this week, MOST, a Polish-based Belarusian independent media outlet, published findings that an anonymous person on messaging service Telegram, which is popular among Russians, Ukrainians and Belarusians, had been offering $500 plus travel expenses for a job in Poznań. When an undercover MOST journalist responded to the advert, he was told that the job would involve spray painting “Glory to the UPA” on monuments. The recruiter confirmed that the job was illegal, “but if you cover your face and do everything quickly, they won’t find you”. They also revealed that similar jobs were available in other Polish cities, including Warsaw, Wrocław and Lublin. Subsequently, similar inscriptions appeared in Warsaw on the Monument to the Ghetto Heroes, which honours the Jews who rose up against their German-Nazi oppressors in 1943; a monument commemorating the Polish First Army, which fought in World War Two; and a monument to sappers who served in the war. The vandalism was condemned by Poland’s Jewish Historical Institute (ŻIH), which called it a “disgraceful attack on the memory of the victims of the Holocaust and the heroes of Jewish resistance”. Noting MOST’s findings and the vandalism of other monuments, ŻIH said that “this points to the possibility of an organised provocation intended to incite hatred and divide society”. Warsaw police told PAP that they are investigating and seeking to identify the perpetrator. An unnamed police source also told Gazeta Wyborcza they see the incidents in all four cities as related to one another, pointing to the similar style of the inscriptions. On Sunday afternoon, Warsaw’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, condemned the vandalism and shared images of the municipal authorities cleaning the graffiti off the Ghetto Heroes Monument. “Given the scale of similar incidents in other cities, we must consider the possibility that this is a planned provocation,” added the mayor. “Let us not let ourselves be divided – the authorities are working to identify both those who carried out these acts and those who ordered them.” Nie ma zgody na wandalizm w Warszawie. Minionej nocy służby miejskie wyczyściły pomniki oszpecone przez wandali – między innymi Pomnik Bohaterów Getta. Sprawców szuka policja. Patrząc na skalę podobnych incydentów w innych miastach, musimy brać pod uwagę, że mamy do czynienia… pic.twitter.com/5xMgPhnHf8 — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) November 15, 2026 A day earlier, on Saturday, the Ukrainian embassy had also condemned the acts of vandalism, calling them a “disgraceful provocation”. “In our view, these unlawful acts are a manifestation of the hybrid war that Russia is attempting to wage by any means in European states, and in Poland in particular,” wrote the embassy. “The objective is clear: to incite hostility between Poles and Ukrainians, undermine mutual trust, and weaken support for Ukraine.” Writing in both Polish and Ukrainian, the embassy appealed to Ukrainians “not to be tempted by offers of ‘easy money’ in exchange for painting graffiti, damaging property, or carrying out other illegal tasks” and to report any such offers to the Polish police. “Let us respect the laws of the country in which we reside, as well as historical memory and each other’s dignity,” they added. “Polish-Ukrainian solidarity is our shared strength. Let us not allow the enemy to destroy it.” Poland has been a primary target for Russia’s so-called hybrid actions in Europe, which have included acts of sabotage, espionage, disinformation and efforts to stir hostility towards Ukrainians. Such operations are rarely carried out by Russian operatives themselves. Instead, Russia often recruits people already on the ground, often members of Poland’s large Ukrainian and Belarusian migrant communities, as well as Poles themselves in some cases. In July this year, a Ukrainian teenager was indicted by Polish prosecutors on charges of painting dozens of pro-UPA slogans in public places, including on a monument to victims of the Volhynia massacres. An 18-year-old Ukrainian will stand trial in Poland accused of working on behalf of Russia to stir tension between Poland and Ukraine by painting dozens of inscriptions in public places glorifying the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, which massacred Poles in WWII https://t.co/0w0gVYiGpp — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 16, 2026 There have long been tensions between Poland and Ukraine over the massacres, which Poland recognises as a genocide. Ukraine rejects that label, and also continues to honour the UPA for its role in fighting for independence. The issue has recently flared up again this year after President Volodymyr Zelensky named a Ukrainian military unit after the “heroes of the UPA”. That sparked widespread anger in Poland and prompted Polish President Karol Nawrocki to strip Zelensky of his country’s highest honour. World.title: Polish president vetoes law on removing harmful online content, warning of “censorship”
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. President Karol Nawrocki has vetoed a government bill creating new powers to block harmful online content. Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, argued that the measures were too far-reaching and could be abused to introduce “censorship”. Government figures have strongly criticised the president’s decision, arguing that it will leave young people in particular more exposed to dangerous content. It also means that Poland still has not fully implemented the European Union’s Digital Services Act (DSA). ❌ Nie dla cenzury Internetu! pic.twitter.com/WusnK7LImD — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) November 13, 2026 Previously, in January this year, Nawrocki had vetoed an earlier bill intended to implement the DSA, describing the measures as “Owellian”. That prompted the government to split the legislation in two. In September, Nawrocki agreed to sign one of those bills, which appointed the president of the Office of Electronic Communications (UKE) as Poland’s digital services coordinator, responsible for overseeing enforcement of the DSA. A second bill was then needed to introduce the actual powers to block harmful online content. In October, it was approved in parliament by the ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right. The right-wing and far-right opposition either voted against it or abstained. Among the new powers included in the legislation were authorisation for the heads of UKE and the National Broadcasting Council (KRRiT) to order the blocking of online content containing violence or threats based on race, nationality, ethnicity, religion or political affiliation. It also allowed the immediate blocking, at the request of a prosecutor or the police, of content involving the acceptance of a contract to commit murder or inciting or assisting in suicide or self-harm. “Perpetrators of serious crimes should not be allowed to use the internet to spread violence and threats,” said digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski. “The state must have effective tools to quickly respond to such threats. The safety of internet users must transcend political divisions.” The government also argued that last month’s series of stabbings in schools and this month’s deadly terrorist attack in Kraków – which have raised concern about the online radicalisation of young people – have emphasised the importance of tough controls over digital content. There are "strong traces of right-wing extremism" in the activity of the man who carried out the mass shooting in Kraków, says Poland's justice minister. His search history included websites relating to Anders Breivik, the Norwegian far-right terrorist https://t.co/UhVbkWSaCq — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 10, 2026 However, on Friday, the final day by which the president had to make a decision on the bill, Nawrocki announced that he was vetoing it. He argued that “the government has clearly mixed up European obligations with its own political interests”. The measures in the bill threaten to create a “censorship official” and “essentially give the government arbitrary control and the ability to decide what we can and cannot say, write or publish, said the president. Decisions on whether content is permitted or not should be “the exclusive competence of the justice system and independent judges”, he argued. Nawrocki also said that the powers in the vetoed bill were “disproportionate”, allowing an entire domain to be blocked due to a single example of illegal content. “The security of citizens cannot be a pretext for weakening their freedoms,” said Nawrocki. “We must not create a false choice: either the security or the freedom of its citizens. A responsible state must ensure and balance both.” Dlaczego Prezydent RP Karol Nawrocki zawetował ustawę o DSA? ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/1BUJVFEftl — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) November 13, 2026 Deputy digital affairs minister Dariusz Standerski, however, said that the president was “not defending free speech” but instead “once again siding with global [digital] platforms and allowing them to decide what users see”. “The vetoed provisions concerned illegal content, not opinions or views expressed online,” added the ministry, which also noted that all decisions on blocking content were subject to appeals and judicial review. Prime Minister Donald Tusk, meanwhile, accused Nawrocki of “waging war on the government at the expense of Polish children and Polish security”, which would both be threatened by the absence of the vetoed measures. Z prezydenckiego weta zadowoleni są hejterzy, rosyjskie farmy trolli, pedofile, ekstremalni nihiliści i lobbyści. Ofiarami tego weta są polskie dzieci, rodzice, bezpieczeństwo wszystkich obywateli. Tego nie da się w żaden sposób usprawiedliwić. — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) November 14, 2026 Aleksandra Wójtowicz, an analyst on new technologies at the Polish Institute of International Affairs (PISM), told the Fakt newspaper that the measures do “not in any way relate to alleged censorship”. They are intended to force digital platforms to remove illegal content, she explained. Wójtowicz added that the measures would actually have protected free speech by giving Polish users whose accounts were unjustly deleted by social media platforms the right to appeal against those decisions outside of the platform itself. However, Nawrocki’s veto was praised by Przemysław Czarnek, deputy leader of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s largest opposition party. Czarnek told TV Trwam that the proposed measures had been intended to “fight the opposition” rather than actual hate speech. World.title: Poland research hub launched at Oxford University
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
