World.title: India crush Pakistan’s SAFF Championship dream with late comeback in Dhaka
World.content:
RIYADH: What could have been a historic night for the Pakistan national football team ended in heartbreak after archrivals India came from behind to win 2-1 late on at the National Stadium in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

The six-team 2026 SAFF Championship concluded on Tuesday after a hard-fought battle that saw Pakistan initially dominate, only to crumble after going down to 10 men.

The final was a repeat of the teams’ championship opener on Nov. 5, when India scored three first-half goals that went unanswered until injury time. Pakistan then scored twice in three minutes of stoppage time, but India held on to win 3-2.

India eventually topped Group B and beat Bhutan in the semifinals to reach their 14th final, while a late goal from Abdul Samad Arshad in the same round guided Pakistan to a 1-0 victory over hosts Bangladesh and into their first final.

Arshad, who was not available for the defeat to India in the group stage due to the match falling outside FIFA days, added much-needed impetus to the Pakistani team alongside fellow Scandinavia-based arrival Abdullah Iqbal.

On Tuesday the now strengthened Pakistan came in with a completely different energy, dominating the first 45 minutes of the final and keeping India scoreless during that period.

Nolberto Solano set the Shaheens up in a 5-4-1, which largely nullified the Indian attack’s threat and allowed the central midfielders to exploit the space behind striker McKeal Abdullah. The striker almost opened the scoring in the 18th minute with a flying backheel off the end of right-back Haris Zeb’s cross, but India goalkeeper Arsh Anwer Shaikh did well to keep the ball out.

India responded in the 34th minute with their best chance of the first half, after a scramble over the ball in the Pakistan area fell to Ricky Shabong on the volley. This time it was Pakistan’s goalkeeper Yousuf Butt who turned hero with a powerful save to keep the score level.

Pakistan waited until the final moments of the first half to take a deserved lead, when a low cross from Junaid Shah was misdirected by Khaiminthang Lhungdim into the path of Alamgir Khan, who unleashed a curler past Shaikh into the far corner.

The Shaheens emerged in a buoyant mood in the second half but ultimately paid the price for a rash tackle by Shah. He lunged at winger Brison Fernandes with a high foot and after a VAR review was sent off for violent conduct on the hour mark.

Within seconds of the red card, exciting young striker Suhail Bhatt capitalized on a lapse in concentration from the Pakistan defense to finish a cross from Lhungdim that was nudged his way by Mackarton Nickson to equalize for the Blue Tigers.

And from that moment India never looked back. In the 88th minute substitute Abdul Rabeeh delivered a perfectly placed corner for Sandip Mandi to head toward goal. The ball bounced off the ground and up toward Butt, who misjudged its flight and watched it edge past his hand into the net. The goal secured a 2-1 victory and the championship for India.

India, who sent a second-string squad to Bangladesh while their main senior side played friendlies in New Zealand, have now won the SAFF Championship three times in a row for the first time in their history.

For Pakistan, the final told a different story. After reaching this stage for the first time, the Shaheens were expected to end their trophy drought, which stretches back to their gold medal at the South Asian Games in 1991. While the wait will continue, Solano and co. have plenty to look forward to as the Shaheens continue to rise on the international football stage.

World.title: UN warns winter could reverse fragile food security gains in Gaza
World.content:
LONDON: Harsh winter weather could reverse the fragile improvements to food security achieved in the embattled Gaza Strip, as critical funding shortages and Israeli restrictions on aid deliveries threaten efforts to provide food and shelter for displaced families, UN agencies warned on Tuesday.

The International Organization for Migration and the World Food Programme said the gains continued to depend largely on humanitarian assistance, rather than any improvements in livelihoods, markets or local food production.

Meanwhile, the increasingly severe seasonal weather was damaging shelters and spoiling food supplies, increasing pressure on families already struggling to meet their basic needs.

More than 1.7 million people remain displaced in Gaza, 1.4 million face acute levels of hunger, and nearly 2 million need shelter assistance, the agencies warned.

“Families in Gaza are facing their first sleepless nights of a very long winter ahead,” said Shaun Hughes, the WFP’s country director for Palestine.

“Unless we get immediate support to scale up the humanitarian response, we risk this becoming not only a shelter crisis but also a deeper food security crisis.”

Funding shortages have already forced the WFP to reduce hot meals to one every other day and cut the amounts of food parcels and cash assistance it provides. Meanwhile, flooding has destroyed household food supplies, and sewage contamination poses additional food-safety and health risks, the agencies said.

Supplies of gas and firewood for cooking remain scarce and unaffordable, forcing many families to burn garbage to prepare meals. With 80 percent of the population unemployed, households have few resources available to replace lost supplies or buy more nutritious food.

The WFP faces a $436 million funding gap over the next six months as it attempts to provide aid for 2 million people across the Palestinian territories. According to the latest Integrated Food Security Phase Classification assessment, as many as 1.9 million people, about 90 percent of Gaza’s population, could face acute levels of food insecurity by the end of this year unless humanitarian assistance can be adequately sustained.

The threats to food security are compounded by the deteriorating condition of shelters; at least 40,000 have reportedly been damaged or destroyed since early November alone, the agencies said, and stocks of emergency shelters were rapidly running out.

“Displaced families in Gaza need the basics to get through this winter: a shelter that won’t flood, blankets and clothing to protect children, and fuel to cook warm meals,” said Karl Baker, the International Organization for Migration’s regional crisis coordinator.

His organization needs $173 million to sustain its shelter response, including tents, tarpaulins, blankets and repair materials, and another $9 million for site management and improvements such as drainage channels, lighting and community heating points.

The entire population of Gaza has been forced into an area that is less than 40 percent of the territory as a whole, and more than half of the 1,700 displacement sites are in flood-prone areas, the agencies said. Most of the sites need sandbags to reinforce shelters and pathways, and more than 40 percent require drainage and ground improvements.

Ongoing Israeli restrictions on deliveries of aid are further hampering the humanitarian response. Kerem Shalom, also known as Kerem Abu Salem, remains the only authorized crossing point for humanitarian and commercial goods entering Gaza, which increases transportation times and costs, the agencies said.

Restrictions on the main north-south route in Gaza add to those difficulties. Attempts to deliver essential winter supplies and equipment, including water pumps, spare parts, heaters, fuel, engine oil, heavy machinery and wood, also face delays or entry restrictions.

The agencies said they were working with other UN organizations and humanitarian partners to coordinate deliveries so that they can reach those most in need.

“Partnerships between IOM and WFP help ensure aid is delivered efficiently,” Baker said. “But we need the resources and consistent, predictable access to do our jobs.”

World.title: Tensions rise over COP31 draft deal
World.content:
ANTALYA: Climate negotiators warned Tuesday that a sprawling and contentious draft COP31 deal set the stage for tough negotiations before the UN talks in Turkiye end later this week.



The 18-page draft “cover decision” published by co-host Australia includes a broad range of demands, from calls for a phaseout of fossil fuels to a defense of climate science and age-old battles over finance.



“It is hugely important that here at this COP that is about implementation, we do not get distracted by other things,” the European Union’s climate envoy, Wopke Hoekstra, said in a speech.



“And to be frank, that is unfortunately what the draft cover decision is doing,” he said, warning ministers assembled in Antalya that it could make the process “untenable.”



Hoekstra later told reporters that while the document includes elements that the EU likes, it had “many of the characteristics of a shopping list” that reopens old issues.



“I think the cover decision does not go in the right direction and needs significant change,” he said.



Some European officials described the text as a “Christmas wish list” that, by trying to make everyone happy, is not making anybody happy.



Australian Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who is steering COP31 negotiations, acknowledged when he released the document on Monday that the text included elements “that not all parties agree on.”



Bowen said there would be “at least one more draft” before the end of the week.

- ‘Kitchen sink approach’ -

The talks are scheduled to end on Friday, but climate negotiations usually run into overtime as agreements must be reached by consensus, meaning even a single country can block the entire process.



A Latin American official, who requested anonymity, said the document is too long and warned that the “clock is ticking.”



“We would like to have a short, sharp cover decision,” said another European negotiator, who described the Australian strategy as a “kitchen sink approach.”



“So we’ve got a long journey to go from what we’ve got to what we’d like to see,” the negotiator said.



The text includes a call for wealthy nations to achieve net zero emissions by 2030 — a target few could hope to realistically meet.



“Emerging countries want to impose as many obligations as possible on developed countries. It’s tactical,” said another official from a European country who requested anonymity.



“These things are obviously unacceptable,” the official said, pointing to a bloc of countries whose members include Saudi Arabia and India.

- Fossil fight -

The draft includes wording on phasing out fossil fuels that oil-rich countries have long resisted.



“We would love to see a commitment that calls on the phasing out of fossil fuels,” Michael Joseph, the environment minister of Antigua and Barbuda, told AFP.



But he acknowledged that getting consensus on the issue at COP31 “might be very, very difficult.”



Saudi Arabia is also at the center of another battle over the timeline for the publication of crucial reports by the UN’s climate science panel.



Dozens of European, African and Pacific nations want the next Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) reports published ahead of a crucial stocktake of global carbon-cutting efforts at COP33 in 2028.



But Saudi Arabia and India are among a smaller number of countries accused of pushing for the IPCC’s “seventh assessment report” to be delayed until 2029.



Saudi Arabia’s COP31 delegation defended its stance on Tuesday, saying the kingdom “advocates publication timelines that allow sufficient scientific review, transparency and meaningful participation, particularly from developing countries.”



Ilana Seid, who chairs the Alliance of Small Island States, said the IPCC report must be ready for the global stocktake and that any delay “is unjustifiable to us.”

World.title: UK’s William says world must act urgently on climate at Indian awards ceremony
World.content:
MUMBAI: Britain’s Prince William said the impact of climate ​change was now clear to see but gave an upbeat message that positive action would become “irreversible” as he announced the winners of his annual environmental awards on Tuesday.

At a glittering awards ceremony in Mumbai for the Earthshot Prize, the heir to the British throne said the impact of global warming was becoming conspicuous, with repeated heatwaves and devastating floods, calling it a pivotal moment for the planet.

“We cannot look into the eyes of the next generation and tell them that we knew what was happening, we knew ‌what was at stake, ‌and yet we did not do everything in ​our ‌power ⁠to change it,” ​he ⁠said.

“They will not judge us by the promises we made, but by the world we leave behind. And they deserve a generation prepared to act with urgency, determination and optimism.”

Prize held amid COP31 talks

William, 44, set up Earthshot six years ago with the aim of finding practical solutions to climate change, giving five winners £1 million ($1.3 million) each to scale up their projects.

The latest ceremony coincided with the UN’s COP31 climate talks, which have highlighted the difficulty ⁠in finding agreement between countries over fossil fuels and climate financing.

A UN ‌report last month said the world is already ‌on course to exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warming ​threshold, a level scientists say should ‌limit the worst effects of climate change.

Despite the gloomy background, William said he believed people ‌were rising to meet the challenge, heralding the innovation of the latest Earthshot Prize winners as testament to the ability to produce answers to the growing challenges.

The winners included Mumbai-based electric vehicle maker Mahindra Last Mile Mobility and the Kingdom of Bhutan for requiring 60 percent of its land to ‌stay under forest cover.

“I choose to believe that this will be the decade where positive change becomes irreversible,” William said. “To ⁠our finalists, and to ⁠everyone choosing action over apathy, thank you for proving that change is possible.”

William joined by wife Catherine

At the ceremony, hosted by Bollywood filmmaker Karan Johar, the prince was joined by Indian cricketing great Sachin Tendulkar, actors Alia Bhatt and Rami Malek, and British pop group Take That, who gave their first-ever performance in India.

William’s wife Catherine, on her most high-profile overseas visit since receiving treatment for cancer in 2024, also presented one of the awards.

“The people we’re celebrating tonight are a huge part of that story,” said the princess, 44, often referred to by her maiden name Kate Middleton. “Their work will inspire and create seismic change that will improve lives for generations to come.”

Earlier, William drove Catherine ​in a Mahindra electric auto-rickshaw through Mumbai, ​India’s financial capital, before a meeting with the Earthshot finalists.

Their three-day visit concludes on Wednesday when they will meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi.

World.title: Diallo wants to restore “broken” trust in soccer as he challenges Infantino for FIFA presidency
World.content:
PARIS: French soccer leader Philippe Diallo wants to restore “broken” trust in the sport’s governance and rid the game of the “poison of division” after confirming his intention on Tuesday to challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency.

His candidacy was ratified following an executive committee meeting at the French soccer federation’s headquarters in Paris.

“A few days ago, my colleagues from the UEFA Executive Committee asked me if I could carry this voice in the world of football,” Diallo, 63, said. “I wasn’t initially a candidate, but the insistence of my European colleagues led me to accept the offer to be the candidate for the FIFA presidency.”

UEFA is pursuing legal action in US courts and seeks discovery of evidence for a possible criminal complaint against Infantino in his and FIFA’s home country Switzerland alleging financial mismanagement. FIFA hit back by accusing UEFA of “smear campaign.”

Concerns include Infantino seeming to act alone in creating a peace prize for US President Donald Trump last year and, at the World Cup, letting United States forward Folarin Balogun avoid a mandatory ban for a red card after Trump intervened.

“There have been a series of decisions taken inside FIFA: I think of the peace prize, I think of the distribution of revenue of television rights in the United States, the red card for Balogun, the length of the halftime break in the final and the private investors (sell-off plan),” Diallo said.

“All of these decisions shocked the world of football in a very big way, the fans, the clubs, the sponsors, the federations.”

Diallo said “there are a lot of questions” for Infantino and that the fall-out has seriously damaged the game.

“It created a situation this summer whereby the trust placed in FIFA and it’s president was broken,” he said. “They have damaged the image of football and have introduced the poison of division.”

UEFA, European soccer’s ruling body, proposed Diallo on Monday after a meeting of its 21-member executive committee that includes the French Football Federation president.

He joins Japanese official Kohzo Tashima as an official entry in the March 18 election, with entries required by a FIFA-set deadline of midnight Swiss time (2300 GMT) on Wednesday.

“I could not shy away from the demands. I think I have the experience, the convictions and the values which offer a credible alternative,” Diallo said. “Football deserves a credible change which I represent. I am candidate for the FIFA presidency. What happened in recent months was shocking.”

Who is Diallo?

Diallo sat smiling alongside Zinedine Zidane when he was announced as France’s new national team coach in late July.

Diallo is a long-time soccer administrator with French clubs, and the league, who rose to interim president at the FFF in January 2023, before being fast-tracked in an election of UEFA member federations to join the European body’s executive committee.

Diallo has worked for world soccer’s ruling body FIFA as a judge on its Dispute Resolution Chamber, handling contract disputes between players and clubs.

Until his emergence, speculation on a candidate focused on Qatari soccer and broadcast executive Nasser Al-Khelaïfi, the president of Champions League titleholder Paris Saint-Germain and a UEFA executive committee member. He said he would not run against Infantino, who has backing from Qatar.

Focus them shifted onto former Arsenal coach Arsène Wenger, hired by FIFA since 2019 as the global head of developing the game. He made it clear he would not stand.

When the World Cup ended on July 19, Infantino was set to be re-elected unopposed effectively by a coronation. FIFA said he had about 200 letters of support from the 211 member federations who will vote in March in Rabat, Morocco.

One of those letters was from France.

But Diallo formally withdrew the FFF in September, citing that trust in Infantino was broken by the World Cup sell-off plan secretly devised with Joshua Kushner, the younger brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.

“The last time I saw him (Infantino) was at the World Cup, he came to a few France games,” Diallo said. “I regret, as others did, that he did not share the ideas of his projects ... it was an unacceptable act of defiance.”

Chasing money?

Diallo said the 48-team men’s 2026 World Cup generated record profits of $15-16 million, vastly more than the 2022 edition of 32 teams in Qatar. Therefore the sell-off plan, which “no one really understands,” was totally baffling.

“FIFA’s (cash) reserves are $5-6 million,” Diallo said. “We find it hard to understand ... the need to find private investors to bring further billions, when these billions are already here.”

Infantino has promised at least $25 million in development funds to each member federation through 2030.

“(Cash) reserves that had lay dormant for years and would still be dormant in FIFA accounts if we had not intervened,” Diallo said. “There are a lot of things that need answering, there is no clarity regarding this and there are curious strategies.”

Infantino’s critics

Germany coach Jürgen Klopp said Infantino has turned out worse than Blatter.

Diallo will announce his campaign team in Belfast in early December.

“I will have a clear program of solidarity and excellence, and guarantee those who love soccer that these values will be respected,” he said.

Diallo said he can count on the support, too, of French President Emmanuel Macron, and that he has been “pleasantly surprised” by the number of people from the African and Asian soccer federations offering him their support.

Although no African or Asian federation has publicly expressed support for Diallo, he is optimistic that will soon change.

“It’s down to me, with a whole team, to go and convince other continents,” he said. “Since yesterday, I have already received strong and firm signs of support from other continents, which will be revealed in the coming days.”

World.title: Quds Force commander meets Iraqi officials, leaders of armed factions in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani arrived in Baghdad on Monday evening on an urgent mission to defuse tension between the Iraqi government and the Iran-backed armed faction Kataib Hezbollah.

Reports mentioned that Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei dispatched Qaani directly to prevent the dispute from turning into an armed confrontation.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi issued a deadline requiring Kataib Hezbollah to vacate the strategic Jurf al-Sakhar district in Iraq’s central province of Babil by the weekend or face a military assault by Iraqi Counter-Terrorism forces.

The government’s attempts to organize weapons under state control and deal with suspected faction-linked smuggling in the region—which Kataib Hezbollah disputes—are the root causes of the issue. According to reports, both sides have increased their military presence in the district.

Qaani met with members of the Kataib Hezbollah Shura Council and leaders of the Coordination Framework to advocate for political involvement in opposition to a military solution and to call for de-escalation.

There has not been any immediate progress in the initial discussions. According to reports, al-Zaidi turned down a meeting with Qaani, insisting that the government’s attempt to reclaim Jurf al-Sakhar is unavoidable, despite ongoing backchannel attempts.

World.title: Iraq resumes oil flows via rehabilitated Kirkuk–Ceyhan pipeline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq officially resumed on Tuesday crude oil exports through the rehabilitated Kirkuk–Ceyhan pipeline to Turkey.

Pumping restarted at an initial rate of 120,000 barrels per day following a 12-year hiatus.

Operations began at 120,000 barrels per day from the IT1A station through a 46-inch pipeline to the MS metering station.

Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair confirmed that flows will gradually scale up to 500,000 barrels per day, though a specific timeline for reaching full target capacity has not been announced.

Technical teams from the state-run North Oil Company completed extensive maintenance, hydrostatic testing, and operational checks to restore the federal line.

The 960-kilometer pipeline had been inactive since March 2014 due to severe damage caused by repeated attacks carried out by the terrorist group of ISIS.

The restart operates under a one-year interim agreement signed between Baghdad and Ankara in August 2026. That deal sets a minimum transportation capacity of 750,000 bpd through the Turkish system to the Mediterranean port of Ceyhan.

Baghdad has prioritized northern and overland export corridors since the outbreak of the military conflict in the Middle East in late February 2026, which severely disrupted maritime shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Mövenpick to open lakeside resort near Erbil in 2030
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Accor, a global hospitality business, has collaborated with Erbil-based KRD Holding to develop the Mövenpick Erbil Gomaspan Resort, a 150-room luxury resort overlooking Gomaspan Dam about 35 kilometers northeast of Erbil.

The project, set to open in 2030, will be Mövenpick’s first hotel in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region and second in the nation, after the Mövenpick Hotel Al Zaytoon in Baghdad.

The resort will have hotel rooms and suites, restaurants, bars, a spa, swimming pools, a fitness center, and over 1,300 square meters of meeting and event space.

The plans also include a lakeside corniche with restaurants and cafés, a dining island encircled by the dam’s waters, and an adventure sports area featuring safari trails, quad riding, mountain motorcycling, and skydiving.

On September 29, Accor and KRD Holding inked a development agreement with the goal of luring both local and international visitors to the hilly terrain around Erbil.

Gomaspan Dam, which opened in October 2024, is the largest dam in Erbil Governorate and was built largely to support irrigation and fish farming, with the aim of boosting tourism in the surrounding region.

World.title: Chinese refiners ramp up Iraqi crude purchases
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Chinese independent refineries have ramped up purchases of Iraqi crude oil via international trading houses at narrower premiums, capitalizing on stabilized Gulf export flows, ample regional supply, and softer global benchmark prices, according to market traders cited by Reuters.

The surge in buying activity centers on China’s independent “teapot” refiners—primarily clustered in the eastern province of Shandong—seeking to utilize their remaining year-end crude import quotas while replacing sanctioned Iranian barrels choked off by the ongoing U.S. naval blockade.

Traders reported that spot premiums for Iraqi grades have dropped back into single-digit territory as trading firms lowered offers amid steady Gulf shipments. In recent deals, ADNOC Trading sold cargoes of both Basrah Medium and Basrah Heavy to an independent refinery in Shandong for late-December delivery at a premium of roughly $6 per barrel above March ICE Brent futures.

Similarly, TotalEnergies’ trading arm, TOTSA, sold 2 million barrels of Basrah Heavy to a Chinese independent refiner for January delivery at a premium ranging between $7 and $8 per barrel over ICE Brent.

Parallel transactions across other regional Gulf grades reflected a similar pricing trend. Mercuria sold 2 million barrels of the UAE’s Upper Zakum crude to an independent Chinese refiner for second-half January delivery at roughly $8 per barrel over March Brent, while Vitol sold 1 million barrels of Qatar’s Al-Shaheen crude to another Shandong processor for February delivery at around $9 per barrel over February Brent.

Several converging commercial factors accelerated Chinese demand for Iraqi barrels. A sharp pullback in ICE Brent crude futures following the U.S. midterm elections—combined with declining tanker freight rates—improved refining margins for private Chinese processors.

Furthermore, data intelligence analysts note that Iraqi crude currently ranks among the most competitively priced grades of comparable quality on a delivered-China basis, offering prompt cargo availability at a time when Russian ESPO barrels remain prohibitively expensive due to competition from Chinese state-owned majors. With year-end deadlines approaching, independent refiners are moving quickly to exhaust their remaining 2026 import quotas before expiration.

World.title: US dollar holds above 171,000 dinars across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar recorded a renewed upward tick across major domestic parallel markets on Tuesday morning, November 17, 2026, holding firmly above the 171,000 IQD threshold across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra.

According to morning trading figures across key commercial hubs, physical banknote rates traded as follows:

Baghdad: Currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 171,050 IQD against buying offers of 170,250 IQD per $100.

Erbil: Currency desks quoted selling rates at 171,250 IQD alongside buying bids of 170,500 IQD per $100.

Basra: Foreign exchange offices matched Erbil’s selling ceiling at 171,250 IQD, with purchasing offers settling firmer at 170,750 IQD per $100.

This sustained parallel-market elevation maintains a spread of more than 19,000 dinars above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar)—a peg established following the government’s October 7, 2026 currency adjustment.

The persistent premium reflects heightened domestic political and security uncertainty alongside continued physical cash demand to settle unrecorded cross-border imports outside formal electronic banking channels.

World.title: Sirens activated after drone flew over Iraq’s Khor Mor gas field
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Warning sirens were activated at the Khor Mor gas field in Iraqi Kurdistan on Monday after an unidentified drone flew over the facility.

Two security sources confirmed the alert to Reuters, noting there were no immediate reports of a strike, casualties, or new damage.

Security officials have not identified who launched the drone. Kurdish authorities have previously attributed similar threats against the site to Iran-backed armed factions.

The overflight comes just one week after a drone attack targeted the gas field on September 8, forcing joint field operator Dana Gas to halt production entirely.

The strike hit a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) storage tank, causing a large fire that was later extinguished.

The facility is the main source of energy for the Kurdistan region of Iraq and the largest gas field there.

Between 2,500 and 2,800 megawatts of power output had been cut off due to the stoppage of gas operations, reducing 70 to 80 percent of the energy grid’s overall capacity.

Iraqi Kurdistan’s major cities, including Erbil, Sulaimaniyah, Duhok, Bazian, and Chamchamal, were no longer receiving direct electricity supply.

The facility was temporarily closed in July due to security concerns resulting from escalating military tensions between the United States and Iran.

World.title: Iraqi security identifies two illegal oil refineries in Jurf al-Nasr
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi authorities uncovered two illegal oil refineries, storage facilities, and evidence of pipeline tampering in the Jurf al-Nasr, also known as Jurf al-Sakhar, area in Iraq’s central province of Babil.

The discoveries were confirmed following a high-level government investigation launched by Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and a parliamentary inquiry.

Six places were investigated by government detectives, who found two refineries operating illegally, oil tanks, and a tanker truck, as well as hidden changes in state oil pipelines.

A parliamentary committee examined drone footage, thermal images, and documents indicating around 25 tanker trucks, each with the capacity to carry 36,000 liters, were used within the smugglers’ network.

According to reports, the illicit operations had been ongoing since 2021, developing from exposed oil pits to covered loading points and underground storage to avoid being detected.

Following an emergency security meeting on Saturday, al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior security, intelligence, and oil-sector officials. He also ordered all individuals implicated in the smuggling operations to be referred to the judiciary for prosecution.

On Monday, government spokesperson Haider al-Aboudi announced that al-Zaidi ordered Iraqi troops into Jurf al-Nasr to restore state control and dismantle the networks.

Authorities also gave the Iran-backed armed group Kataib Hezbollah, which controls Jurf al-Nasr, until the weekend as a deadline to withdraw.

World.title: West Bank’s displaced Palestinians hold little hope for post-Netanyahu era
World.content:
Tulkarem – After Israeli forces pushed him and thousands of others out of the West Bank refugee camp of Tulkarem last year, Adel Darsieh held onto his hope of returning home, but it is fading fast.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed no return for the displaced people from the camp near the northern city of Jenin, known as a hub for militants.

He is now fighting for his political life after his party lost seats in Israel’s general election last month and former general Gadi Eisenkot was tasked with trying to form a new government.

But even the prospect of an end to Netanyahu’s rule is not enough to lift Darsieh’s hopes.

“Whether it’s this government or a new one, what does it change?” said the 64-year-old. “They’re two sides of the same coin.”

The Israeli military carried out a major operation in the north of the occupied Palestinian territory in early 2025, during a temporary ceasefire in Hamas-ruled Gaza, having vowed to root out extremists.

Shortly before the election, Netanyahu announced that no one removed from Tulkarem would be allowed back.

For Palestinian families, it is a second form of displacement. The Tulkarem camp was set up in 1950 for refugees who fled or were forced out during the creation of the state of Israel two years earlier. The West Bank has been occupied by Israel since 1967.

“Successive generations have lived through displacement without being able to return to their homes. If our grandparents and parents couldn’t return, how can we believe that our return will be possible?” Darsieh said.

According to UN figures, the Israeli operation launched last year displaced 12,100 people from the Tulkarem camp.

– ‘Empty stomachs’ –

With the Israeli military keeping up periodic operations around the region, Darsieh is living near the camp in a modest, makeshift home with a sheet metal roof. His wife uses a wheelchair.

He went to receive trays of mansaf, a dish of rice, meat and fermented yoghurt, prepared by Fazaa Kitchen, a solidarity group that serves food to the displaced.

Working from the building of the Wadi al-Hawarith charity, volunteers in orange jackets fill, seal and package portions of food in an assembly line.

The group prepares and distributes some 1,200 meals to 400 families.

“If we weren’t cooking, families would be going to bed with empty stomachs,” said the organisation’s head, Hussein al-Sheikh Ali, 60, who himself is displaced.

He described Israel’s actions in the West Bank since the Gaza war — a conflict launched in response to the unprecedented attack on Israel by Hamas on October 7, 2023 — as “collective punishment”.

Netanyahu’s now-caretaker government, which includes far-right figures, rapidly expanded Israeli settlements in the West Bank which are considered illegal under international law.

“Some Palestinians hope that a new Israeli government might emerge with a less extremist, more moderate tone,” Ali said.

“Yet the fear remains that the same policies towards the Palestinians will persist, even if the political figures themselves change.”

Faisal Salama, who heads Tulkarem camp’s popular committee, which represents residents, called Netanyahu’s decision to stop residents returning illegal.

But he held out guarded hope for an end to military operations. He pointed to how Israel, soon after the election, ended an operation in Hebron that displaced 3,000 Palestinians, which was launched after gunmen shot dead two Israeli soldiers.

– ‘Scale of suffering’ –

Even if residents could return, much of the camp has been destroyed. Houses have been razed, buildings emptied and businesses burnt down.

Eisenkot, who commanded forces in the West Bank during the second Intifada, a Palestinian uprising from 2000 to 2005, has sought to appeal to a broad spectrum including liberals but has only taken some distance from Netanyahu on security.

Eisenkot backs the existence of the major settlements but has also spoken out forcefully against extremist settlers who have attacked Palestinians with virtual impunity.

Beth Oppenheim, a policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, said a consensus has emerged among Jewish Israelis on key policies on the West Bank, including opposition to the creation of a Palestinian state.

Still, she said that Eisenkot as prime minister could be more flexible on allowing a return to Tulkarem.

“I think that given the political atmosphere in Israel today, this will be done through a security pretext,” she said.

“They would make the case that this is necessary to stabilise the situation in the West Bank and that having people displaced could create the conditions for unrest,” she said.

For Asia Assaf, 44, a Fazaa Kitchen volunteer whose home was destroyed in March 2025, political debates are far away from her daily concerns.

“One cannot truly grasp the scale of suffering until one has experienced it firsthand,” she said.

World.title: 'Have they read SC order?' Karnataka CM DKS questions Tamil Nadu parties opposing Mekedatu project
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Tuesday questioned political parties in Tamil Nadu opposing the Mekedatu dam project, asking whether they had read the Supreme Court's order on Cauvery water sharing.

He said Karnataka was bound to release water to Tamil Nadu under the court's directions and would continue to do so.

Shivakumar's remarks came amid renewed opposition to the proposed dam from Tamil Nadu parties, including the AIADMK, DMK and PMK. He said the Supreme Court had already considered Tamil Nadu's objections through a revision petition and questioned what further opportunity the state had to challenge the matter.



"I want to ask AIADMK, DMK and any other parties if they have seen the Supreme Court order. The SC order clearly states that we are bound to give them (Tamil Nadu) water, and we will do so. They went to court with a revision petition too. But what happened? What more opportunity do they have?" news agency ANI quoted Shivakumar saying.

DKS speaks about meeting Tamil Nadu CM Vijay

The Karnataka chief minister was also asked about his meeting with Tamil Nadu CM Vijay at the launch of Sonia Gandhi's book in Delhi on Monday.





Shivakumar said the two leaders shared friendly relations despite their political challenges.

"Of course, we are friends. They have their own political problems," he said.

PMK chief opposes Mekedatu project

Meanwhile, PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss strongly opposed the proposed Mekedatu dam, saying Tamil Nadu would not allow Karnataka to begin construction.

Speaking to reporters in Chennai, Ramadoss said the Cauvery was a lifeline for Tamil Nadu and accused the Karnataka chief minister of making misleading claims about the Supreme Court's position on the project.

"The Cauvery issue is a lifeline for Tamil Nadu. We have been enjoying Cauvery water for thousands and thousands of years, and suddenly some CM from Karnataka comes and says, ' This is our right...you just can't build a dam suddenly. And now, the Karnataka chief minister, with the Prime Minister on stage, is saying that this is their right, that they have to build this dam, and that the Supreme Court has given permission.

A chief minister lying in front of the country is unheard of,â Ramadoss said.

He maintained that the Supreme Court had not given Karnataka permission to construct the dam and warned that his party would oppose any attempt to take the project forward.

âThe Supreme Court has not given any permission for Karnataka to build a dam...the Mekedatu Dam will not be built; we will not allow even one brick to be laid. This is completely Tamil Nadu's lifeline...the

Tamil Nadu government definitely needs to convene an all-party meeting. I have requested the Tamil Nadu government to convene this meeting more than a hundred times...if Karnataka builds a dam upstream and takes controlâwhich doesn't listen to the Cauvery Tribunal, doesn't listen to the Supreme Court, doesn't listen to the Central Water Commission, and doesn't listen to any law or agreementâthen we are finished.

The Mekedatu project envisages a balancing reservoir across the Cauvery river in Karnataka. It has been a longstanding point of dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, with the latter objecting to the project over concerns about its impact on the state's share of Cauvery water.

World.title: Bird hits IndiGo flight at Navi Mumbai airport after arrival, grounded
World.content:

NEW DELHI: An IndiGo flight from Mangaluru reported a bird strike on Tuesday after arriving at Navi Mumbai Airport, news agency PTI reported, citing a source.According to the source, the bird hit the right side of the aircraft's fuselage. The aircraft has since been grounded for inspection, the source added."The Navi Mumbai-bound IndiGo flight 6E 865 from Mangaluru reported a bird hit on its arrival at the Navi Mumbai International Airport on Tuesday," the source told PTI.Meanwhile, IndiGo confirmed the incident and said that "the aircraft is grounded and will resume operations after necessary checks."According to PTI, the airline, however, declined to issue a statement on the incident.Earlier in the day, an IndiGo aircraft flying from Mangaluru to Bengaluru aborted take-off due to a technical issue. The aircraft subsequently returned to the bay and was later declared Aircraft on Ground (AOG).All 229 passengers and seven crew members on board were safely deplaned, with no injuries reported.The incidents come as the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is conducting an audit of India's aviation safety oversight standards, mainly covering aircraft operations, airworthiness and personnel licensing.The audit, which commenced on November 16, will continue until November 20, according to an official.Currently, India has Category 1 status under the FAA's aviation safety assessment programme. Under its International Aviation Safety Assessment (IASA) programme, the FAA determines whether a country's oversight of air carriers that operate, or seek to operate, in the US or codeshare with a US carrier complies with safety standards established by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).The IASA programme focuses on a country's ability to adhere to international aviation safety standards and recommended practices relating to personnel licensing, aircraft operations and airworthiness.

World.title: 'Squandered nation’s best opportunity': Ex-ally Akhil Gogoi accuses Congress of weakening CJP agitation
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress' former ally and Raijor Dal MLA Akhil Gogoi on Tuesday accused the grand old party and Lok Sabha leader of opposition

of weakening the Cockroach Janata Dal (CJP) agitation through "parallel protests".

In a letter sent to Rahul, Gogoi described the CJP agitation as the "single most powerful and effective people's movement capable of shaking this dictatorship" since 2014. The Raijor Dal MLA also warned that the Opposition cannot unseat the government in 2029 without backing an independent mass movement.

âAs someone who has spent his entire life on the streets fighting alongside peasants, workers, and the masses â not inside air-conditioned rooms, your continued silence troubles me deeply," Gogoi said in the letter.



âEvery conscious citizen who sees where India is heading wants to remove this BJP-RSS regime, which is systematically selling off our national resources and handing over every market to a handful of favoured corporates. Let me state this clearly from decades of grassroots struggle: if there is no independent peopleâs movement, there is no chance of changing this communal-fascist government,â the letter read.

Gogoi also said that Congress had weakened the genuine mass revolt by dividing the streets and competing with the movement, claiming that the move gave the government room to contain it.





âSince 2014, the CJP agitation has been the single most powerful and effective peopleâs movement capable of shaking this dictatorship. Within five months, it awakened the youth where traditional opposition politics had failed for twelve years. Yet, instead of standing solidly behind this organic uprising, the Indian National Congress launched parallel protests. By dividing the streets and competing with a genuine mass revolt, your party weakened the CJP movement, gave the ruling regime room to contain it, and squandered the nationâs best opportunity for a decisive fight,â he wrote.

âYou cannot defeat a fascist regime through party control or press-conference politics. Real political change only happens through an honest, independent peopleâs movement backed unconditionally by the opposition,â he added.

Warning of the oppositionâs electoral prospects in 2029, Gogoi wrote, âOtherwise, even if you disagree with me, I must tell you plainly that the opposition will not be able to overthrow this peopleâs enemy government in 2029.â

This was the third letter Gogoi had written to Rahul Gandhi after receiving no response to his earlier letters dated October 29 and November 12.

Gogoi also urged the Congress leader to respond to his concerns and address what he described as a strategic error by Congress.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Tuesday condemned the missile attack on a Panama flagged tanker carrying 24 Indian seafarers in the Strait of Hormuz.In a statement, the ministry said 21 of the 24 Indian nationals had been safely evacuated, while two crew members were injured and one remained missing. The ministry added that the Indian Embassy in Oman was closely monitoring the ongoing search and rescue operations."We condemn the attack on the Panama-flagged LPG tanker MT TARA GAS in the Strait of Hormuz on 16 November 2026. Of the 24 Indian nationals on board, 21 have been safely evacuated ashore at Khasab, two injured Indian crew members have been admitted to hospital, while one Indian national remains missing," the ministry said."Our Embassy in Oman is closely monitoring the ongoing search and rescue operations in coordination with the Omani authorities. We appreciate the timely assistance and support extended by the Government of Oman in the rescue efforts," it added.MEA also reiterated that the continuing attacks on shipping in the region were "worrisome" and posed a serious threat to the safety of civilian seafarers."The targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through international waterways, in keeping with international law, must be restored at the earliest," the ministry said.Earlier, in a social media post on X, Sonowal said, "All 24 Indian nationals, along with the entire 25-member crew, are completely safe with no injuries."We are continuously monitoring the situation and remain in close contact with the ship management company to ensure the ongoing security and wellbeing of our seafarers," he said.Hours later, Sonowal, in a post on X, further said that in a distressing development, the Panama-flagged LPG tanker TARA GAS was subjected to a subsequent attack, forcing the entire crew to abandon the vessel."While 24 crew members have been safely accounted for, one Indian seafarer remains missing," he said."We are urgently coordinating with the ship management company and regional rescue authorities to locate our missing seafarer and ensure the immediate safety, welfare and logistical support of the rescued crew members," the minister added.

World.title: The endless chase for the next new 'It Thing'
World.content:
The endless chase for the next new 'It Thing'

,

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Labubu dolls dangling from exclusive designer handbags, squishmallows adorning beds, and your next purchase waiting for you to click âadd to cartâ. That is the new normal in a society where trends decide what one absolutely needs, and the excuse? #InstagramMadeMeBuyItKananpreet Kaur,19, from Delhi,had purchased an apple watch because it was all the hype. However, the whoop health tracking band is the new âit thingâ now, so the watch sits unused. âI had bought it just because everyone around me had one,â she says.Modern marketing and consumer culture often promote the belief that more possessions mean a happier, more content life. s and social media apps like Instagram, Facebook, and X constantly introduce us to products we never knew we needed. These apps help create the notorious Fear of Missing Out (FOMO), which makes the brain think we are falling behind, ultimately tricking us into frivolous purchases. A 2023 study published in the Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services, titled Fear of Missing Out and Compulsive Buying Behaviour: the Moderating Role of Mindfulnessexamined 569 participants and found that FOMO had a significant effect on compulsive buying.Dubai-resident Ahaana Arora, 19, finds herself with a new craving for tin desserts as they shot to fame on Instagram. âI never anticipated how a dessert tin would find its way to my doorstep every week,â she says.What started with simply trying out a viral sweet treat, has now become an obsession.Overconsumption today goes by a new name: self-care. This includes buying âaestheticâ outfits, the latest Stanley water cup, and stocking up on makeup and skincare products. And although it is pitched as luxurious bubble baths, curated skincare fridges, and expensive workout sets, the focus has shifted from feeling good to looking good for the camera.In today's time where the world is constantly selling you a commodity, recognising the value in each purchase becomes difficult. Something that often begins as a simple purchase leads to a series of transactions you never anticipated, because buying just a foundation is meaningless unless you get the primer for a better grip, a concealer for more coverage, setting powder to avoid creases, and you unquestionably need a setting spray for the look to come together. The growing demand for beauty products in India is also reflected in a 2023 Kantar Worldpanel study which revealed that over 100 million cosmetic products were sold in the country in a span of just six months, generating more than Rs 5000 crores in revenue.Moreover, the fashion industry is responsible for the considerable amount of waste. The total greenhouse gas emissions from the production of textiles clocks in at 1.2 billion tons a yearâthatâs more than all international flights and maritime ships combined. All the glory goes to the flawlessly engineered algorithm that cleverly blurs the lines between choice and impulse.Today, every purchase has another already waiting in cue. Buying an Iphone leads to icloud, apple music, apple arcade; a dermatologist visit translates to getting a long list of treatments and add ons; join a dating app hoping to meet someone new and wanting more visibility or simply the ability to see who's into you will cost extra; a small purchase from quick delivery apps requires a minimum cart value to avoid several additional fees.Mankeerat Kaur Chaudhary, a 19 year old veterinary student from Amritsar, downloaded the notes app thinking it is free of cost, only to later pay Rs 1200 annually for the premium features.Prisha Kapoor, 20, from Noida, finds it ridiculous how streaming platforms constantly modify their subscriptions plans. Ad free experience, which was once included in the original plan, is now an additional charge away.All these examples point towards a larger phenomenon, called the âdiderot effect.ââ The Diderot effect occurs when acquiring a new possession leads to a spiral of consumption.The selling will never end, influencers will continue to stand in front of the camera telling us about their âfind of the monthâ, and the apps will continue to refine their user interfaces to get you hooked. The very notion of âauthentic selfâ is challenged as consumerism permeates our consciousness and molds our perception of what it truly means to be an individual. Perhaps the biggest triumph of modern consumerism is not that our pockets are bleeding dry, but that it makes us believe that we are never quite enough, and how there's always a better version of ourselves waiting for us to swipe the card.

World.title: PM Modi to meet Council of Ministers on Wednesday, focus on governance and welfare delivery
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to meet his entire Council of ministers on Wednesday to review governance and reform initiatives, with a focus on improving the delivery of welfare schemes and expanding outreach to women and youth.

The meeting will take place after his return from the annual India-ASEAN Summit, official sources said, news agency PTI reported.

The discussions are expected to focus on ensuring better coordination among ministries and departments and improving the implementation of around 40-45 government welfare schemes. Modi is also likely to seek feedback from ministers and offer directions on various aspects of governance.

World.title: Quad steps up Indo-Pacific push with new maritime, AI initiatives; warns against economic coercion
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Quad on Tuesday announced a series of new initiatives to deepen cooperation on maritime security, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity and business ties.

They also raised concerns over economic coercion and unilateral attempts to change the regional status quo.

At the Quad Leadersâ Summit in Manila, leaders of India, the United States, Australia and Japan revealed plans for a Quad Business Leaders' Forum, enhanced cybersecurity cooperation and a new maritime surveillance initiative. They also reaffirmed their commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific, with an emphasis on protecting vital supply chains and ensuring safe maritime routes.



In a joint statement issued after the meeting, US president Donald Trump, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese and Japanese prime minister Takaichi Sanae said the grouping remained committed to peace, stability and prosperity in the region.

âWe strongly oppose any destabilising or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability,â the leaders said.





They also expressed âgrave concernsâ over economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions, and pledged to work together to secure critical supply chains, protect freedom of navigation and overflight, and expand the use of trusted technologies.

Quad announces maritime surveillance initiative

A key announcement was the launch of the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration, aimed at improving information-sharing and maritime domain awareness across the region.

The leaders said Quad countries' P-8 and P-3C maritime patrol aircraft were scheduled to take part in a joint maritime exercise in 2027. It would be the first such exercise involving the aircraft in a Quad context, according to the statement.

The initiative is intended to strengthen the grouping's ability to monitor maritime activity and contribute to safer sea routes across the Indo-Pacific.

The leaders also committed to ensuring open, safe and resilient maritime transit corridors, underlining the importance of freedom of navigation and overflight.

Business forum and AI cooperation

The Quad announced the inaugural Quad Business Leaders' Forum, scheduled to be held in early 2027. It will bring together business leaders, government officials and policy experts from the four countries to strengthen private-sector ties and encourage commercial deals and partnerships across the Indo-Pacific.

The leaders also reaffirmed their support for the AI Accelerator, announced by their foreign ministers in Atlanta.

The initiative is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to improve access to trusted AI, its deployment and technical assistance across the region.

The joint statement also highlighted progress under the Quad Partnership for Cable Connectivity and Resilience, which aims to expand access to secure communications infrastructure.

Australia will expand its contribution to the partnership to include electricity cables, with the stated aim of strengthening regional energy security and connectivity.

The leaders also welcomed upcoming undersea cable projects in the Indian Ocean.

Quad steps up cybersecurity and counterterrorism cooperation

The four countries announced enhanced Quad Cybersecurity Cooperation, citing a rapid increase in the number and scale of cyber incidents across the region. The initiative is intended to strengthen cooperation towards an open and secure cyberspace.

The leaders also unequivocally condemned terrorism and violent extremism in all forms, including cross-border terrorism, and committed to strengthening the grouping's existing counterterrorism cooperation.

Reaffirming their support for Asean centrality and unity, the leaders said they would continue working with regional partners to address shared challenges and deliver tangible benefits across the Indo-Pacific.

The Manila summit comes nearly a decade after the Quad was revived in 2017. The joint statement also marked the 10th anniversary of the vision of a Free and Open Indo-Pacific, first articulated by former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe in 2016.

World.title: SP leader Azam Khan gets interim bail in money laundering case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Allahabad high court on Tuesday granted interim bail to senior

leader

in a money laundering case being investigated by the

(ED). The relief came while the court was hearing his plea challenging his arrest under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).

A division bench of Justices Rajiv Gupta and Devendra Singh-I also allowed the ED seven days to file a detailed counter-affidavit on the merits of the case. Khan, 78, has been given up to 10 days to file a rejoinder. The court posted the matter for further hearing on December 10.

Court seeks responses from both sides

During Tuesday's hearing, both Khan and the ED placed affidavits before the court, including one filed by the agency in compliance with an order passed on Monday.



The bench allowed both sides time to respond to the claims made in the affidavits.

On Monday, the court had asked the ED to submit an affidavit clarifying whether it had served the grounds of arrest on Khan when it took him into custody.

Khan's counsel, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, had argued that the proceedings against his client were driven by political vendetta ahead of next year's Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.





He also contended that mandatory procedures were not followed before the arrest.

Appearing for the ED, SB Raju maintained that the agency had followed all prescribed norms and alleged that Khan had not cooperated with the investigation. He also presented a video before the bench in support of the agency's submission.

Why was Azam Khan arrested

The ED arrested Khan at Rampur district jail on October 31, shortly after he was released on bail in a dual PAN fraud case.

The 10-time MLA subsequently approached the Allahabad high court to challenge his arrest.

The Supreme Court had on November 5 directed the transfer of his writ petition challenging the arrest to the Allahabad high court.

The money laundering investigation is linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust, founded and controlled by Khan. The probe concerns alleged diversion of government funds, irregularities in land acquisition and the construction of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, where Khan is the honorary chancellor.

World.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledges ‘mistakes,’ signals interest in return if company chooses
World.content:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has signalled his interest in returning to lead the AI computer chip company in his first public statement since he abruptly left the company last week following revelations of an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he said in a social media post.

He acknowledged making “serious mistakes” in his personal life but said that he’s received an “outpouring” of support from employees, investors, business partners and customers for his return.

The statement comes after an online petition to reinstate Mr. Huang gathered more than 1,90,000 signatures, including from tech industry figures like SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk. President Donald Trump also endorsed the bid.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Mr. Huang’s statement.

Also on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), key House lawmakers said that Mr. Huang has voluntarily agreed to appear for transcribed interviews as the chipmaker faces intensifying national scrutiny over sales of its advanced computer chips.

Mr. Huang will appear before the committees on December 1, followed by the company’s general counsel, Tim Teter, on Dec. 2.

“We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security,” said a statement from the chairmen of three House committees with oversight of China and intelligence issues.

“The American people need answers on Mr. Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous PRC actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal,” the lawmakers said, referring to the People’s Republic of China.

Meanwhile, Nvidia said it’s creating a new board committee to oversee national security and global trade compliance following revelations that Mr. Huang had an extramarital affair with an alleged spy for China.

Nvidia said the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee will be responsible for oversight of national security policies and compliance with export controls.

Nvidia’s advanced chips are in high demand because they’re essential for cloud computing and data centres that underpin the artificial intelligence boom, but they face restrictions on their sale to China.

The committee will meet at least once every quarter and have three members from Nvidia’s board of directors. It will work with independent third-party experts as it oversees efforts to enhance the company’s existing national security and global trade compliance team.

“We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation,” Chairman Harvey Jones said in a statement.

President Donald Trump said it was “good” that Nvidia had created a national security and export control oversight committee shortly after arriving in the Philippines on Tuesday evening (November 17, 2026).

“Yes, that’s a good idea. It’s a great company,” Trump said during a photo opportunity in Manila with the leaders of Australia, India and Japan. “It’s a great idea.”

Mr. Huang was forced to resign as Nvidia’s CEO last week following scrutiny of his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who used to lead Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed International, which is suspected of diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China in violation of U.S. export controls.

World.title: U.K. sanctions Israeli companies building West Bank settlements
World.content:
The UK has sanctioned Israeli construction and property development companies it says are involved in building West Bank settlements, the first concrete step in Britain's previously announced effort to slow the expansion of settlements and preserve the possibility of a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

The sanctions are the first announced since Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said Sept. 8 that Britain would toughen its stance toward its longtime ally. His announcement followed Israel's decision to seek bids to build 1,200 homes in the E1 area east of Jerusalem and an increase in settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank.

The long-discussed E1 project would effectively cut off eastern Jerusalem from Palestinian population centres in the occupied West Bank, harming the prospects for a viable independent Palestinian state, Britain says.

“Illegal settlement expansion in the West Bank is destroying the prospects of a two-state solution, so today we are sanctioning companies involved in this activity and disrupting their access to the finance that enables it,” Miliband said in a video posted on X. “And our warning to companies thinking about being part of settlement expansion, including the unconscionable E1 project, is clear: We will clamp down on you.”

Britain has long been one of Israel's staunchest allies. Miliband recently described himself as a “proud British Jew” whose grandmother survived the Holocaust.

But the U.K. government has grown increasingly critical of Israel's government as the war in Gaza has drawn tens of thousands of protesters onto the streets of London and other cities. Earlier this year, Britain joined five other Western countries in imposing additional sanctions on settlers and settlements.

The latest measures target eight property development and construction firms, as well as Tzav 9, an Israeli activist movement that has blocked humanitarian aid convoys from entering Gaza, the government said.

The companies are Har Hevron Development Co., Hemdat Shomron, S.A.G. (Velvel) Construction and Development, Lev HaHar Yazamut, Harey Zahav, Ariel Residential Judea & Samaria, Ami Gvirtzman Architects 2021 and Z.F. Building Co.

All eight companies and Tzav 9 are now subject to UK asset freezes, and people associated with them will be barred from serving as directors of UK-based companies.

There was no immediate comment from Israel.

Announcing Britain's plans Sept. 8, Miliband said Israel had crossed a “long-standing red line” by advancing the E1 project. First proposed in the 1990s, it has been repeatedly delayed by international opposition. Israel's outgoing government, dominated by settler leaders, has begun seeking bids to build several thousand homes.

Miliband said Britain would target companies that facilitate settlement building, block the import of goods produced in the settlements and ban advertising for settlement land. Britain also plans to extend its international human rights regime to “enable swifter action to deter settlement expansion” and place restrictions on some arms exports to Israel, he said.

He said the full legislative package would be in place within six to nine months.

After Miliband's September speech, the Israeli government banned a number of British members of Parliament from entering the country and downgraded Britain's Jerusalem consulate, which focused on West Bank issues. The move forced 20 staff members to leave the country.

“We know that we have many friends in Britain. Unfortunately, we have a hostile Labour government that is consistently operating against the state of Israel, and it has left us no choice but to respond to its hostile actions,'' Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said at the time.

World.title: Kenyan delegation explores academic ties with Andhra University
World.content:
A delegation from the Kenyan High Commission met officials of Andhra University on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) to discuss academic cooperation, the welfare of Kenyan students, and alumni engagement.

The delegation comprised Rachel Ngetich, Education Counsellor; Christine Muia, Trade Counsellor; Ann Kasichana, First Secretary; and Chris Otomu, Immigration Counsellor.

A release by the University said 51 Kenyan students had studied between 2017 and 2026, of whom 21 had graduated. Enrolment stood at 27 in 2025-26 and 28 in 2026-27.

AU Vice-Chancellor G.P. Raja Sekhar said the university was ready to work with Kenyan universities and had over 1,200 foreign students from 58 countries. He suggested linking alumni settled in Kenya with the university. The university proposed exchanges, joint research, training, conferences and memoranda of understanding.

Ms. Ngetich said the Indian Council for Cultural Relations’ support gave Kenyan students quality higher education.

Rector P. King, Registrar K. Rambabu and Dean of International Affairs S. Paul Douglas were present.

World.title: Two flights held up at Thiruvananthapuram international airport after crane raised on flight  path
World.content:
A major scare was averted at the Thiruvananthapuram international airport on Tuesday following quick action against a crane operator who had raised the heavy machine in a private plot on the flight approach path.

The incident occurred around 4 p.m. on Tuesday. The crane on the flight approach path showed up on the airport surveillance radars and the matter was reported to the air traffic control, according to airport authorities.

Since the site had to be identified, the airport security and the Poonthura police, who were informed about the incident, reached the spot and removed the crane.

Two flights had to be held up for nearly 25 minutes as a result, the airport authorities said.

The Poonthura police said the plot was a yard for parking cranes. The equipment had been raised as part of maintenance. The people there were reportedly not aware of the security risks it could pose. No action had yet been taken against the operator, they said.

World.title: Rahul Gandhi invokes Hindu faith to defend his ‘Mama sitting on Papa’s lap’ remark
World.content:
Invoking his Hindu faith, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) defended his comments that “Mama would sit on Papa’s lap during meals” by pointing to a temple sculpture depicting Goddess Parvati sitting on Lord Shiva’s lap.

After Mr. Gandhi’s remarks about the affectionate relationship between his parents at the launch of his mother Sonia Gandhi’s autobiography, Belonging: A Journey of Love, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma. was among the BJP leaders who claimed that the Congress leader had embarrassed his mother on a special occasion.

Mr. Gandhi said fear, anger, and hatred had woven a web in the hearts of BJP and RSS supporters, preventing them from experiencing and expressing love.

“As a true Hindu, it is my duty to free them from this web, so that they too can start to experience the breathtaking beauty and joy of love and belonging in their lives. Satyam Shivam Sundaram,” Mr. Gandhi said in a post on X, along with a photograph of the Shiva-Parvati temple sculpture

‘Love need not be hidden’

The Congress backed Mr. Gandhi, saying he had opened up a much-needed conversation on love, affection, and equality in relationships.

“Love need not be hidden, affection is not a weakness, and equality begins with treating your partner as an equal,” the party said on social media. It also cited depictions of Shiva-Parvati and Lakshmi-Narasimha to argue that Hinduism recognised the goddess as the god’s companion and equal.

The debate on social media was divided, with some criticising Mr. Gandhi while others defended his candid account of his parents’ relationship.

World.title: A period of good governance, says CM; a betrayal of people says Pinarayi
World.content:
Keralam Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan and the Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan have expressed divergent views on six months of Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government.

Mr. Satheesan sought to paint a rosy picture of good governance, development, welfare, and fulfilled promises. He has claimed a 28 per cent increase in tax revenue. The UDF has also rolled out politically popular goodies, including free travel for women on State transport buses, priority ration cards for financially hard-pressed families, a senior citizens welfare programme and a hike in the honorarium of scheme workers, pre-primary teachers and child carers in anganwadis.

‘New Age Keralam’

He has also claimed that the government was focused on laying the groundwork for a “New Age Keralam”. The government also touted its legislative successes in passing laws to improve the ease of doing business, slash red tape, and provide investors with a transparent, single-window clearance mechanism.

Mr. Satheesan also dwelt at length on his flagship programme, Mission Samudra, a ₹400 crore maritime development initiative. He has sought to cast the commencement of Export-Import (EXIM) operations from the Vizhinjam International Sea Port as his government’s signature achievement.

Mr. Satheesan also promised citizens two international sea ports, 18 mini airports, aviation-linked industries, and more tech parks to transform Keralam into an economic powerhouse. He promised lakhs of new jobs for Keralam’s educated youth by 2031.

Mr Satheesan also projected Operation Toofan, the law enforcement anti-drug enforcement drive, as an administrative achievement.

‘Betrayal of people’

In stark contrast, Mr. Vijayan was scathingly critical of the UDF government, calling Mr. Satheesan’s six months of governance a betrayal of the people.

Mr. Vijayan said Mr. Satheesan had “put up Keralam for sale”, opening the door to corruption, including hasty agreements with private entities to purchase electricity at exaggerated rates, citing a “non-existent” power scarcity and dishonestly raising the spectre of economically crippling power cuts.

He accused the UDF of sacrificing the welfare of the coastal community at the altar of mercantilism. He said the UDF had opened the floodgates of environmental exploitation by allowing corporate players to exploit Keralam’s rare earths, including mineral-rich beaches, the fragile marine ecosystem, and green-flagged deep-sea mining.

World.title: Prince William says Gen Z is the torchbearer of the global movement for change
World.content:
Young people from around the world are not waiting for someone else to find the solution, they are the torchbearers of the global movement for change, Britain’s Prince William said in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

Also read | Prince William, Catherine Honour Young Changemakers at First-Ever Children’s Earthshot Awards in Mumbai

He was speaking at the 2026 Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony, which was held in India for the first time.

Winners of the Earthshot Prize award were declared under five categories in a glittering ceremony. The awardees include the Himalayan Kingdom of Bhutan and Mahindra Last Mile Mobility.

“They [Gen Z] are bringing fresh ideas and showing what is possible when optimism is matched with action. Their ideas, their energy, and their determination are helping to shape the future,” he said.

During his address, Prince William reflected on the achievements of this year’s finalists and the growing global movement behind environmental innovation.

The ceremony was attended by environmental innovators, philanthropists, business leaders, government representatives and global figures from sport, entertainment and culture.

Mahindra Last Mile Mobility won the Earthshot Prize in the ‘Clean Our Air’ category. Accepting the award, the company’s CEO, Suman Mishra, said it showed how urgent optimism worked.

The company has won 1 million pounds for its efforts, due to which 33 per cent of India’s three-wheelers are now electric.

In the ‘Revive Our Oceans’ category, Niue Ocean Wide Trust was chosen for protecting the oceans, especially the vast Pacific region.

Coral Pasisi, vice chair and co-architect of Ocean Conservation Commitments, expressed gratitude for indigenous, people-led sustainability efforts being honoured.

“It is collective responsibility in action. We want to protect the oceans that protect us all,” she said while accepting the award.

The Earthshot Prize to Protect and Restore Nature was awarded to Bhutan for their work in protecting the Himalayan forests which help the water systems that sustain 1.6 billion people downstream across South Asia.

While accepting the award, Bhutan’s Princess Chimi Yangzom Wangchuck said, “Long before environmentalism become a global priority, Bhutan made a national commitment. 60% of our land must remain under forest cover at all times. A duty enshrined in our Constitution. Deeply honoured to accept this prize.”

The Earthshot Prize in the ‘Build a Waste-free World’ category was declared for PFAS — Free France. The initiative is a national, cross-party movement to ban toxic forever chemicals in consumer products and to make polluters pay for the clean-up.

“This victory belongs to all those who stood by us and said, ‘We will not be poisoned in silence’. Thank you,” said Nicolas Thierry, Member of Parliament and lead spokesperson of the firm while accepting the award.

Orsed was declared the winner in the ‘Fix Our Climate’ category for transforming its business from coal-intensive utilities to renewable energy.

Before the ceremony, Prince William and Princess Catherine were among the celebrities who walked the green carpet. The ceremony was hosted by director Karan Johar.

Among the celebrities who took to stage were British actress and musician Simone Ashley, actor and previous Earthshot Awards presenter Rami Malek, Indian cinema stars Alia Bhatt and Sonam Kapoor, and international cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar.

Singer Shreya Ghoshal and British band Take That performed during the event.

Earlier in the day, Prince William drove an electric rickshaw with Princess Catherine sitting as a rider, as the couple met the finalists at Bandra on Tuesday morning (November 17).

They also attended the Children’s Earthshot Awards in the afternoon.

World.title: NATO allies to discuss U.S. troop levels with Pentagon strategy chief
World.content:
NATO allies will discuss Washington’s review of U.S. troop levels in ​Europe with Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), German Defence ⁠Minister Boris Pistorius said, with more clarity on the scope of any drawdown expected within weeks.

U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth unveiled the six-month review in June and threatened to withhold some ‌U.S. dues to NATO if “free riding” allies fell short of defence spending commitments.

He did not explicitly say the review could lead to cuts ‌in the 80,000 U.S. troops deployed to Europe, but stressed the goal of ‌prompting ⁠the continent to do more while enabling the U.S. military to ⁠meet global commitments.

“We expect changes in troop levels, but we don’t know anything concrete yet,” Mr. Pistorius said ahead of a meeting with his EU counterparts in Brussels that Colby will join for a working ​lunch.

“But again, a shift in ‌the balance of conventional forces would have occurred under any other U.S. President, due to increased engagement in the Indo-Pacific.”

Germany hosts about 35,000 U.S. troops, the largest American military presence in Europe. The result of the review is expected ‌to be presented before Christmas.

European military sources have speculated Washington might move ​a brigade or some 5,000 troops from Germany either to Asia or closer to NATO’s eastern flank in Poland.
